findings.title: No test combines --only with --exclude, so mixing the two argument lists would pass every test
findings.body: The goal requires that `--only` and `--exclude` stay separate and that the tests fail if this regresses. `next` builds one positional list for `build_scope`: 11 fixed args, then the `only_count` pathspecs, then the exclusions (executable_revmux-round.sh:376-383). `build_scope` separates them by shifting `only_count` values off the front (lines 89-93). No test passes both options together. Test 015 uses only `--exclude`, and tests 026-028 use only `--only`. Test 026 also filters the scope through awk, which keeps just the Scale/Limited-to/Read/Commits/Changed-files sections and drops any `Exclusions:` block. So a regression like swapping the two append loops at lines 378-383 keeps every current test green. On a real call such as `next --only app --exclude 'skip generated files'`, the scope would then say `Limited to: skip generated files`, print `git diff <base>..HEAD -- skip\ generated\ files` as the read command, and list `- app` as an exclusion. Scale, commits and changed files would still come out right, because `next` computes them before this point, so reviewers would get read commands that contradict the facts. The code is correct today; the problem is that the goal's regression-detection criterion is not met for this requirement.
findings.fix: In test 026, or in one new case, pass `--exclude '<text>'` next to the `--only` values. Then assert the full scope exactly, or at least assert the `Exclusions:` section together with the `Limited to:` line and the read commands, so pathspecs and exclusions cannot swap without a failure.

findings.title: Тесты не проверяют совместное использование --only и --exclude
findings.body: Тест ограничения scope вызывает --only без --exclude, а существующий тест исключений вызывает --exclude без --only. Поэтому регрессия, при которой передача --only удаляет текст исключений из scope.md или превращает --exclude в Git-фильтр, может пройти оба теста. Это нарушает требование цели проверять, что две опции остаются раздельными.
findings.fix: Добавить к случаю с --only один или несколько --exclude и проверить одновременно ограниченные Git-данные и точный текст исключений.

findings.title: Pathspec-suffix loop duplicated in build_scope and git fact calls duplicated across `only_count` if/else branches
findings.body: `build_scope` prints the ` -- <pathspec>...` suffix with two identical loops (lines 111-116 and 119-124). `next()` writes each of shortstat, log and name-status twice, in `if [ "$only_count" -gt 0 ]` / `else` branches (lines 347-360). The branches exist only to avoid expanding an empty array under `set -u` on Bash 3.2. Either an array that always holds `--`, or the `${only_values[@]+"${only_values[@]}"}` idiom, avoids this without branching: `git diff`/`git log` with a bare `--` behave exactly as with no pathspec. The duplication makes it possible to update one git fact and forget its twin, which is the failure the goal guards against ("every git fact takes the same pathspec list"). The combined `diff --name-only` check (lines 335-344) also repeats a query whose answer `changed_files` already holds. All copies agree today, so this is a quality issue, not a bug.
findings.fix: In next(), either build `pathspec_args=(--)` and append each `--only` value, or pass `-- ${only_values[@]+"${only_values[@]}"}`. Call each git fact once, with no if/else. In build_scope, compute the `%q` suffix string once and append it to both read commands. Optionally replace the combined name-only check with an emptiness test on `changed_files`.

findings.title: `--only` guidance contradicts step 1's rule that every later round covers the same cumulative scope
findings.body: The new text (lines 102-103) says: "When the follow-up targets only part of the cumulative change, add one repeatable `--only <pathspec>` per part to review." Step 1 of the same skill (lines 23-24) still says: "Every later round covers this same cumulative scope plus its fixes, against the same base." The change made the new option available without updating that rule, so the file now says both. Unlike profile narrowing, which has explicit conditions (lines 72-78, e.g. "A partial or failed review cannot justify narrowing"), `--only` comes with no rule for when a narrowed round is allowed. The text also does not say that a clean narrowed round says nothing about the unselected paths, which matters for step 5's finish rule. An agent following this skill gets contradictory instructions. It can narrow a confirming round and then finish under step 5 as if the whole cumulative scope converged. Or it can follow line 23 and never use the option. The skill is a contract that the agent executes. The impact is limited to how wide a follow-up round's coverage is, so this is minor.
findings.fix: Amend line 23-24 to allow a follow-up round limited with `--only`, and say when that is allowed (e.g. the fixes since the previous round are confined to those paths). Also say that the round's report must state the limited coverage, as line 82-83 already requires for narrower profiles.

findings.title: `# post-apply:` run-order key bumped from 27 to 28 as if it were a test count
findings.body: The change edits `# post-apply: 27 host-safe` to `28` while adding tests. The number is not a test count. It is the file's run-order key in `tests/run-post-apply.sh`: suites are sorted by it numerically, and a duplicate value aborts the whole runner. It has been 27 since the file was added, when the file had 24 tests. Today 28 collides with nothing and still sorts between 25 and 40, so the run order is unchanged. But the edit repeats the wrong idea that the number counts tests. The next author who copies it can land on another suite's key, and then `make test-suite` and `make test-ubuntu` fail for every change.
findings.fix: Revert the header line to `# post-apply: 27 host-safe`.

findings.title: `--only` guidance contradicts step 1's rule that every later round covers the same cumulative scope
findings.body:
The new text says: "When the follow-up targets only part of the cumulative change, add one repeatable `--only <pathspec>` per part to review." Step 1 (lines 23-24) still says: "Every later round covers this same cumulative scope plus its fixes, against the same base." Step 1 also records "paths" as part of that scope (line 21). The carry-forward rule at lines 106-107 names only the original goal and the exclusions, not the recorded paths. Profile narrowing has explicit conditions ("A partial or failed review cannot justify narrowing"); path narrowing has none. The text also does not say that a clean narrowed round says nothing about the paths it did not select, or whether an `--only` set must be repeated in later rounds.

Agents can read this two ways:
- (a) Never pass `--only`, so a path-scoped original review silently widens to the whole `base..HEAD`.
- (b) Narrow a confirming round, then finish under step 5 as if the whole cumulative scope had converged.
findings.fix: Reconcile lines 23-24 with the new text. One option: make `--only` carry the step-1 recorded paths into every later round, and add paths to the carry-forward sentence at line 106. The other: state when narrowing below the recorded scope is allowed (e.g. the fixes are confined to those paths), and require the round report to state the limited coverage, as lines 82-83 already do for narrower profiles.

findings.title: Совместное использование `--only` и `--exclude` не проверяется
findings.body: Новые тесты передают `--only` без `--exclude`, а существующий тест исключений не передаёт `--only`. Поэтому все они останутся зелёными, если при ограниченном раунде текст исключения перестанет попадать в `scope.md`: ревьюеры тогда получат область без явно заданного ограничения. Цель изменения прямо требует сохранять эти два параметра раздельными.
findings.fix: Дополнить тест ограниченного раунда вызовом с `--exclude` и проверить, что исключение присутствует в scope, а Git-факты ограничены только `--only`.

findings.title: A negative pathspec on its own is checked against everything it does not exclude, so a typo passes
findings.body: Git applies a lone negative pathspec to all changed files. With `--only app --only ':(exclude)app/generatd'` (a typo for generated), the per-pathspec check passes as long as any other file changed. The combined selection is also non-empty, so the round includes the files that were meant to be excluded. The requirement is that every pathspec that matches no change fails before the round is created.

findings.title: No test combines --only with --exclude, so a regression that mixes the two lists would pass every test
findings.body:
Issue #520 says "Keep `--only` separate from `--exclude`". code-review/SKILL.md tells follow-up rounds to carry every recorded exclusion as `--exclude`, so passing `--only` together with `--exclude` is the normal way the new option will be used. (The issue's acceptance criteria only ask for tests of the limit case and the no-match case. It does not literally require a test of this separation.)

The change routes both lists through one positional list. `next` passes 11 fixed args, then the `only_count` pathspecs, then the exclusions. `build_scope` peels `only_count` values off the front with `shift 11` and a loop (executable_revmux-round.sh build_scope and the scope_args loop in next).

No test exercises that split with both lists non-empty:
- Test 015 uses `--exclude` with only_count=0.
- Test 026 uses `--only` with no exclusions, and its awk projection drops the `Exclusions:` block.

Several regressions would keep the whole suite green:
- swapping the two append loops
- miscounting only_count
- also appending pathspecs to exclude_values
- dropping exclusions when `--only` is set

On `next --only app --exclude 'skip generated files'`, such a regression could produce `Limited to: skip generated files`, with read commands filtered by the exclusion text and `- app` listed as an exclusion. It could also drop the exclusion from scope.md. Either way, reviewers get a scope that contradicts the Git facts or loses a carried exclusion.

The code is correct today. The problem is that the new separation logic has no test that goes red when it breaks.
findings.fix: Add `--exclude '<text>'` to test 026's `run_prepare_only` call, or add one sibling case. Assert the `Exclusions:` block together with the `Limited to:` line and both read commands, ideally as the whole scope exactly, so pathspecs and exclusions cannot swap or vanish without a failure.

findings.title: Shell quoting of pathspecs in the read commands is never exercised
findings.body: `build_scope` prints each pathspec with `printf ' %q'` (executable_revmux-round.sh lines 113-116 and 121-124), so that the `git diff`/`git log` lines reviewers paste stay runnable. Test 026 uses only `app` and `docs/guide.md`, which `%q` leaves unchanged, and tests 027/028 fail before any scope is written. Edit that stays green: replace `%q` with `%s`. With that regression, `--only ':(exclude)alpha.txt'` or `--only 'missing/**/*.md'` produces a read command that fails with a bash syntax error at `(`, or gets glob-expanded or rejected by zsh's no-match rule. The reviewer then can't reproduce the limited diff the goal says the read commands must produce.
findings.fix: In test 026, make one pathspec need quoting, e.g. `--only 'docs/guide*.md'` (still selects only guide.md), and expect the escaped form (`docs/guide\*.md`) in the read-command lines.

findings.title: `--only` branching duplicates three git calls and the pathspec-printing loop
findings.body:
Each of shortstat, log and name-status is written twice in `if [ "$only_count" -gt 0 ]` / `else` blocks, and `build_scope` repeats the same ` --` plus `%q` loop for the diff and log lines. The branching exists only to avoid expanding an empty array under `set -u` in Bash 3.2. Two simplifications keep behavior the same:

- Pass `-- ${only_values[@]+"${only_values[@]}"}` to each call once. This idiom is Bash 3.2-safe and already used in `tests/lib/bashunit`, e.g. line 1742. `git diff`/`git log` with a bare `--` and no paths output exactly what they output without it.
- In `build_scope`, build the quoted suffix string once and append it to both read lines.

Also, the combined `diff --name-only` check at 335-344 repeats a query whose answer `changed_files` (line 356) already holds: name-status is empty exactly when name-only is. Testing `[ -z "$changed_files" ]` before the scope loop gives the same error, still before `revmux new`. The `cannot evaluate combined` branch would be lost, but it only fires if the combined set fails after every pathspec on its own succeeded.
findings.fix: Use the `${only_values[@]+"${only_values[@]}"}` expansion after `--` for scale/commits/changed_files and drop the if/else. Compute the `%q` suffix once in build_scope. Optionally replace the combined name-only check with an emptiness test on `changed_files`.

findings.title: Тест не проверяет совместное использование --only и --exclude
findings.body: Новый тест вызывает --only без --exclude, а существующие проверки --exclude не передают --only. Если изменить script так, чтобы при наличии --only он игнорировал текст --exclude, тесты останутся зелёными. В таком случае scope.md не передаст reviewer заданное исключение.
findings.fix: Передать --exclude вместе с --only и проверить, что выбранные Git-факты ограничены pathspec, а текст исключения присутствует в scope.md.

findings.title: --only trigger is ambiguous and contradicts the 'same cumulative scope' rule; path scope carry-forward unstated
findings.body: The new text says "When the follow-up targets only part of the cumulative change, add one repeatable `--only <pathspec>` per part to review." Step 1 (line 23-24) says "Every later round covers this same cumulative scope plus its fixes, against the same base", and step 1 records "paths" as part of that scope (line 21; revmux supports a path-scoped round 1). The carry-forward rule at lines 106-107 names only "the original goal and every exclusion", not recorded paths. Two readings follow and agents diverge: (a) a path-scoped original review is "the cumulative change", so no `--only` is added and the follow-up silently widens to the whole `base..HEAD`; (b) "only part" licenses narrowing a follow-up to e.g. just the files the fix touched, contradicting line 23 and the follow-up policy's "A partial or failed review cannot justify narrowing" — with no criterion for when path narrowing is allowed. Nor does it say whether an `--only` set used in round 2 must be repeated in round 3, the way exclusions must be.
findings.fix: Make --only the carrier of the recorded step-1 paths: e.g. "When step 1 recorded paths, pass one `--only <pathspec>` per recorded path, relative to the workdir, in every later round," and add paths to the carry-forward sentence at line 106; or, if narrowing below the recorded scope is intended, state the condition and reconcile it with line 23.

findings.title: Shell quoting of --only pathspecs in the read commands is never tested on a path that writes a scope
findings.body: `build_scope` prints each pathspec into the `git diff`/`git log` read commands with `printf ' %q'` (executable_revmux-round.sh lines 113-116 and 121-124), so the commands reviewers paste stay runnable. Test 026 is the only test that reaches a written scope. It uses `app` and `docs/guide.md`, which `%q` and `%s` print the same way. Magic and glob pathspecs appear only in tests 027/028, which fail before any scope is written. If `%q` regressed to `%s`, every test would still pass. Yet `--only ':(exclude)x'` would then print `git diff <base>..HEAD -- :(exclude)x`, which bash rejects with a syntax error at `(`. Glob pathspecs would also be expanded by the shell or rejected by zsh's no-match rule. Reviewers could not reproduce the limited diff.
findings.fix: In test 026 (or a sibling test), pass one pathspec that needs quoting and still matches, e.g. `--only 'docs/guide*.md'` or `--only ':(glob)app/*.txt'`. Assert the exact escaped read-command line.

findings.title: No test exercises --only together with --exclude, so their separation is unguarded
findings.body: `--only` values and `--exclude` values reach build_scope as one positional list, split only by the `only_count` argument and the order of the two append loops. The goal requires that `--only` and `--exclude` stay separate and that the tests fail if this regresses. No test passes both options together: test 26 passes no `--exclude`, and the existing exclusion tests have `only_count=0`. If the two loops were swapped, or `only_count` were miscounted, exclusion text would become `Limited to:` entries and pathspecs in the read commands, and pathspecs would become exclusion bullets. Every current test would still pass.
findings.fix: Add `--exclude "<text>"` to test 26's `run_prepare_only` invocation and assert the Exclusions section alongside the unchanged `Limited to:` and read-command lines.

findings.title: Повторный запрос выполняется и для ошибок, которые не являются MembraneError
findings.body: Проверка распознаёт любой объект с `data.key === 'rate_limit_exceeded'`, не проверяя признак MembraneError. Если `client.run` выбросит обычную ошибку с таким полем, `connectionGraphql` подождёт и повторит запрос до двух раз, хотя по контракту должна сразу вернуть исходную ошибку. Это также относится к GraphQL-мутациям, которые проходят через эту функцию.
findings.fix: Включить в проверку признак MembraneError и добавить случай обычной ошибки с тем же ключом.

findings.title: Rate-limit retry matches any error with data.key === 'rate_limit_exceeded', not only a MembraneError
findings.body: The goal's contract is that connectionGraphql retries only a MembraneError whose data.key is 'rate_limit_exceeded'. `RateLimitRefusal` is `Schema.Struct({ data: Schema.Struct({ key: Schema.Literal('rate_limit_exceeded') }) })` and never checks the `isMembraneError` marker, even though the test fixture `rateLimitRefusal` sets `isMembraneError: true`. Any thrown object with that data shape gets waited on and retried up to 3 times, MembraneError or not. The 'rethrows any other error' test uses a different key, so nothing checks that an unmarked error is left alone. Impact is small: at most a few seconds of delay plus two repeat calls on a mislabelled error. I could not confirm how the runtime marks a MembraneError because node_modules is not installed in this checkout.
findings.fix: Add `isMembraneError: Schema.Literal(true)` to the `RateLimitRefusal` struct, and add a test where an error with the rate-limit key but no marker is rethrown after one call.

findings.title: Проверка повтора принимает ошибки, которые не являются MembraneError
findings.body: Схема проверяет только `data.key`. Если `client.run` отклоняет запрос другой ошибкой с `{ data: { key: 'rate_limit_exceeded' } }`, код ждёт и повторяет запрос вместо немедленного возврата исходной ошибки, как требует контракт в goal.md. Это также касается GraphQL-мутаций: повтор может повторно выполнить операцию, если первая попытка уже изменила данные.
findings.fix: При распознавании отказа также проверять признак MembraneError.

findings.title: Nothing pins the thread-read bound in the sync routine; a revert to unbounded Promise.all passes every test
findings.body: The change bounds the sync routine's thread reads with `mapBounded(..., THREAD_READ_LIMIT, ...)`, but only `listCandidates` (linear-port.test.ts) gets a concurrency assertion. `packages/ux-chain/lib/sync-entry.test.ts` already drives `entries/ux-chain-sync` end to end through a mocked `membrane()` that answers each GraphQL operation, yet no test there counts concurrent thread reads. If this call site regresses to `Promise.all(issues.map(...))`, or someone passes a larger limit, the sync routine again fires one `call-connection` per updated issue at once and hits the platform's 100-parallel refusal. The suite stays green. The goal only required the fake-port test, so this is a coverage gap rather than a goal violation.
findings.fix: In sync-entry.test.ts, give the mocked `cmd.run` an in-flight counter on the thread-read operation, return more than 8 updated `ux-chain` issues that need their threads read, and assert the peak is 8.

findings.title: Тест не проверяет отказ с ключом rate_limit_exceeded вне MembraneError
findings.body: Тест другого отказа использует ключ connection_is_defunct. Поэтому он не обнаруживает, что connectionGraphql повторяет вызов при обычной ошибке с data.key === 'rate_limit_exceeded' и без признака MembraneError. По заданному контракту такая ошибка должна быть сразу передана вызывающему коду без ожидания. Если повторный вызов успешен, исходная ошибка будет скрыта.
findings.fix: Добавить случай с обычной ошибкой и ключом rate_limit_exceeded, который проверяет один вызов, отсутствие ожидания и возврат той же ошибки.

findings.title: Проверка rate limit не распознаёт тип MembraneError
findings.body: Схема проверяет только `data.key`. Если `client.run` выбросит ошибку другого типа с `data.key === 'rate_limit_exceeded'`, код повторит запрос вместо того, чтобы сразу вернуть исходную ошибку. При успешной повторной попытке ошибка будет полностью скрыта. Контракт допускает повтор только для MembraneError.
findings.fix: Добавить в проверку признак MembraneError и повторять запрос только при совпадении обоих условий.

findings.title: Тест пропускает повтор для ошибки, которая не является MembraneError
findings.body: Тест проверяет другую ошибку только с ключом connection_is_defunct. Ошибка с data.key равным rate_limit_exceeded, но без признака MembraneError, также должна передаваться без повтора по заданному контракту. Текущая проверка RateLimitRefusal принимает её и повторяет вызов. Это затрагивает и GraphQL-мутации.
findings.fix: Добавить случай с тем же ключом у ошибки без признака MembraneError и проверять тип ошибки перед повтором.

findings.title: Test does not check that the last attempt's error is the one rethrown
findings.body: All three attempts throw the same refusal object. The test would therefore still pass if the implementation rethrew the first attempt's error after the third attempt. When the refusals differ, the caller would get a stale cause instead of the latest one.
findings.fix: Throw a separate error object on each attempt and assert that the rethrown error is identical to the third one.

findings.title: No test would catch --only values leaking into the Exclusions section
findings.body: The goal says `--only` and `--exclude` must stay separate and that the tests must fail if that regressed. No test does that. No test passes both options (`--exclude` shows up only around lines 355-364, `--only` only in tests 026-028). The one success test, 026, also runs `scope.md` through an awk filter. That filter prints only the Scale and Limited-to lines and the three fenced blocks (read commands, commits, changed files), so an `Exclusions:` section is dropped before the assertion. That matters because `build_scope` takes a single argument list and splits it by `only_count`: the first N arguments after `shift 11` are `--only` values and the rest become exclusions. Suppose a regression copies the only values without shifting them off, for example `only_values=("${@:1:only_count}")`. Then each `--only` path is also listed as an exclusion. `Limited to:` and the read commands stay correct, so test 026 still passes, while reviewers are told to leave alone exactly the paths they were asked to review. The reverse mix-up, exclusions read as pathspecs, is also untested because no test combines the two flags. The current code is correct; what is missing is a test that would fail on this regression.
findings.fix: In test 026, add `--exclude 'some exclusion'` to the `run_prepare_only` call. Then assert the whole scope, or at least that the Exclusions section is exactly `- some exclusion`, rather than only the awk-filtered sections.

findings.title: The per-pathspec liveness check cannot catch an exclude-magic pathspec that excludes nothing
findings.body: The check runs `git diff --name-only base..HEAD -- "$candidate"` on each `--only` value by itself. Git treats an exclude-only pathspec as "everything except X", as test 028's own given-step shows. So a mistyped exclusion such as `--only app --only ':(exclude)app/generted'` passes both the per-pathspec check and the combined check, even though it removes nothing. The round is created with a wider scope than requested, and `Limited to:` lists the exclusion as if it took effect. Test 028 shows exclude magic is a supported input, yet the typo check cannot see it. The scope comes out too wide, never empty.
findings.fix: For a candidate starting with `:(exclude)`, `:!` or `:^`, compare the combined `--name-only` output with and without it and error when they are identical. Otherwise, document that `--only` takes only positive pathspecs.

findings.title: The pathspec list is threaded through five copy-pasted branches instead of one argument array
findings.body: Each git fact gets its own `if [ "$only_count" -gt 0 ]` branch that repeats the same command with `-- "${only_values[@]}"` added (scale at 347-351; commits and changed files at 354-360). `build_scope` then repeats the same `printf ' --'; for … printf ' %q'` loop twice (110-116 and 118-124). The goal's main invariant is that every git fact takes the same pathspec list, but here that holds only because five places stay in sync by hand. A later edit to one branch can drift without anything noticing. One array built once removes all five branches, for example `pathspec_args=(--)` plus a loop appending `only_values` (a `git diff A..B --` with no paths behaves exactly like no `--`), or the repo's existing empty-array idiom `${arr[@]+"${arr[@]}"}` (tests/bashunit/scripts_test.sh:138). Both are Bash 3.2-safe under `set -u`. Likewise, building the quoted suffix once with `printf -v` would serve both read-command lines.
findings.fix: Build `pathspec_args` once after the liveness checks, use it in the three git calls without branching, and format the quoted ` -- …` suffix once in build_scope for both read commands.

findings.title: SKILL.md adds a scope-narrowing option without saying how a limited round counts toward finishing
findings.body: SKILL.md sets out how far a follow-up may narrow its profile ("Follow-up profile selection", including "A partial or failed review cannot justify narrowing"). Step 5 rule 3 then ends the loop on "this complete round needs no further eligible fixes". The new sentence lets the agent limit a round to "only part of the cumulative change" but gives no condition for when that is allowed. It also does not say whether a clean `--only` round satisfies the finish rule for paths outside the limit, or how unresolved findings outside the limit carry forward. The agent running the loop follows this document as a contract. It could narrow to the fix paths, get zero findings, and report convergence while earlier findings in excluded paths are left out of that round's coverage report. The profile policy needs exactly this kind of rule for the profile axis, but the pathspec axis has none.
findings.fix: Add one sentence: use `--only` only when the paths outside the limit have not changed since a complete earlier round; report the limit in the round's coverage; findings outside it carry forward unresolved.

findings.title: No test passes --only and --exclude together, so the positional split in build_scope is unguarded
findings.fix: Add an `--exclude` (e.g. `'defer documentation polish'`) to test 026's `run_prepare_only` call. Then assert the exact scope, or at least that `Exclusions:` lists only that text while `Limited to:` and the read commands list only the `--only` pathspecs.

findings.title: The per-pathspec dead check never fires for an exclude-magic pathspec, so a mistyped exclusion silently widens the scope
findings.body: The per-pathspec check runs `git diff --name-only base..HEAD -- "$candidate"` on each `--only` value by itself. When git is given only exclude pathspecs, it treats them as "everything except X". So a pathspec like `:(exclude)aap/x.txt` (a typo for `app/x.txt`) still matches every other changed file on its own and passes. The combined check passes too, because `app` still matches. The round is created with `app/x.txt` still in scope, and nothing tells the caller the exclusion did nothing. Test 028 shows that exclude-magic pathspecs are a supported `--only` input, yet the check that exists to catch typos is blind to them. The cost is a wider review than intended, not an empty one, so the impact is contained.
findings.fix: For each candidate that starts with `:(exclude)`, `:!` or `:^`, compare the combined `--name-only` output with and without that candidate. Error when the two are identical, meaning the pathspec removed nothing.

findings.title: No test passes --only and --exclude together, so the positional split in build_scope is unpinned
findings.body:
`build_scope` gets both lists through one positional array. It shifts 11 fixed arguments, takes `only_count` values as pathspecs (lines 89-93), and treats whatever is left as exclusions. `next` builds that array in a fixed order, pathspecs first and then exclusions (executable_revmux-round.sh:376-383).

No test runs both options. Test 015 has exclusions and `only_count=0`; tests 026-028 have pathspecs and no exclusions. Test 026's awk filter also drops the Exclusions section, so it would not see a pathspec that ended up there.

What a regression would do (inferred, not run): swap the two append loops, or count the shift wrong, and with both options present an exclusion like 'do not review generated files' becomes a git pathspec in the read commands. Alternatively, `--exclude` gets turned into `:(exclude)` git magic. Every current test would still pass. The goal explicitly requires that '--only and --exclude stay separate' and that 'the tests would fail if any of these regressed'. That requirement is not met for this one.
findings.fix: Add one prepare-only case that passes `--only alpha.txt --exclude 'do not review generated files'`. Assert the exact scope text: `Limited to: alpha.txt`, read commands ending in `-- alpha.txt`, and the exclusion under `Exclusions:` as prose. Alternatively, extend test 026 with one `--exclude` and stop its awk filter from dropping the Exclusions section.

findings.title: Shell quoting of pathspecs in the read commands (`printf ' %q'`) is untested; test 026 uses only plain paths
findings.body:
The scope's read commands quote each pathspec with `printf ' %q'` (executable_revmux-round.sh:114, 122). That quoting is what makes the command a reviewer copies into a shell use the same pathspec list as the script's own `git -C` calls, which take the values directly as arguments. I checked that bash 3.2's `%q` output reads back unchanged in zsh, for example `:(glob)docs/**/*.md`.

Test 026 uses `app` and `docs/guide.md`, which come out identical with or without `%q`. Test 027 uses a glob but only checks the rejection. If `%q` regressed to `%s`, every test would still pass. A glob or magic pathspec such as `docs/*.md` or `:(exclude)x` would then reach the reviewer's zsh unquoted. zsh would either fail with 'no matches found' or expand the glob to files in the working tree, dropping deleted files. Either way the reviewer reads a different change than the one in the scope's Scale and Changed files. That breaks the goal's rule that every git fact uses the same pathspec list.
findings.fix: Add one pathspec that needs quoting to test 026's `--only` list, such as `'docs/*.md'` or `':(exclude)docs/notes.md'`. Assert the exact quoted form in the expected `git diff` and `git log` lines.

findings.title: post-apply header bumped 27→28 as if it were a test count; it is the suite's unique run-order key
findings.body: The change edits `# post-apply: 27 host-safe` to `28` alongside adding tests 026–028, treating the number as a test count. `tests/run-post-apply.sh` uses it as the file's execution order (`sort -n -k1,1`). If two files share a value, the whole post-apply run fails with `duplicate post-apply order`. 28 is unused today, so nothing breaks now. But the header was set to 27 when the file was created and is not tied to its test count. If later rounds keep bumping it per test, it will eventually hit a key another file already uses (e.g. 40 for platform_test.sh) and abort the suite.
findings.fix: Revert line 2 to `# post-apply: 27 host-safe`.

findings.title: No test checks the %q quoting of --only pathspecs in the scope's read commands
findings.body: The read commands quote each pathspec with `printf ' %q'` (executable_revmux-round.sh:114, 122). Test 026 uses only `app` and `docs/guide.md`, which print the same with `%q` or `%s`. Tests 027 and 028 use glob and magic pathspecs, but only on rejection paths, which never render read commands. If `%q` regressed to `%s`, every test would still pass. A pathspec like `docs/*.md` or `:(exclude)x` would then reach the reviewer's shell unquoted. zsh would either fail with 'no matches found' or expand the glob against the working tree. The read commands would then select a different set than the reported Scale, Commits and Changed files. That breaks the rule that every git fact takes the same pathspec list.
findings.fix: Use a pathspec that needs quoting on test 026's success path (e.g. `'app/*.txt'` or `':(exclude)docs/notes.md'`) and assert the exact quoted read-command lines.

findings.title: Pathspec plumbing written five times: three if/else git branches plus two identical quoting loops
findings.body:
The pathspec list is copied by hand in five places:
- `next()` repeats `if only_count > 0 … -- "${only_values[@]}" else … fi` for scale (347–351), and again for commits and changed_files (354–360).
- `build_scope` repeats the same ` --` plus `%q` loop for the git diff line (110–117) and the git log line (118–125).

The goal's central invariant, that every git fact uses the same pathspec list, holds only because these copies stay in sync. A sixth git fact added later has to remember to copy the branch. Building `pathspec_args=(--)` and appending only_values gives a never-empty array that is safe under `set -u` on Bash 3.2. `git diff A..B --` with no paths behaves the same as without `--`. The quoted suffix could also be built once.
findings.fix: Replace the three if/else blocks with one `pathspec_args=(--)` plus only_values array used unconditionally, and compute the quoted ` -- …` suffix once in build_scope (keeping the `only_count > 0` guard for the unrestricted scope text).

findings.title: Combined --only check runs an extra git diff that changed_files already answers
findings.body: After every pathspec has been checked on its own (323–333), the combined block runs `git diff --name-only base..HEAD -- all pathspecs` only to test for emptiness. Line 356 then runs `git diff --name-status` over the same range and pathspecs. Its output is empty exactly when `--name-only` is empty, and nothing between the two has side effects (only rev-parse, shortstat and log). Moving the check to `[ -n "$changed_files" ] || { error "combined --only pathspecs match no changes in $base..HEAD"; return 1; }` right after line 356 gives the same message, the same exit status 1, and still runs before the scope loop and `revmux new`. Test 028 keeps covering it. The 'cannot evaluate combined' branch can only fire if the combined call fails after every single-pathspec call succeeded. In that case `set -e` on the later assignment already aborts before any round is created. This removes one git call, one error branch and one use of only_match. Keep the per-pathspec loop as it is: its error wrapper turns a git failure into exit 1, where `set -e` would give 128.
findings.fix: Delete lines 335–344 and add an emptiness check on changed_files inside the only_count > 0 branch after it is computed.

findings.title: Red/green calibration of tests 026–028 against their target regressions is not shown
findings.body: docs/solutions/design-patterns/semantic-regression-tests-over-source-shape.md requires red/green calibration, and no results were provided for the new tests 026–028. The regressions to check are concrete: drop the filter from one git command, check only the first --only, or remove the combined-emptiness check. Reading the code, the tests should catch these, but no confirming runs exist. The finding does not claim the tests already give false green. What would settle it: evidence that each test fails on its mutation for the expected reason and passes on the fixed version.

findings.title: New `--only` trigger conflicts with step 1's full-scope rule for later rounds and does not say which paths to pass
findings.body:
The new text says: "When the follow-up targets only part of the cumulative change, add one repeatable `--only <pathspec>` per part to review." Step 1 (line 23) still says: "Every later round covers this same cumulative scope plus its fixes, against the same base." Nothing reconciles the two, so an agent following step 1 never narrows a round and one following step 2 does.

The trigger is also vague. It never says who decides that a follow-up is partial or which pathspecs are correct. Fix commits often touch both the code and its test, or a matching occurrence elsewhere (step 4). An agent that passes `--only` for just the file named in the finding gets a confirming round that leaves the rest of the fix commits unreviewed. The script rejects a pathspec only when it matches nothing. It does not reject one that leaves out files the fixes changed. As a result, the step-5 rule "every fix gets a confirming round" can be met by a round that never saw part of the fix.
findings.fix: Add the exception at line 23 ("…unless the round is limited with `--only` as described in step 2"). Make the trigger checkable: name who decides, and require the pathspecs to cover every path changed since the previous round's tip (`git diff --name-only <previous tip>..HEAD`) as well as the part being targeted.

findings.title: Nothing requires reporting a path-limited round's reduced coverage or stops the loop from finishing on it
findings.body: For a narrower profile, the skill says to carry unresolved findings forward and to report the resulting coverage explicitly (lines 80-83). `--only` narrows coverage by path instead, and it gets no matching rule. Step 5 rule 3 finishes when "this complete round needs no further eligible fixes", and the closing report lists only the actual profile and source coverage. So a clean `--only` round satisfies the finish rule with nothing saying it covered only the listed paths. An agent can narrow the round to the fix paths, get zero findings, and report convergence on the whole cumulative change. Paths outside the limit, and any unresolved findings in them, go unreviewed and unreported. The `Limited to:` line in scope.md reaches only the reviewers, not the caller's report.
findings.fix: After the `--only` instruction, add: a round limited by `--only` covers only those paths; carry unresolved findings outside them forward; state the pathspecs in the final report's coverage. Extend the step-5 wording so that a round limited by `--only` does not by itself count as the complete round that finishes the loop.

findings.title: No test combines --only with --exclude, so the required --only/--exclude separation can regress undetected
findings.body:
The goal requires that `--only` and `--exclude` stay separate, with `--exclude` remaining prose for reviewers, and that the tests fail if this regresses. `next` gives `build_scope` one flat positional list: the fixed args, then the `only_count` pathspecs, then the exclusion values (executable_revmux-round.sh:376-383). `build_scope` takes the first `only_count` values as pathspecs and treats the rest as exclusions (:89-93, :128-133).

No test passes both options. Test 026 passes only `--only`, tests 027/028 are rejections without `--exclude`, and test 015 (around :363) passes only `--exclude`. Test 026's awk filter also prints only the Scale, Limited-to, read-command, Commits and Changed-files sections, so it never inspects `Exclusions:`.

These regressions would all pass the suite:
(a) Swapping the two append loops in `next`. With `--only app --exclude 'skip docs'`, scope.md would then say `Limited to: skip docs` and `git diff <base>..HEAD -- skip\ docs`, and list `- app` under Exclusions.
(b) `build_scope`, or the parser, copying pathspecs into the exclusion list without shifting them off. They would appear as exclusion bullets.
(c) Exclusions being dropped, or fed to git as pathspecs, only when `--only` is present.

This is the main way the option will be used. The canonical SKILL.md follow-up command always passes `--exclude`, and `--only` is now added on top of it. A regression would send reviewers to the wrong paths, or lose the exclusions agreed in earlier rounds.
findings.fix: In test 026 (or one new case), pass `--exclude '<text>'` alongside the `--only` values. Then assert the full scope.md exactly, or extend the awk filter to keep the `Exclusions:` section. Check that the pathspecs appear only in `Limited to:` and both read commands, that the exclusion text appears only as a `- …` bullet, and that the git facts are unchanged.

findings.title: Совместное использование --only и --exclude не проверяется
findings.body: Тест с --only запускается без --exclude, а существующий тест с --exclude — без --only. Поэтому регрессия, при которой --exclude начинает фильтровать Git-факты только при наличии --only, оставит оба теста зелёными. В таком случае выбранные изменения исчезнут из scope.md, хотя --exclude должен оставаться только текстом для ревьюеров. Цель изменения прямо требует, чтобы тесты выявляли нарушение этого разделения.
findings.fix: Добавить к тесту с --only значение --exclude и проверить, что Git-факты остаются прежними, а исключение присутствует только в текстовом разделе.

findings.title: No test passes --only and --exclude together, so the --only/--exclude boundary in build_scope's arguments can regress unnoticed
findings.body:
The goal requires that `--only` and `--exclude` stay separate and that the tests fail if this regresses. `next` hands `build_scope` one flat list: the only count, then the pathspecs, then the exclusions (executable_revmux-round.sh:376-384). `build_scope` treats the first `only_count` arguments as pathspecs and the rest as exclusions (:89-93, :128-133).

No test exercises both groups at once. Test 026 passes only `--only`, and its awk filter (:747-759) keeps just the Scale/Limited/read/Commits/Changed sections, so it discards any `Exclusions:` section. The existing exclusion test (:363-364) passes only `--exclude`.

Concrete regression the suite would pass: swap the two append loops at executable_revmux-round.sh:378-383 so exclusions come before pathspecs. With `--only app --exclude 'skip docs'`, scope.md would say `Limited to: skip docs` and `git diff <base>..HEAD -- skip\ docs`, and list `- app` under Exclusions. Reviewers would be told to skip the very paths the round covers. Every current test still passes, because none supplies both flags. A regression that also copies `--only` values into `exclude_values` would likewise go unseen: 026 filters out the Exclusions section and no other test passes `--only`.
findings.fix: In test 026 (or a sibling), pass an `--exclude '<text>'` alongside the two `--only` flags. Assert the exact `Exclusions:` section, plus the `Limited to:` line and both read commands, so a crossed or leaked argument fails exactly.

findings.title: Each git fact is written twice (with and without pathspecs), and the pathspec printf loop is duplicated in build_scope
findings.body:
The scale, commits and changed_files queries (:347-360) each sit in an `if [ "$only_count" -gt 0 ]`/`else` pair. The branches differ only by `-- "${only_values[@]}"`, and the combined pre-check at :335-344 repeats the same call shape. In `build_scope`, the ` --` plus `%q` loop is pasted verbatim for the `git diff` and `git log` read commands (:110-125).

The goal requires every git fact to use the same pathspec list. This layout lets a later edit update one branch and miss another. Branching isn't needed for Bash 3.2 `set -u` safety either: a trailing `--` with no pathspecs is equivalent to none. So a never-empty array such as `range_args=("$base..HEAD" --)` plus the `only_values` can feed every call. The combined `--name-only` pre-check is empty exactly when `changed_files` is empty, so it could become an emptiness check on `changed_files` with one fewer git call.
findings.fix: Build `range_args=("$base..HEAD" --)` (or `pathspec_args=(--)`) once, append `only_values`, and use it in every git call without branching. Replace the combined pre-check with an empty check on `changed_files` that keeps the same error message. In build_scope, build the quoted pathspec suffix once and print it after both read commands.

findings.title: Post-apply declaration bumped 27→28 as if it were a test count; it is the suite's run order
findings.body:
`tests/run-post-apply.sh:43-100` reads the number in `# post-apply: <order> <eligibility>` as a unique sort key: it sorts suites by it and rejects duplicates. It is not a test count. The diff changes it from 27 to 28 even though the suite now has 27 test functions (001-028, with 004 missing). That only makes sense if the number was misread as a count.

Runtime ordering does not change, since 28 still falls between morning_cleanup (25) and platform (40). But the edit spreads the misreading: the next author who adds tests may keep bumping the number until it collides with or passes a neighbouring suite's order. That would reorder suites or trip the runner's `duplicate post-apply order` error.
findings.fix: Revert line 2 to `# post-apply: 27 host-safe`.

findings.title: New --only guidance contradicts step 1's rule that every later round covers the full cumulative scope, and gives no coverage policy for limited rounds
findings.body:
The new text says: "When the follow-up targets only part of the cumulative change, add one repeatable `--only <pathspec>` per part to review." Lines 23-24 were not changed and still say: "Every later round covers this same cumulative scope plus its fixes, against the same base". The revmux loop reference (`loop.md`: "Every round reviews the cumulative diff") says the same, so the agent gets conflicting instructions.

Nothing gives a criterion for when a follow-up "targets only part". Nothing says how a limited round counts in step 5: rule 1 blocks on incomplete coverage, and rule 3 finishes when "this complete round needs no further eligible fixes". The skill also doesn't say whether the limit carries into the next round, the way `--exclude` does at line 107, or whether the final report (line ~220, "actual profile and source coverage") must name the limited paths. Profile narrowing does have explicit rules (lines 72-83: a partial review cannot justify narrowing; report the resulting coverage explicitly). Path narrowing has nothing comparable.

Failure case: an agent narrows a confirming round to the paths it fixed, gets a clean round, and reports convergence for the whole change. Fixes or paths outside the pathspecs never get a confirming review.
findings.fix: Amend line 23 to allow the `--only` exception. Next to the follow-up profile policy, state when a follow-up may be limited, for example only when every open finding and fix since the previous round falls under the named paths. Say whether a limited round satisfies step 5 rule 3 and whether `--only` carries forward. Require the final report to name the limited paths as its coverage.

findings.title: Инструкция для частичного раунда противоречит правилу о полном охвате
findings.body: Для последующего раунда эта инструкция разрешает ограничить проверку частью накопленного изменения. Но строки 23–24 требуют, чтобы каждый последующий раунд охватывал тот же полный исходный scope вместе с исправлениями. Агент получает противоречивые команды и может отказаться от --only либо считать частичный раунд проверкой всего исходного scope.
findings.fix: Согласовать правило об охвате последующих раундов с допустимым частичным scope и указать, как сообщать об ограниченном покрытии.

findings.title: Совместное использование --only и --exclude не проверяется
findings.body: Новые тесты передают только --only, а существующий тест исключений передаёт только --exclude. Поэтому регрессия, при которой --exclude теряется именно при использовании --only, оставит все эти тесты зелёными. В таком раунде ревьюеры не получат ранее согласованные исключения и могут проверить исключённые области.
findings.fix: Дополнить успешный тест вызовом с обоими параметрами и проверить ограниченные Git-факты и отдельный раздел Exclusions в созданном scope.

findings.title: No test passes --only together with --exclude, so a mix-up in how build_scope splits the two would pass every test
findings.body:
The goal requires that `--only` and `--exclude` stay separate, and that the tests fail if this regresses. `build_scope` receives both lists through one positional array: `scope_args` gets the pathspecs first, then the exclusions (executable_revmux-round.sh:376-383). It uses `only_count` to decide where the pathspecs end and the exclusions begin (lines 89-93).

I checked every `--only` and `--exclude` use in the suite. Tests 026-028 pass only `--only`. Test 015 (lines 363-364) passes only `--exclude`. No test passes both.

The gap: if the two append loops were swapped, or `only_count` were off by one, `build_scope` would put exclusion prose under `Limited to:` and into the `git diff ... --` / `git log ... --` read commands, and list the pathspecs under `Exclusions:`. The git facts are computed separately in `next()` from `only_values`, so they would stay correct. The read commands would then no longer match the commits and files listed. Every current test would still pass, because each one uses only one of the two options.

The current code orders them correctly; this finding is about the missing regression guard the goal asks for.
findings.fix: Add `--exclude '<text>'` to the `run_prepare_only` call in test 026. Extend its awk projection to keep the `Exclusions:` bullet, and assert the exact output: `Limited to:` and both read commands carry only the pathspecs, and `Exclusions:` carries only the prose.

findings.title: SKILL.md still says every later round covers the full cumulative scope, which now contradicts the new --only instruction
findings.body:
Lines 23-24 were not changed: "Every later round covers this same cumulative scope plus its fixes, against the same base." The new text at lines 102-103 tells the agent to add `--only <pathspec>` when "the follow-up targets only part of the cumulative change." That narrows a later round to a subset of the cumulative scope. The agent that runs this skill now gets two instructions that conflict.

The skill also gives no rule for how a limited round counts in step 5. Rule 1 stops as blocked when "coverage is incomplete". Rule 3 finishes when "this complete round needs no further eligible fixes." Narrowing by profile has an explicit policy (lines 74-79: retain the broader coverage when unsure; a partial review cannot justify narrowing). Narrowing by path has nothing comparable.

What I observed is the contradiction itself. The consequence is inferred: an agent could treat a clean `--only` round as a complete round and finish the loop, even though the paths outside the limit were not re-reviewed after the latest fixes. Or it could treat the round as incomplete coverage and block. The skill does not settle which.
findings.fix: Change line 23 to allow the exception, for example: "Every later round covers this same cumulative scope plus its fixes, against the same base, unless it is limited with `--only`." In step 5, say whether a round limited by `--only` counts as complete coverage for finishing the loop.

findings.title: Тесты не проверяют совместное использование --only и --exclude
findings.body: Новые тесты вызывают --only без --exclude, а существующий тест --exclude не передаёт --only. Поэтому suite останется зелёным, если при совместном использовании скрипт начнёт передавать текст --exclude в Git как pathspec или опустит его из раздела Exclusions. Это нарушит заданный контракт: --only ограничивает Git-факты, а --exclude остаётся текстом для ревьюеров.
findings.fix: Добавить к успешному случаю с --only аргумент --exclude и проверить выбранные Git-факты и текст раздела Exclusions.

findings.title: No test combines --only with --exclude, so the goal's 'stay separate' criterion is not covered
findings.body:
The goal says `--only` and `--exclude` must stay separate and that the tests must fail if this regresses. No test passes both options. The only `--exclude` tests (around line 363) run without `--only`, and none of tests 026–028 pass `--exclude`. Test 026 also could not catch this as written: its awk filter prints only the Scale, Limited-to, Read-the-change, Commits and Changed-files sections, so it never reads the Exclusions section.

The positional split in `build_scope` is fragile: next() appends the only_count pathspecs and then the exclusions to `scope_args` (executable_revmux-round.sh:376-383), and build_scope shifts off only_count values before treating the rest as exclusions. A change that swaps the two append loops in next() still passes every test, because there is no test with both options. With that change, `--only app --exclude 'do not review generated files'` would produce `Limited to: do not review generated files` and the read command `git diff <base>..HEAD -- do\ not\ review\ generated\ files`, while `app` would be listed as an exclusion. The Commits and Changed-files lists would still be right, because they are computed in next(). This combination is the main way the option gets used: the canonical command in SKILL.md always passes `--exclude`, and the new text tells the agent to add `--only` to that command. The current code is correct; this is a coverage gap.
findings.fix: In test 026 (or one new test), pass `--exclude 'defer docs'` alongside the two `--only` values. Assert the exact Limited-to line, the read commands and an Exclusions section that contains only `- defer docs`, for example by adding `/^Exclusions:/` and its `- ` lines to the awk filter.

findings.title: Each git fact is written twice (with and without pathspecs), and the combined pre-check repeats the changed_files query
findings.body:
The change runs three git queries (scale, commits, changed_files) in `if [ "$only_count" -gt 0 ]` / `else` branches that differ only by `-- "${only_values[@]}"`. The goal requires every git fact in the scope to use the same pathspec list, and this layout lets a later edit update one branch and miss the other.

A bare `--` with nothing after it is equivalent to no pathspec. I checked this in this repo: `git diff --shortstat`, `git diff --name-status` and `git log --oneline` give byte-identical output with and without a trailing `--`. So one Bash 3.2-safe array covers both cases: `pathspec_args=(--)`, append the values, then always call `git ... "$base..HEAD" "${pathspec_args[@]}"`. The array is never empty, so `set -u` stays satisfied on macOS /bin/bash.

Separately, the combined `--name-only` check at lines 335-344 is empty exactly when `changed_files` (`--name-status`, same range, same pathspecs) is empty. Checking `[ -n "$changed_files" ]` right after it is computed would give the same refusal, still before `revmux new`, with one fewer git call. Inside build_scope, the identical ` --` plus `%q` loop is also written twice (lines 110-125). Building the suffix once removes the second copy, and the existing exact-output tests still pin the no-`--only` form.
findings.fix: Build `pathspec_args=(--)` plus `only_values` once in next() and use it in all three git calls with no if/else. Replace the combined pre-check with an empty check on `changed_files` that uses the same error message. In build_scope, build the ` -- %q...` suffix once and print it after both read commands.

findings.title: Тест не проверяет совместное использование --only и --exclude
findings.body: Новый тест передаёт только --only, а существующий тест исключений передаёт только --exclude. Если при наличии --only перестать добавлять исключения в scope.md, оба теста останутся зелёными. Тогда ревьюеры получат ограничение по путям, но потеряют решения о том, что исключить из проверки. Цель изменения явно требует сохранить независимость этих опций и проверять это тестами.
findings.fix: Добавить --exclude в успешный тест с повторяющимся --only и проверить секцию исключений вместе с выбранными Git-данными.

findings.title: --only success test uses no pathspec that needs shell escaping, so replacing %q with %s would go unnoticed
findings.body: Neither pathspec in the successful `--only` test contains characters the shell treats specially. If the scope.md read commands were built with `%s` instead of `%q`, the test would stay green. A path with a space, or a glob with `*`, would then be split or expanded by the shell, and a reviewer running the command from scope.md would pass git a different set of paths.
findings.fix: In test 026 (ideally the same case that adds --exclude), use one pathspec that needs quoting, such as a glob `'app/*.txt'` or a name with a space. Then assert exactly the escaped form in the two read-command lines (e.g. `-- app/\*.txt docs/guide.md`). An exact assert_output then fails if %q is replaced with %s. Running the command is not needed.

findings.title: `--only` trigger has no decision criterion and contradicts step 1's "every later round covers this same cumulative scope"
findings.body:
The new text says "When the follow-up targets only part of the cumulative change, add one repeatable `--only <pathspec>` per part to review." Nothing in the skill says when a follow-up "targets only part". Step 1 (lines 23-24) still says "Every later round covers this same cumulative scope plus its fixes, against the same base". The revmux loop reference agrees with step 1 (`~/.agents/skills/revmux/references/loop.md:16,55`: "Every round reviews the cumulative diff").

An agent following step 1 never uses `--only`. An agent reading line 102 may narrow a follow-up to the paths its fixes touched. So runs diverge on how much each confirming round covers.

The skill already treats narrowing as a coverage decision with rules: the follow-up profile policy (lines 72-83) has "A partial or failed review cannot justify narrowing", "Carry unresolved findings ... forward" and "Report the resulting coverage explicitly". None of these is applied to `--only`. Two things are left unsaid:
- whether the limit carries into the next round, the way `--exclude` explicitly does at line 107;
- whether the final report (line 220, "actual profile and source coverage") must name the limited paths.

An agent could narrow a confirming round to the fixed files and then report convergence over the whole change. That is the exact case the profile policy forbids.
findings.fix: Give `--only` a criterion next to the follow-up profile policy, for example "Limit a follow-up with `--only` only when the remaining open findings and the fixes all sit under the named paths; omit it otherwise." Amend step 1's "every later round covers this same cumulative scope" to carve out that case. State whether `--only` carries forward, and require the final report to name the limited paths as part of its coverage.

findings.title: No test proves `--only` values stay out of the Exclusions section
findings.body:
The goal says `--only` and `--exclude` must stay separate, and that the tests must fail if this regresses. Test 026 projects `scope.md` through an awk filter. The filter prints only the `Scale:` and `Limited to:` lines and the Read/Commits/Changed-files fences, so it never sees an `Exclusions:` section.

No test runs `--only` together with `--exclude`. Test 015 covers `--exclude` alone.

Suppose the argument parser also appended `--only` values to `exclude_values`, or the `scope_args` assembly at `executable_revmux-round.sh:378-383` emitted pathspecs into the exclusion tail. The pathspecs would then show up as `- app` / `- docs/guide.md` under Exclusions, and every test would stay green. The opposite direction is covered: `--exclude` text treated as a pathspec would trip the dead-pathspec check and fail test 015.
findings.fix: In test 026 (or one new case), pass both `--only app` and `--exclude 'defer docs'`. Assert the full `scope.md`, or at least an exact `Exclusions:` block containing only the `--exclude` text.

findings.title: Sticky summary bar is fixed inside a container-type element, so it pins to the editor rather than the viewport
findings.body: `.minis-summary-bar` uses `position: fixed; inset-block-start: 0` (global.css ~line 285) but it is rendered as a child of `.minis-editor` (PaperMinisGenerator.tsx ~line 914), and this change gives `.minis-editor` `container-type: inline-size`. Per MDN's containing-block rules (quoted in csswg-drafts#10102), an ancestor with any `container-type` other than `normal` is the containing block for `position: fixed` descendants. The bar is therefore positioned against the top of `.minis-editor`, the same place as the header card, and not against the viewport. Scenario: add 8 minis and scroll down until the header card leaves the viewport. IntersectionObserver sets `data-visible=true`, but the bar sits at the top of the editor, which is scrolled away, so the user never sees the summary, the 'Изменить' button or the sticky 'Скачать PDF'. `inset-inline: 0` also sizes the bar to the editor's width instead of the full viewport. This defeats the goal's main sticky-bar requirement.
findings.fix: Render the summary bar outside the element with `container-type` (for example as a sibling of `.minis-editor`, or through a portal to `document.body`), or put `container-type` on an inner wrapper that holds only the header card and workspace. The `@container (width < 40rem)` rules for the bar would then need a media query or their own container.

findings.title: Sticky-bar browser test cannot fail on the bar's real hidden or pinned state
findings.body: The test locates the bar's button with `page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Изменить' })`. The bar has `aria-hidden={!headerOutOfView}` (PaperMinisGenerator.tsx:917), and Playwright role locators exclude aria-hidden subtrees. So `toBeHidden()` on load and after clicking 'Изменить' passes because the locator matches nothing, whatever global.css:293-311 does (`visibility: hidden`, `translateY(-100%)`). After scrolling, `toBeVisible()` only needs a non-empty box and no `visibility: hidden`. It does not check that the bar sits at the top of the viewport. A regression where the base rule stops hiding the bar on load, or the bar is not pinned to the viewport (it renders inside `.minis-editor`, which has `container-type: inline-size`), would still pass. happy-dom never fires IntersectionObserver, so this e2e test is the only place that could catch it. This is a test gap on one page, not a product defect.
findings.fix: Locate the bar through a hook that is not a role (`page.locator('.minis-summary-bar')` or a data-testid). Assert `data-visible='false'` plus `not.toBeInViewport()` on load and after 'Изменить'. After scrolling and before clicking inside the bar, assert `toBeInViewport()` with the bounding box y near 0.

findings.title: Summary text is truncated on narrow screens, hiding some current settings
findings.body: At about 320 px wide, a long summary (format, margins, style, cut marks, numbering, measured scale) does not fit on one line. The `truncate` class replaces the end with an ellipsis, so while the card is off screen the user cannot read the rest of the current settings in the bar.
findings.fix: Allow the summary text to wrap, or give the user a way to see it in full.

findings.title: Sticky bar's PDF button shows no busy, preparing or error feedback; it is only in the off-screen card
findings.body: The bar's 'Скачать PDF' calls the same `download()` and checks the same `canGenerate` as the card's button. All feedback is rendered only in the settings card: the 'Подготовка PDF…' label, the 'Создаём PDF…' / 'Обрабатываем изображения…' status, `draftError`, and the PDF or object-URL generation error stored in `message`. The bar is used when that card has scrolled out of view, so this feedback is off screen. During generation the bar's button just goes grey with a fixed `aria-label="Скачать PDF"`. If the download fails, or the button is disabled while images are being prepared or because of an invalid margin draft, the user sees nothing download and gets no reason. This goes against docs/DESIGN.md's requirement to design loading and error states.
findings.fix: Mirror the card's state in the bar: use the label `busy ? 'Подготовка PDF…' : 'Скачать PDF'`, and show a short status or error line (busy, preparing, draftError, download error) in `.minis-summary-content`.

findings.title: Sticky bar's PDF button gives no busy, preparing or draft-error feedback, unlike the card's
findings.fix: Mirror the card's button in the bar: use `aria-label`/text `busy ? 'Подготовка PDF…' : 'Скачать PDF'`, and/or render a short status line (busy/preparing/draftError) in `.minis-summary-content`.

findings.title: 'Изменить' focuses before scrolling, so the smooth scroll and reduced-motion branch have almost no effect
findings.body: The handler calls `firstField?.focus()` without `preventScroll`, then `header.scrollIntoView({ behavior: shouldAnimate ? 'smooth' : 'auto', block: 'start' })`. `focus()` already jumps the page to the field instantly, so the later smooth scroll only animates a small adjustment to `block: 'start'` and the scroll margin. The page scrolls twice. Users who allow motion still get an instant jump, and the `prefers-reduced-motion` lookup barely changes anything.
findings.fix: Call `firstField?.focus({ preventScroll: true })` so the single `scrollIntoView` handles both the scroll and the motion preference.

findings.title: Accordion primitive has no consumer after the sidebar was removed
findings.body: This change removed the only import of `@/components/ui/accordion`, which was in `PaperMinisGenerator.tsx`. Nothing else in the repo references the file: no page, component, test or doc. It is now dead code in `src/components/ui/`, and future contributors would take it for a supported, in-use primitive.
findings.fix: Delete `src/components/ui/accordion.tsx`, or state in the PR that it is kept on purpose as a library primitive.

findings.title: Scale popover className draws a double edge and repeats or dead-codes the primitive's styling
findings.body: The scale popover's className adds `border border-border`. The `Popover` primitive (`src/components/ui/popover.tsx:37`) always applies `ring-1 ring-foreground/10`, and tailwind-merge keeps both, so the popover gets a 1px border plus a 1px ring just outside it. Neighbouring primitives use one edge each: `select.tsx` uses only a border and `dropdown-menu.tsx` only a ring. The className also includes `minis-scale-popover`, which is defined nowhere. `rounded-lg` and `shadow-md` repeat the primitive's defaults, and `bg-surface-elevated` resolves to the same colour as `bg-popover`. Only the width override changes anything.
findings.fix: Reduce the className to `w-[min(24rem,calc(100vw-2rem))] p-4`. If a border is wanted, switch the primitive to `ring-border` so there is only one edge.

findings.title: 'popover closes on Escape and an outside click' test duplicates the test.each above it
findings.body: The parametrised test 'closing the printer scale with $close…' (l.102-178) already closes the popover both by Escape and by an outside pointerdown, then clicks the trigger and calls getByRole on the measurement input. If either way of closing broke, that click would toggle the popover shut and getByRole would throw. The focus-return test (l.180-206) also asserts `open: false` after Escape. The standalone test at l.208-239 therefore fails only when those do, with weaker assertions. CLAUDE.md asks component tests not to overlap.
findings.fix: Delete the standalone test, or fold its open/closed assertions into the test.each and make that test the owner of dismissal.

findings.title: Ошибка скачивания из закреплённой панели остаётся за пределами экрана
findings.body: Когда карточка настроек ушла вверх и пользователь скачивает PDF из закреплённой панели, ошибка генерации или создания object URL записывается в message. Это сообщение отображается только внутри карточки на строках 853–856, поэтому пользователь не видит причину отсутствия скачивания. Во время генерации статус также остаётся в карточке. Это противоречит требованию docs/DESIGN.md проектировать состояния загрузки и ошибки.
findings.fix: Показывать состояние загрузки и результат скачивания рядом с закреплённой кнопкой, когда карточка не видна.

findings.title: Браузерный тест не проверяет закрытие окна масштаба
findings.body: Браузерный сценарий открывает окно масштаба и переводит фокус из поля, но не проверяет закрытие по Escape или внешнему нажатию, возврат фокуса и восстановление невалидного значения. Регрессия в обработке этих событий именно в браузере может пройти браузерные тесты, хотя цель изменения требует, чтобы они обнаруживали такие сбои. Компонентные тесты выполняются в happy-dom и не проверяют поведение браузера.
findings.fix: Добавить браузерные проверки обоих способов закрытия, фокуса и доступности PDF-действий после невалидного ввода.

findings.title: Sticky-bar 'hidden' assertions are satisfied by aria-hidden alone, so a CSS regression that leaves the bar visible over the card goes undetected
findings.body: `edit` is `page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Изменить' })`. The bar carries `aria-hidden={!headerOutOfView}` (PaperMinisGenerator.tsx:916), and Playwright's getByRole excludes aria-hidden subtrees by default (includeHidden: false). So `await expect(edit).toBeHidden()` before scrolling and after clicking 'Изменить' passes merely because the locator resolves to nothing — independent of the CSS that actually hides the bar (`.minis-summary-bar { visibility: hidden; transform: translateY(-100%) }` / `[data-visible='true']` in global.css). If that CSS regresses (rule dropped, selector renamed, specificity change), the fixed bar overlays the top of the page while the card is in view and no test fails; the component tests cannot catch it either since happy-dom never drives the IntersectionObserver. The goal requires the tests to fail if the bar's visibility breaks; only the JS (observer → aria-hidden) half is covered.
findings.fix: Locate the bar by a stable non-role hook (e.g. `page.locator('.minis-summary-bar')` or a data-testid) and assert visual hiddenness directly — `toHaveAttribute('data-visible','false')` plus `toBeHidden()`/`not.toBeInViewport()` on that element — at the initial and post-'Изменить' checkpoints.

findings.title: DESIGN.md records the header card but not the new sticky summary bar, popover, or the new tinted surfaces
findings.body: The change updates the layout bullets for the header card but says nothing about the fixed summary bar (translucent `color-mix(... surface-elevated 94%, transparent)` with backdrop blur and a box-shadow) or the PDF column's `color-mix(in oklch, var(--color-primary) 5%, ...)` tint (global.css:271, 286-289). DESIGN.md itself states 'Не вводить новые цвета без обновления этого файла' and 'Не использовать ... drop-shadow по умолчанию'; a contributor reading the design doc as the source of UI rules has no record that these surfaces exist or were sanctioned.
findings.fix: Add a line under Spacing & layout / Components describing the summary bar (appears when the settings card leaves the viewport, shows settings + Изменить + Скачать PDF) and list the two tinted surfaces in the palette notes.

findings.title: Браузерный тест не проверяет закрытие popover и восстановление черновика
findings.body: Тест вводит допустимое значение и нажимает Tab, но не проверяет закрытие через Escape или внешний клик, возврат фокуса и восстановление после недопустимого значения. Поэтому регрессия, при которой в браузере popover не закрывается или после закрытия кнопки PDF остаются заблокированы, не будет обнаружена браузерным тестом. Это покрытие явно требуется для изменения.
findings.fix: Добавить браузерные сценарии закрытия через Escape и внешний клик с недопустимым значением, проверкой фокуса и доступности действий PDF.

findings.title: PDF check would pass if the sticky bar downloaded the wrong document
findings.body: The test only checks the `%PDF-` signature. If the sticky bar's button downloaded some other PDF, such as the scale test sheet, instead of the minis, the check would still pass. It does not confirm the requirement that the bar's button does the same thing as the card's button.
findings.fix: Check the downloaded PDF's content for something that independently identifies the loaded minis, or compare it with the card action's output for the same inputs.

findings.title: The sticky-bar e2e test checks "hidden" through aria-hidden and "visible" without checking position, so CSS breakage would still pass
findings.body:
The bar is always rendered. `aria-hidden={!headerOutOfView}` and `data-visible` both come from the same React state. Visual hiding is done only in CSS (`.minis-summary-bar` with `visibility: hidden` and translateY(-100%), and `[data-visible='true']` to show it).

The test locates the button with `page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Изменить' })`. Playwright role locators leave out elements with aria-hidden="true". So `await expect(edit).toBeHidden()` at line ~298 and again after the edit click pass because the locator matches nothing. They pass whatever the CSS does.

The reverse check has the same gap. `toBeVisible()` only needs a non-empty box with visibility not hidden. It does not need the bar on screen. The PDF click and the edit click scroll their target into view before clicking.

Concrete green-while-broken cases (inferred from Playwright's documented semantics, not run):
- The base rule loses `visibility:hidden` or `transform`. The bar then sits over the page header on load, and the test still passes.
- `position: fixed` stops pinning to the viewport, for example because an ancestor becomes a containing block. The bar then scrolls away with the editor, and the test still passes.

The goal asks for tests that fail when the bar's visibility breaks. These tests only check the React state, not what the user sees.
findings.fix: Find the bar by locator instead of by role (e.g. `page.locator('.minis-summary-bar')`) and assert `toBeHidden()` on load and after Изменить. After scrolling, also check that its `boundingBox().y` is about 0 and within the viewport, e.g. with `toBeInViewport()`.

findings.title: The fixed summary bar covers the top of the viewport and there is no scroll-padding, so focused controls can end up underneath it
findings.body:
While the header card is out of view, `.minis-summary-bar` is `position: fixed; inset-block-start: 0; z-index: 40` with `min-block-size: 3rem` plus padding (about 56px). Nothing sets `scroll-padding-block-start` on the scrolling root; only the card gets `scroll-margin-block-start`.

When a keyboard user Shift+Tabs upward through the minis list, the browser scrolls each newly focused control to the top edge of the viewport, where the bar sits. Row controls are about 40–44px tall (`h-10`/`min-h-11`), so the focused control and its focus ring can be fully hidden behind the bar.

The project's review profile names controls that can't be reached or understood by keyboard. This regression comes from adding the fixed bar. The old sticky sidebar did not overlay the list.
findings.fix: While the bar is visible, set `scroll-padding-block-start` on `html` to about the bar's height, e.g. `html:has(.minis-summary-bar[data-visible='true']) { scroll-padding-block-start: 4.5rem; }`.

findings.title: The "▾" glyph is plain button text, so it becomes part of the scale trigger's accessible name
findings.body:
The printer scale trigger renders `'Масштаб ▾'` (or `… мм ▾`) as plain text. Its accessible name is therefore "Масштаб ▾", and the tests even query by that name. Screen readers read the decorative glyph aloud, for example as "black down-pointing small triangle".

The rest of the component marks the disclosure chevron as decorative: "Сменить высоту" uses `<ChevronDownIcon aria-hidden="true" />`. This new control breaks that pattern, so a keyboard or screen-reader user hears a symbol name as part of the label.
findings.fix: Replace the text `▾` with `<ChevronDownIcon aria-hidden="true" />`, as "Сменить высоту" does, and update the test queries to `'Масштаб'` / `'Масштаб · 91 мм'`.

findings.title: Сводка настроек обрезается без переноса
findings.body: На узком экране длинная сводка, например с форматом, полями, стилем, нумерацией и масштабом, обрезается классом truncate. Пользователь видит многоточие вместо части текущих настроек и не может прочитать их в панели.
findings.fix: Разрешить перенос текста сводки или предоставить способ увидеть её целиком.

findings.title: Ошибка скачивания отображается только в карточке вне экрана
findings.body: Если создание PDF или объектного URL завершается ошибкой после нажатия кнопки в плавающей панели, сообщение появляется только в карточке настроек. В этот момент карточка находится вне экрана, поэтому пользователь видит отсутствие скачивания без объяснения причины.
findings.fix: Показать сообщение о результате рядом с действием в плавающей панели.

findings.title: `Изменить` focuses before scrolling, so focus() jumps the page instantly and the smooth scroll / reduced-motion branch has nothing left to animate
findings.body: The handler calls `firstField?.focus()` first and `header.scrollIntoView({behavior: shouldAnimate ? 'smooth' : 'auto', block: 'start'})` second. A plain `focus()` already scrolls the browser so the focused element is in view, and that scroll is instant. By the time scrollIntoView runs, the page has already jumped to the header. The only movement left to animate is the small adjustment to `block: 'start'` plus `scroll-margin-block-start`. The page therefore scrolls twice, and the `matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference)')` lookup barely changes anything. Issue #151 asks for a button that "scrolls back to the header and focuses its first field", and the code reads as if it means to animate that scroll.
findings.fix: Use `firstField?.focus({ preventScroll: true })` so that the single `scrollIntoView` call handles the scroll and the motion preference.

findings.title: The 'closes on Escape and an outside click' test repeats the dismissal contract already covered by the test.each above it and the focus-return test
findings.body: I tried to find a change that turns this test red and nothing else. Two candidates: make the popover non-dismissable (`isDismissable={false}`), or disable keyboard dismissal. With either one, the onOpenChange commit never runs. The `closing the printer scale with $close…` test.each then fails on both rows, because `enabledAfterClose` stays `[false,false,false]` and reopening through `triggerName` toggles instead. The focus test also fails on `open: false` after Escape. This test adds no change of its own that would make it fail, and neither test says which one owns dismissal. It is extra suite surface that every later reviewer has to read and keep in sync, with no added protection.
findings.fix: Delete this test, or merge its open/closed assertions into the test.each and name that test as the owner of dismissal.
