findings.title: The scale popover passes an undefined class and restyles things the new Popover primitive already sets
findings.body: `minis-scale-popover` is defined nowhere: `rg minis-scale-popover` finds only this line, with no CSS rule and no test selector. `rounded-lg` and `shadow-md` repeat the primitive's own defaults in `src/components/ui/popover.tsx:37`. `bg-surface-elevated` replaces `bg-popover`, but `--color-popover` is `var(--color-surface-elevated)` (global.css:76), so the colour is the same. The new primitive exists so callers don't have to restyle it, yet this one caller re-declares its look. The added `border border-border` also stacks on the default `ring-1 ring-foreground/10`, which gives the popover a doubled edge. If you drop the dead class and the repeated utilities, the result is identical because tailwind-merge resolves to the same values. Only the width override does something.
findings.fix: Reduce the className to `w-[min(24rem,calc(100vw-2rem))] p-4`. Keep `border border-border` only if the doubled edge is intended, and in that case drop the ring.

findings.title: No test passes --only and --exclude together, and test 026's awk filter drops the Exclusions section, so the required separation can regress silently
findings.body:
The goal requires `--only` and `--exclude` to stay separate, with tests that fail if that breaks. `build_scope` gets one flat argument list: fixed values, then `only_count` pathspecs, then exclusions (script L376-384, split by shift at L89-93). Keeping the two apart depends on `only_count` and on the order of the two append loops in `next`.

Tests 026-028 pass `--only` with no `--exclude`. Tests 007 and 015 pass `--exclude` with no `--only`, so with only_count=0 the order of the loops never matters. Test 026 also filters scope.md through awk, which prints only the Scale, Limited to, Read the change, Commits and Changed files sections. After the Changed-files fence closes, the Exclusions heading and its bullets are dropped.

Two regressions that leave the suite green:
- (a) The two append loops are swapped. Then `--only app --exclude 'skip docs'` writes `Limited to: skip docs`, `git diff BASE..HEAD -- skip\ docs`, and `- app` under Exclusions.
- (b) The shift loop stops consuming, or the pathspecs are also appended as exclusions. Then scope.md tells reviewers to exclude the very paths it limits them to.

The git facts stay correct in both cases, but reviewers get the wrong scope.
findings.fix: In test 026, or a sibling test, also pass `--exclude 'some prose'`. Assert the whole scope.md exactly, or extend the awk filter to print the Exclusions section, so that the pathspecs appear only in Limited to and the read commands, and the exclusion appears only as a bullet.

findings.title: The `%q` quoting of pathspecs in the generated read commands is untested
findings.body:
`build_scope` writes the `Read the change:` commands with `printf ' %q'` (script L113-114, L121-122), so glob and magic pathspecs reach git literally. The only success-path test that checks the read commands (026) uses `app` and `docs/guide.md`, which print the same under `%q` and `%s`. Tests 027/028 use `missing/**/*.md` and `:(exclude)alpha.txt`, but they fail before any scope is written.

If `%q` became `%s`, every test would still pass. Reviewers would then get `-- :(exclude)alpha.txt`, a bash syntax error at `(`, or `-- docs/*.md`. Bash expands that glob to files that exist now, so deleted files drop out of the diff. In zsh it fails with `no matches found`. Either way the read commands would no longer select the same pathspec list as the git facts.
findings.fix: Use a glob or magic pathspec in test 026's `--only` set, or in a sibling success-path test, e.g. `':(glob)app/*.txt'`. Assert the exact `%q`-escaped `git diff`/`git log` lines.

findings.title: Pathspec plumbing duplicated across three if/else branches and two identical printf loops
findings.body: In next() (L347-360), the scale, commits and changed_files computations each have an if/else whose branches are the same git command with and without `-- "${only_values[@]}"`. In build_scope (L111-116 and L119-124), the loop that prints ` --` and each `%q` pathspec is pasted twice. A single `pathspec_args=(--)` array with the only values appended would work without branching: a trailing bare `--` gives the same git output, and a one-element array expands safely under `set -u` on Bash 3.2. As written, any change to how pathspecs reach git must be made in five places, or the scope's git facts and its read commands drift apart.
findings.fix: In next(), build `pathspec_args=(--)` plus the only values once and pass `"${pathspec_args[@]}"` to each git command. In build_scope, build the `%q` suffix once and append it to both read commands.

findings.title: `--only` guidance contradicts the unchanged rule that every later round covers the whole change, and the finish rule ignores path-limited rounds
findings.body: The change adds (L102-103) "When the follow-up targets only part of the cumulative change, add one repeatable `--only <pathspec>` per part to review." Two other places in the same file were not updated. Step 1 (L23-24) still says "Every later round covers this same cumulative scope plus its fixes, against the same base". Step 5 rule 3 (L212-214) ends the loop when "this complete round needs no further eligible fixes", with nothing saying whether a round limited by `--only` counts as complete coverage. An agent runs this file as its instructions, so it gets two conflicting orders and no rule for when narrowing is allowed. It can go either way. It may never use `--only` because L23 forbids partial rounds. Or it may run an `--only` round, see no eligible findings, and apply rule 3, which finishes the review and reports it converged when only the selected paths were re-reviewed. The profile-narrowing rules already guard against this for profiles (L78, "A partial or failed review cannot justify narrowing"; L82-83, report coverage explicitly), but nothing similar covers path narrowing. Which side is wrong: L23 and rule 3 have fallen behind the new option, so the fix is in the prose, not the script.
findings.fix: Change L23 so a follow-up round may be limited with `--only`. Add to step 5 that a round limited with `--only` cannot finish the loop or count as full coverage: finishing needs a round over the full scope, or the final report must name the limited paths as the reviewed coverage.

findings.title: The `# post-apply:` run-order key was changed as if it were a test count
findings.body: `tests/run-post-apply.sh` reads the number in `# post-apply: <N> <eligibility>` as the run order. It sorts files with `sort -n` and rejects duplicate values with "duplicate post-apply order". This file has been order 27 since 6492855 while holding 24 functions. The change moves it to 28, and the file now has 27 functions, so the new value is neither a count nor needed. Nothing breaks today. But bumping it on every test addition will eventually collide with another file's order, for example platform_test.sh at 40, and the runner will then fail the whole host-safe suite.
findings.fix: Restore `# post-apply: 27 host-safe`.

findings.title: Nothing tests the shell quoting of pathspecs in the generated read commands
findings.body: `build_scope` writes the `Read the change:` commands with `printf ' %q'` (script L114, L122), so pathspecs with glob characters or pathspec magic can be pasted into a shell as-is. Test 026 only uses `app` and `docs/guide.md`, which come out the same under `%q` and `%s`. If the quoting were dropped or swapped for `%s`, test 026 would still pass. Reviewers would then get `git diff <base>..HEAD -- :(exclude)alpha.txt` (a bash syntax error at `(`) or `-- missing/**/*.md`, which the shell expands as a glob instead of passing it to git. Tests 027/028 already use exactly these pathspecs (`missing/**/*.md`, `:(exclude)alpha.txt`), so these are inputs the option accepts.
findings.fix: In test 026, or a sibling success case, use a glob or magic pathspec that matches, e.g. `--only ':(glob)app/*.txt'`. Assert that the read-command line holds the `%q`-escaped form, and that running that line through `bash -c` gives the same `--name-status` output as the `Changed files:` block.

findings.title: Test 26 checks scope.md through an awk filter that cannot see the Exclusions section, and no test uses --only together with --exclude
findings.body:
One of the goal's stated correctness conditions is that `--only` and `--exclude` stay separate, and that the tests would fail if that broke. Neither direction is tested.

What I read:
- Test 26 does not compare the whole scope.md. Its awk program prints only the `Scale:` and `Limited to:` lines and the lines inside the Read-the-change, Commits and Changed-files fences.
- After the Changed-files fence closes, `section = 0`. From then on the `Exclusions:` heading and its `- …` lines match no rule and are dropped.
- No test anywhere passes `--only` and `--exclude` together.

The mixing only exists inside `build_scope`. It receives the `--only` values and the exclusions as one argument list (`scope_args`) and separates them by counting off `only_count` with `shift`. Suppose that hand-off breaks: the shift loop at executable_revmux-round.sh:90-93 stops consuming, or `next` also appends the `--only` values to the exclusion arguments. Then scope.md gains `Exclusions:\n\n- app\n- docs/guide.md` and test 26 still passes.

The effect on a real round would be a scope that tells reviewers to exclude the exact paths it limits them to. Existing exclusion-only tests do not catch this because they never pass `--only`. The code is correct today; this is a coverage gap against the goal, not a current defect.
findings.fix: In test 26, also pass `--exclude 'fixture exclusion'` and assert scope.md exactly (for example by extending `expected_scope`), so a pathspec that leaks into Exclusions, or an exclusion that leaks into the pathspec list, turns the test red.

findings.title: No test pathspec contains a shell metacharacter, so the `%q` quoting of the Read-the-change commands is never checked
findings.body:
`build_scope` writes the reviewer's commands as `git diff BASE..HEAD -- <%q pathspec>…` (executable_revmux-round.sh:113-114 and 121-122). Test 26's pathspecs are `app` and `docs/guide.md`, which `%q` leaves unchanged. Test 27's glob `missing/**/*.md` only reaches the error path, before any scope is written.

So if `%q` became `%s`, the suite would stay green. The broken output would be `git diff BASE..HEAD -- docs/*.md`:
- In bash, the shell expands the glob to files that exist now, so deleted files drop out of the reviewer's diff, while the Changed-files list (computed by git with the literal pathspec) still shows them.
- In zsh, the default shell here, an unmatched glob makes the command fail with `no matches found`.

Either way the read command would stop selecting the same pathspec list as the git facts, which the goal requires and requires tests to protect. Bash 3.2 and Homebrew bash both produce correct `%q` output today (checked: `:\(glob\)docs/\*\*/\*.md`), so this is a test gap, not a current bug.
findings.fix: Make one of test 26's pathspecs contain a glob or magic, for example `':(glob)app/*.txt'`, and assert the escaped form in the expected `git diff`/`git log` lines.

findings.title: SKILL.md lets the agent narrow a follow-up round by path but gives no rule for when that is allowed or what a clean narrowed round proves
findings.body:
SKILL.md is the contract the agent executes for follow-up rounds. The new sentence permits `--only` whenever "the follow-up targets only part of the cumulative change".

Profile narrowing in the same skill is guarded: it says "A partial or failed review cannot justify narrowing", tells the agent to keep the broader coverage when unsure, and to report coverage explicitly. Path narrowing gets none of these rules. Step 5 rule 3 then ends the loop on any complete round that produced no eligible fixes, and rule 2 requires every fix to get a confirming round.

A reachable sequence:
1. Round N's fixes touch paths A and B.
2. The agent runs round N+1 with `--only A`.
3. The round comes back clean, so rule 3 ends the loop.
4. B's fix never got a confirming round, and the final report does not say coverage was limited to A.

The script behaves correctly here. The gap is in the agent-facing policy, so the severity follows what the agent would do wrong; it stays minor because reaching it takes an agent choosing a narrower path set than its fixes touched.
findings.fix: Add one sentence: the `--only` set must cover every path the fixes since the previous round touched, and a round limited to paths confirms only those paths. The report states the limit.

findings.title: No test runs --only together with --exclude, so mixing up the two arguments in scope.md stays green
findings.body:
The goal says `--only` and `--exclude` must stay separate and that the tests must fail if that breaks. `build_scope` gets both lists as one positional run: `only_count`, then the only values, then the exclusions (executable_revmux-round.sh:376-384). It takes the first `only_count` of them as pathspecs and treats the rest as exclusions. Tests 026–028 pass only `--only`. Test 015 passes only `--exclude`, with only_count=0, so the order of the two append loops never matters. Test 026 also uses awk to keep only the Scale, Limited-to, Read, Commits and Changed-files sections, so an Exclusions section is never checked.

Here is an edit that should fail a test but does not: swap the two append loops at lines 378-383 so the exclusions are appended first. Then `next --only app --exclude 'skip generated'` writes `Limited to: skip generated`, `git diff BASE..HEAD -- skip\ generated` and `Exclusions: - app`. Reviewers get the wrong read commands and a wrong exclusion. The git facts are still right, because `next()` computes them from `only_values` directly. All 28 tests stay green.
findings.fix: Add `--exclude 'some prose'` to the `run_prepare_only` call in test 026. Then either stop filtering the scope through awk, or add `Exclusions:` and its list items to the sections the awk script prints. That pins `Limited to: app, docs/guide.md`, the `-- app docs/guide.md` read commands and `- some prose` under Exclusions in one exact assertion.

findings.title: The combined --only check runs a separate git diff that the changed_files computation a few lines later repeats
findings.body:
The combined-pathspec block (lines 335-344) runs `git diff --name-only BASE..HEAD -- "${only_values[@]}"` only to check whether the output is empty. Line 356 then runs `git diff --name-status` on the same range and the same pathspecs to set `changed_files`. For the same range and pathspecs, name-status output is empty exactly when name-only output is empty. Both run before `revmux new` (and before the scope is written), and the steps in between (`rev-parse`, `--shortstat`, `log`) have no side effects. So checking `[ -n "$changed_files" ]` right after line 356 gives the same error message, exit status and no-round-created outcome that test 028 asserts.

The separate block's "cannot evaluate combined --only pathspecs" branch is effectively unreachable. The loop above it has already parsed every pathspec on its own. If git did fail at line 356, `set -e` would stop the script, because `next` is called without any surrounding conditional. With one `--only`, the combined block exactly repeats the check the loop just made. The change removes one git diff over the whole range and a second error branch that duplicates the first.
findings.fix: Delete lines 335-344. Inside the `only_count -gt 0` branch, right after `changed_files` is set at line 356, add `[ -n "$changed_files" ] || { error "combined --only pathspecs match no changes in $base..HEAD"; return 1; }`.

findings.title: `--only` guidance contradicts the cumulative-scope rule and gives no rule for when path narrowing is allowed or what a clean narrowed round proves
findings.body: New L102-103 says: "When the follow-up targets only part of the cumulative change, add one repeatable `--only <pathspec>` per part to review." Step 1 (L23-24, not changed by this PR) still says "Every later round covers this same cumulative scope plus its fixes, against the same base". The two passages give opposite instructions for the same decision. The skill never says what "targets only part" means. Profile narrowing gets a written policy at L69-83 (retain broader coverage when the boundary is uncertain, never narrow after a partial or failed review, report the resulting coverage). Path narrowing gets nothing comparable. In particular, nothing requires the `--only` set to include every path that the fixes since the previous round touched. That leaves a gap. Round N fixes paths A and B, round N+1 runs with `--only A`, and the round comes back clean. B's fix then never gets the confirming round that step 5 rule 2 (L209-211) requires. Rule 1 ("coverage is incomplete, stop as blocked") and L220 ("Report ... source coverage") may catch this, but the skill never says whether a path-limited round counts as incomplete coverage or as the "complete round" of rule 3. So the outcome depends on how the agent reads it. The scope file the script writes does print a "Limited to:" line, but its opening sentence still says "review the cumulative change".
findings.fix: Amend L23-24 to allow `--only` follow-up rounds under a stated rule. Next to the profile-narrowing policy, state: the `--only` set must cover every path touched by fixes since the previous round; never narrow after a partial or failed round; a path-limited round confirms only the selected paths and does not by itself satisfy step 5 rule 3; the final report names the `--only` limit as its source coverage.

findings.title: Rate-limit retry matches any object with data.key, not specifically a MembraneError
findings.body: The goal requires connectionGraphql to retry only a MembraneError with `error.data.key === 'rate_limit_exceeded'`. `RateLimitRefusal` checks only the shape `{ data: { key: 'rate_limit_exceeded' } }`. Nothing checks that the error is a MembraneError, for example the `isMembraneError: true` marker the test fixture `rateLimitRefusal` sets. So any thrown object with that data shape would get up to 3 attempts and real sleeps. Current clients do not produce such an object: the REST client throws CommandError and the routine clients wrap membrane().run. That makes this a divergence from the stated contract rather than an observed failure.
findings.fix: Add `isMembraneError: Schema.Literal(true)` to the `RateLimitRefusal` struct.

findings.title: Rate-limit guard matches any thrown value with data.key, not only a MembraneError
findings.body: The goal says `connectionGraphql` retries only a MembraneError whose `data.key === 'rate_limit_exceeded'`. `RateLimitRefusal` checks only `{ data: { key: 'rate_limit_exceeded' } }` and ignores the `isMembraneError: true` marker. The test fixture `rateLimitRefusal` sets that marker, and the comment on line 252 calls the error a MembraneError, but the guard never reads it. As a result, any other error or plain object with `data.key === 'rate_limit_exceeded'` is retried up to 3 attempts with real sleeps, when the contract says it should be rethrown unchanged. This also applies to GraphQL mutations sent through connectionGraphql, which could be repeated. If a later retry succeeds, the original error is hidden. Today the only thrower here is `client.run('call-connection')`, so the observed impact may be small.
findings.fix: Add `isMembraneError: Schema.Literal(true)` to the `RateLimitRefusal` struct.

findings.title: Rate-limit guard matches any thrown value with data.key, not only a MembraneError
findings.body: The goal says `connectionGraphql` retries only a MembraneError whose `data.key === 'rate_limit_exceeded'`. `RateLimitRefusal` checks only `{ data: { key: 'rate_limit_exceeded' } }`, so it ignores the `isMembraneError: true` marker. The test fixture `rateLimitRefusal` in linear-graphql.test.ts sets that marker, and the comment on line 252 describes the error as a MembraneError, but the guard never reads it. Any other error or plain object that happens to carry `data.key === 'rate_limit_exceeded'` gets retried and slept on, when the contract says it should be rethrown unchanged. In practice the only thrower here is `client.run('call-connection')`, so the impact is small. No test covers a lookalike that is not a MembraneError.
findings.fix: Add `isMembraneError: Schema.Literal(true)` to the `RateLimitRefusal` struct, and add a test where an error with the same key but no `isMembraneError` is rethrown after one call.

findings.title: Повтор выполняется и для ошибок, которые не являются MembraneError
findings.body: Контракт в goal.md разрешает повтор только для MembraneError с ключом rate_limit_exceeded. Эта схема проверяет только data.key, поэтому любой другой объект ошибки с таким ключом тоже вызывает до двух повторных вызовов вместо немедленного возврата исходной ошибки. Это также относится к вызовам GraphQL-мутаций через connectionGraphql.
findings.fix: Проверять признак MembraneError вместе с data.key перед повтором.

findings.title: Nothing tests the bound on the sync routine's thread reads, so a return to unbounded Promise.all would go unnoticed
findings.body: This change routes the sync routine's thread reads through `mapBounded(..., THREAD_READ_LIMIT, ...)`, but the only test that checks the bound is the 120-candidate test in `linear-port.test.ts`, and that test covers only the `listCandidates` path. `packages/ux-chain/lib/sync-entry.test.ts` already runs the real routine (`(await import('../../../entries/ux-chain-sync')).default`) against a fake `cmd` that answers the `Comments` operation. However, every scenario there lists a single issue and never counts how many calls are in flight. If someone changed `entries/ux-chain-sync.ts:247` back to `Promise.all(issues.map(...))`, every test would still pass, and sync would again fire one `call-connection` per issue at once. With 100+ issues needing a thread read, that hits the platform's 100-parallel-request limit, which is the failure this change exists to fix.
findings.fix: In sync-entry.test.ts, add a routine-level case where `IssuesByTeam` returns more than 8 issues that each need a thread read. Have the `Comments` branch of the fake `cmd` track the in-flight count with a short await, then assert the maximum equals 8.

findings.title: The test for an unrelated error uses a different key, so retrying a non-MembraneError lookalike goes unnoticed
findings.body: The test that checks an unrelated error is not retried uses an error with a different key. It does not cover an error that has `data.key === 'rate_limit_exceeded'` but no MembraneError marker. That means it stays green even though `connectionGraphql` retries any error with that key, when the contract requires such an error to be rethrown right away.
findings.fix: Add a case where the error has key `rate_limit_exceeded` but no `isMembraneError` marker. Assert one call, no wait, and the original error rethrown unchanged.

findings.title: Проверка отказа не различает MembraneError и другие ошибки
findings.body: Проверка принимает любой объект с `data.key === 'rate_limit_exceeded'`, хотя контракт разрешает повторять только MembraneError. Если `client.run` выбросит другую ошибку с таким полем, `connectionGraphql` повторит запрос вместо немедленного возврата исходной ошибки. Это также относится к мутациям GraphQL.
findings.fix: Добавить в проверку признак MembraneError и проверить случай другой ошибки с тем же ключом.

findings.title: Тест не проверяет, что повторяются только MembraneError
findings.body: Тест передаёт ошибку с другим ключом и потому проходит, даже если код повторяет запрос для любой ошибки с data.key равным rate_limit_exceeded. Это уже делает RateLimitRefusal: он не проверяет признак MembraneError. Если другая ошибка несёт такой ключ, запрос повторится до трёх раз вместо немедленного возврата исходной ошибки.
findings.fix: Добавить случай с ошибкой, у которой есть ключ rate_limit_exceeded, но нет признака MembraneError, и проверять один вызов без ожидания.

findings.title: The exhausted-retry test cannot tell the last refusal from the first
findings.body: All three attempts throw the same refusal object. The test would still pass if the code rethrew the first error after the last attempt instead of the last one. When the refusals differ, the caller would then get stale error details.
findings.fix: Throw a separate object on each attempt and assert that the third attempt's object is the one rethrown.

findings.title: The reviewed state does not contain the PRD-3672 change: offerAccepted sends no section on either offer page
findings.body:
The scoped range 4bdce06aa7..6fbfb05e2f is not the 10-file PRD-3672 change. HEAD (6fbfb05e2f) is four partner-preview commits on merge-base 79810ee497. Those commits touch only partner-profile and Partner dashboard files, 13 files in all. The base 4bdce06aa7 (PRD-3663/3666, #6813) is not an ancestor of HEAD; it is 88 commits further along main. The two-dot diff therefore spans 1090 files (+45,913/−89,634), and no commit for PRD-3672 is reachable.

On HEAD, `press()` builds `accepted = { offerKey, company?, amazonStoreKey? }` with no `section` (amazon-scorecard-offer.tsx:486-495; the checkup page matches). So presses on the ticket, the store block and the close band cannot be told apart. `CTA_SECTIONS`, `CtaSection` and `ctaAttrs` do not exist in site.ts on HEAD, and the Start buttons carry no `data-cta-section`. The test at amazon-scorecard-offer.test.ts:719-724 asserts the payload without `section`.

Every condition the change is meant to meet fails on this state, so the reported green test and typecheck result cannot belong to it. The ctaClicked and CTA-naming removals that appear in the two-dot diff are an artifact of the base being ahead on main: no commit on HEAD's line removes them.
findings.fix: Point the review at the real prd-3672-offer-page-name tip, diffed from its merge-base with main (`git diff $(git merge-base main <tip>)..<tip>`), and rerun the tests there. On both pages, pass the pressed button's section (ticket / hero / close-band) into offerAccepted.

findings.title: offerAccepted не указывает нажатую кнопку
findings.body: На проверенном HEAD обработчик отправляет offerAccepted без свойства section. Поэтому при нажатии на билет, кнопку рядом с магазином или кнопку в конце страницы событие не позволяет определить, какую кнопку нажал посетитель. Та же проблема есть в amazon-checkup-offer.tsx:504. Проблема существовала до сравниваемого изменения; заявленная цель на проверенном HEAD не реализована.
findings.fix: Добавить секции ticket, hero и close-band к соответствующим кнопкам и передавать секцию нажатой кнопки в offerAccepted на обеих страницах.

findings.title: The reviewed state does not contain the PRD-3672 change: offerAccepted sends no section and CTA_SECTIONS does not exist
findings.body: The scope says the change adds `section` (from `data-cta-section`) to `offerAccepted` and a `ticket` entry to `CTA_SECTIONS`. The range it gives, 4bdce06aa7..6fbfb05e2f, is two diverged branches with merge-base 79810ee497. HEAD (6fbfb05e2f) holds four partner-preview commits ('Lock partner preview readiness handshake' and others). 4bdce06aa7 is PRD-3663 (#6813) plus 87 other commits. The diff touches 1090 files and, in console/components/marketing, takes `data-cta-section` and `ctaAttrs` out instead of adding to them. On HEAD, `press()` builds `accepted = { offerKey, company?, amazonStoreKey? }` with no `section` (amazon-scorecard-offer.tsx:488-495), and `console/components/marketing/site.ts` has no `CTA_SECTIONS` or `ctaAttrs`. No commit on any branch adds `'ticket'` to site.ts (`git log --all -S"'ticket'" -- site.ts` is empty), and there is no prd-3672 branch. So every 'correct only if' condition fails on the reviewed state. If this range ships as the PR, the gift ticket, store block and closing band all send `offerAccepted` with no `section`, and PRD-3663's ctaClicked section naming is reverted across the public pages. The supplied '406 tests green' result therefore cannot apply to this tree.
findings.fix: Check out the actual prd-3672-offer-page-name commit, or rebase the PRD-3672 work onto 4bdce06aa7, and run the review again on that state.

findings.title: offerAccepted не содержит section на обеих страницах
findings.body: При нажатии любой из трёх кнопок объект события содержит только offerKey и, при наличии, company и amazonStoreKey. Получатель PostHog не может определить, нажали ticket, hero или close-band. То же построение объекта находится в console/components/marketing/pages/amazon-checkup-offer.tsx:504. Это существовало до рассматриваемого диапазона: исходный обработчик тоже не добавлял section, поэтому заявленный контракт изменения не выполнен.
findings.fix: Добавить секцию на каждую кнопку и передавать её из нажатого элемента в offerAccepted на обеих страницах.

findings.title: Удалён сбор ctaClicked для кнопок и остальных CTA
findings.body: Из кнопок предложения удалены data-cta и data-cta-section; то же произошло на странице Checkup. Кроме того, в console/components/marketing/document.tsx:85 удалён общий обработчик, который отправлял ctaClicked для размеченных элементов. При нажатии кнопки ticket, hero или close-band это событие больше не отправляется, поэтому его нельзя сопоставить с offerAccepted. Удаление общего обработчика также прекращает сбор ctaClicked на остальных маркетинговых страницах. Прежний общий обработчик и разметка задавали существующий способ сбора этих событий.
findings.fix: Восстановить общий обработчик и разметку CTA, указав для кнопок предложения секции ticket, hero и close-band.

findings.title: The reviewed HEAD (6fbfb05e2f) does not contain the PRD-3672 change, and the scoped range reverts PRD-3663
findings.body:
The scope names branch `prd-3672-offer-page-name`, "10 files changed, 114 insertions(+), 14 deletions(-)". The scope's own command, `git diff 4bdce06aa7..6fbfb05e2f`, gives "1090 files changed, 45913 insertions(+), 89634 deletions(-)" instead.

The base 4bdce06aa7 (PRD-3663, #6813) is 88 commits ahead of HEAD. `git merge-base` returns 79810ee497. HEAD is a partner-preview commit ("fix: remove eager partner preview post") with no PRD-3672 work. `git log --all --grep=3672` finds no branch commit.

On HEAD, none of the goal's "correct only if" conditions hold:
- `press()` in amazon-scorecard-offer.tsx:488-495 builds `accepted = { offerKey, company?, amazonStoreKey? }` with no `section`. The same is true of amazon-checkup-offer.tsx:~508. So a gift-ticket, store-block or close-band press sends no `section`.
- `CTA_SECTIONS` and `ctaAttrs` are missing from console/components/marketing/site.ts, so there is no `ticket` CtaSection.
- The diff deletes `CTA_NAMES`, `CTA_SECTIONS`, `ctaAttrs` and `BOOK_CALL_PLACEMENTS`. It strips `data-cta`/`data-cta-section` from the offer pages' gift ticket, store block, blocked notice and close band. It also drops the `section` parameter of `contactEmailHtml`. Together this undoes PRD-3663's `ctaClicked` naming.
- The `offerAccepted` lines in internal-dev-doc/posthog-session-replay.md and .claude/skills/offer-pages/SKILL.md at HEAD say nothing about `section`.

If this range ships as reviewed, the PRD-3663 CTA tracking regresses and the feature is still missing. The reported "406 tests green / typecheck exit 0" results cannot belong to the described change, because it is not in this tree.
findings.fix: Re-point the review at the real `prd-3672-offer-page-name` head, whose merge-base should be 4bdce06aa7, and re-run the diff. Do not open the PR from 6fbfb05e2f.

findings.title: Tests pin offerAccepted without section and check only the first button
findings.body: The test expects offerAccepted without `section` and exercises only the first button; amazon-checkup-offer.test.ts expects the same. Both suites pass even though none of the three buttons sends ticket, hero or close-band on the reviewed version.
findings.fix: On both pages, assert the event from each of the three buttons with its expected section value.

findings.title: Удалены проверки событий CTA для маркетинговых страниц
findings.body: Из набора удалены проверки разметки и событий CTA. Одновременно из POSTHOG_SCRIPT удалён обработчик ctaClicked, поэтому на маркетинговых страницах эти события больше не отправляются. findings.title: Skill step tells the agent to publish to the old offers.membrane.agency host via a procedure that doesn't reach it

The command described above, pages:publish, publishes a static artifact to the platform, and line 100 says uploads to the old host go through a script on Daniil's machine. findings.title: The reviewed HEAD does not contain the PRD-3672 change. The scoped range removes CTA_SECTIONS, ctaAttrs and every data-cta attribute instead
findings.body:
Observed: the scoped command is `git diff 4bdce06aa7..6fbfb05e2f`. 4bdce06aa7 (PRD-3663/3666, #6813) is not an ancestor of HEAD. The merge base is 79810ee497, and the base is 88 commits ahead of it. HEAD's own 4 commits (bbc3780d79..6fbfb05e2f) touch only partner-profile files: 13 files, none of them on the scope's read-in-full list. No branch or commit for PRD-3672 exists in the repo (`git branch -a --list '*3672*'` and `git log --all --grep=3672` return nothing relevant).

What the reviewed state actually has:
- `press()` in amazon-scorecard-offer.tsx:486-495 and amazon-checkup-offer.tsx (~line 508) sends `offerAccepted` with only `offerKey`, `company` and `amazonStoreKey`. There is no `section`.
- `site.ts` has no `CTA_SECTIONS`, `CtaSection`, `CTA_NAMES` or `ctaAttrs`. The scoped diff deletes them (site.ts:119-153 on the base side).
- The scoped diff strips `data-cta` and `data-cta-section` from the gift ticket, the store block, the blocked-notice links and the close-band primaries on both offer pages.

Follows from this: every 'Correct only if' criterion fails or cannot be checked. No button sends `section: 'ticket'`, `'hero'` or `'close-band'`. `ticket` is not a valid `CtaSection` because the type does not exist. `ctaClicked` attributes are gone. Read as the change to ship, this diff would reverse PRD-3663/3666's CTA naming (113 files in #6813) rather than add the offer-page section. The 406-test and typecheck result supplied in goal.md cannot be for this state, because the tests and types it describes are not here.
findings.fix: Point the review at the actual `prd-3672-offer-page-name` head, branched from 4bdce06aa7 or later, and rerun the scope command. Don't ship the current range.

findings.title: В offerAccepted отсутствует поле section
findings.body: При нажатии любой кнопки действующего предложения payload содержит offerKey и необязательные company и amazonStoreKey, но не содержит section. Поэтому нельзя определить, нажали ли кнопку на билете, в блоке магазина или в завершающем блоке. Та же логика находится в amazon-checkup-offer.tsx:504. Это состояние существовало до рассматриваемого диапазона изменений; цель PRD-3672 на проверенной ревизии не достигнута.

findings.title: Удалена разметка и обработчик события ctaClicked
findings.body: На проверенной ревизии у кнопок предложения удалены data-cta и data-cta-section, а из document.tsx удалён обработчик, который отправлял ctaClicked. findings.title: The scoped diff deletes CTA_NAMES/CTA_SECTIONS/ctaAttrs and the guarding tests instead of adding a ticket section
findings.body: Computed as scoped, the range removes `CTA_NAMES`, `CTA_SECTIONS`, `CtaSection` and `ctaAttrs` from site.ts, and drops the `data-cta`/`data-cta-section` attributes from `contactEmailHtml`. It also strips the attributes from the offer pages. It deletes the CTA identity, Calendly placement and 'marks every tracked interaction as a CTA' tests from marketing-render.test.ts, and narrows the offer-test regexes back to `target="_top">`, which pass only once the attributes are gone. Shipped as computed, this would revert the CTA tracking from #6813 on every public page and delete the tests that guard it. No ref adds a `'ticket'` CTA section.
findings.fix: Re-run the review against the real prd-3672-offer-page-name tip, diffed from its merge-base with main, after fetching the branch.

findings.title: Удалены проверки отслеживания CTA на публичных страницах
findings.body: Из набора удалена проверка, которая требовала `data-cta` у ссылок `data-offer-go`, а также проверки имен и секций CTA. В этом же diff атрибуты удалены у кнопок принятия предложения на обеих страницах, поэтому их нажатия больше не дают `ctaClicked`. Удалённая проверка обнаружила бы эту потерю; замены, которая проверяет тот же контракт, в изменённом наборе нет.

findings.title: Reviewed HEAD does not contain the PRD-3672 change: offerAccepted carries no section on either offer page
findings.body: The scope's command `git diff 4bdce06aa7..6fbfb05e2f` does not produce the described 10-file PRD-3672 change. HEAD 6fbfb05e2f is a partner-preview branch whose merge-base is 79810ee497. Base 4bdce06aa7 (#6813, the CTA-naming PR) is 88 commits later on main, so the two-dot diff is a reverse diff across those commits: hundreds of files, about 9.6 MB. `git log --all -S` finds no commit that adds a `ticket` CTA section or reads `data-cta-section` in either offer page. On HEAD, the `press` handler in amazon-scorecard-offer.tsx:486-496, and the same handler in amazon-checkup-offer.tsx:498-508, builds `accepted = { offerKey }` and adds only `company` and `amazonStoreKey` before `track('offerAccepted', ...)`. There is no `section`, and the test at amazon-scorecard-offer.test.ts:738 asserts exactly that payload. The GiftTicket, StoreSlot and close-band Start buttons carry no `data-cta-section`. In the scoped range, site.ts deletes `CTA_NAMES`, `CTA_SECTIONS` and `ctaAttrs` instead of adding `ticket`, so `CtaSection` does not exist at HEAD. Every 'Correct only if' criterion fails on this state: the ticket, store block and closing band all send no section, and `ticket` is not a valid CtaSection. The stated green tests and typecheck cannot refer to the PRD-3672 change. If this ref is pushed as the PRD-3672 PR, the intended instrumentation does not ship.
findings.fix: Point the review and the PR at the real prd-3672-offer-page-name tip, diffed against its merge-base with main (`git diff $(git merge-base main <tip>)..<tip>`), and rerun the tests on that tip.

findings.title: offer-pages skill at HEAD has no funnel table, so step 2 does not document offerAccepted.section
findings.body: At HEAD the skill has neither the 'Where an offer goes today' section nor the 'The funnel and its events' table; the scoped hunk deletes them. The trigger description no longer lists offerAccepted or scorecard/amazon/offer. An agent asked where offer traffic lands, or why a funnel step shows no events, would not load the skill and would find no description of offerAccepted or its section property.
findings.fix: Keep the funnel table, with step 2 naming `section` (ticket / hero / close-band).

findings.title: New `--only` guidance contradicts the skill's own rule that every later round covers the full cumulative scope
findings.body: Lines 102-103 now tell the agent that runs follow-up rounds to add `--only <pathspec>` "when the follow-up targets only part of the cumulative change". Step 1 of the same skill (line 23) still says "Every later round covers this same cumulative scope plus its fixes, against the same base". An agent executes this file as its contract, and the two statements give it opposite instructions. Nothing in the skill says what a narrowed round means for convergence. For example, it does not say that paths outside the `--only` set stay unreviewed in that round, or that a narrowed round with `raised 0` does not show the whole cumulative scope is clean. The profile-selection section spells out that caveat for the `final` profile ("a finding omitted by the narrower profile is not thereby resolved") but not for path narrowing. Concrete failure: the agent runs `next --only app`, gets a clean round, and reports convergence for the whole change, while edits outside `app` since the previous round were never reviewed. The option text does match what the script does; the problem is that it conflicts with the other rule in the same file.
findings.fix: Change line 23 to allow the exception, e.g. "…plus its fixes, against the same base, unless a follow-up round is limited with `--only`". Next to the `--only` sentence, add one line saying that coverage outside the listed pathspecs is not reviewed in that round and must be reported that way rather than claimed as converged.

findings.title: No test checks that `--only` and `--exclude` stay separate; the 026 projection discards the Exclusions block
findings.body: One of the goal's acceptance criteria is that `--only` and `--exclude` stay separate and that a test fails if this regresses. `build_scope` now takes both lists through one positional stream: first `only_count`, then the pathspecs, then the exclusions (script lines 82-93 and 376-384). No test passes `--only` and `--exclude` together. Test 026 uses only `--only`, and its awk projection prints only the Scale/Limited-to lines and the fenced Read/Commits/Changed-files blocks. Test 015 uses only `--exclude`. Example regression that passes the whole suite: the `--only` branch at line 217 also appends to `exclude_values`, or `build_scope` keeps `$@` without shifting past the pathspecs. Either way the pathspecs show up as `- app` bullets under `Exclusions:`, telling reviewers to ignore the very paths they were asked to review. Test 026's awk drops everything after the Changed-files fence, so it stays green.
findings.fix: In test 026, also pass one `--exclude 'some prose'`. Then assert the exact Exclusions block (for example, add an `$0 == "Exclusions:"` rule that prints the following `- ` lines) so it contains only the exclusion text and no pathspec.

findings.title: No test would catch `--only` pathspecs ending up in the Exclusions prose
findings.body: The goal requires that `--only` and `--exclude` stay separate and that the tests fail if this breaks. The change sends both lists through one argument vector: `build_scope` gets `only_count`, then the pathspecs, then the exclusions, and pulls the pathspecs off with `shift` (executable_revmux-round.sh:89-93, 376-384). No test passes `--only` together with `--exclude`. Test 26 is the only success-path `--only` test, and its awk filter prints only the Scale/Limited lines and the three fenced sections. It drops everything after `Changed files:`, including any `Exclusions:` block. Concrete regression: if the shift loop at lines 90-93 is removed or broken, the pathspecs stay in `$@` and the scope prints `Exclusions:\n- app\n- docs/guide.md`. That tells reviewers to skip the very paths the round was limited to. Test 26 would still pass, and tests 1-25 never use `--only`, so `only_count` is 0 there and they cannot see the fault either.
findings.fix: Add `--exclude 'some prose'` to the test 26 call, or write a small companion test with both flags. Assert the exact `Exclusions:` block (only the exclusion text, no pathspecs) next to the `Limited to:` line. Show the test going red with the shift loop removed.

findings.title: The new `--only` guidance contradicts SKILL.md's rule that every later round covers the full cumulative scope
findings.body: SKILL.md:23 says: "Every later round covers this same cumulative scope plus its fixes, against the same base." Step 5 rule 3 lets a round finish the loop when "this complete round needs no further eligible fixes". The new sentence at lines 102-103 lets the agent running follow-up rounds narrow a round to part of the change "when the follow-up targets only part of the cumulative change". It gives no test for when that holds and does not reconcile with line 23 or the finish rule. Compare the profile-narrowing policy just above (lines 72-82): it gates narrowing ("If the boundary is uncertain, retain the broader coverage", "A partial or failed review cannot justify narrowing") and requires the reduced coverage to be reported. SKILL.md is a contract that an agent executes. An agent following it can narrow with `--only`, get a clean round, and finish under rule 3 as if the whole cumulative scope had been confirmed. The final report would not say that unselected paths went unreviewed in that round.
findings.fix: Next to the `--only` sentence, say when narrowing is allowed (for example, the fixes since the previous round touched only those paths and that round was complete). Say that a limited round counts as complete only for its selected paths. Require the final report to state the limit. Also update line 23 to name `--only` as the one exception.

findings.title: Pathspec-suffix code is duplicated in `build_scope` and across three if/else pairs in `next`
findings.body:
`build_scope` repeats the same block for the `git diff` and `git log` read commands: an `only_count > 0` check, `printf ' --'`, then a `%q` loop (lines 110-117 and 118-125).

In `next`, the `--shortstat`, `log --oneline` and `--name-status` calls are each split into an if/else that differs only by `-- "${only_values[@]}"` (lines 347-360). The branching avoids expanding an empty array under `set -u` in Bash 3.2. An array that always starts with `--` is never empty, though, and git accepts a bare `--` with no paths.

As written, a fourth git fact means copying the branch again, which risks breaking the rule that every git fact takes the same pathspec list.
findings.fix: Build `pathspec_args=(--)`, append `only_values`, and call git with `"${pathspec_args[@]}"` without branching. In `build_scope`, compute the quoted read-path suffix once and print it after both read commands.

findings.title: Nothing tests the shell quoting of pathspecs in the scope.md read commands
findings.body: `build_scope` writes the reviewer read commands with `printf ' %q'` (executable_revmux-round.sh:113-123). That quoting is what keeps the commands runnable when a pathspec holds glob or magic characters. Test 026 only passes plain pathspecs (`app`, `docs/guide.md`), which come out the same under `%q` and `%s`. If the code later switched to `%s`, or dropped the quoting some other way, every test would still pass. Yet the scope for `--only ':(exclude)alpha.txt'` would then contain `git diff <base>..HEAD -- :(exclude)alpha.txt`, which bash rejects with a syntax error near `(` (I reproduced this with /bin/bash -n). A `docs/*.md` pathspec would also be expanded by the reviewer's shell instead of reaching git. Reviewers are told to run this command themselves, so they would get a broken or wrong diff. Test 028 already uses `:(exclude)alpha.txt`, but only on the rejection path, which never writes a scope.
findings.fix: In test 026, add a pathspec with a shell metacharacter (e.g. `--only 'app/*.txt'` or a `:(exclude)` magic that still matches) and assert that the expected `git diff`/`git log` lines contain the `%q`-escaped form.

findings.title: SKILL.md never says an --only round leaves the rest of the change unreviewed
findings.body: The new sentence says when to add `--only` ("when the follow-up targets only part of the cumulative change"). It doesn't tell the agent running the loop what that does to coverage. The profile-narrowing policy just above (lines 78-83) requires the agent to report coverage explicitly and says an omitted finding is not thereby resolved. That rule is written only for `final` profiles. A round limited with `--only` re-reviews only the chosen paths, but nothing in this agent-executed contract stops the agent from treating a clean `--only` round as convergence for the whole change. SKILL.md also doesn't say that pathspecs are resolved against `--workdir`, or that a pathspec matching nothing makes `next` fail. The agent learns those only from the error message.
findings.fix: Add a clause after the `--only` sentence saying that a limited round's coverage is only those paths: report it that way, and don't claim convergence for paths it left out. Optionally also note that each pathspec must match a change in base..HEAD.

findings.title: No test passes `--only` with `--exclude`, and test 026's awk filter discards the Exclusions section
findings.body:
The goal requires that `--only` and `--exclude` stay separate and that a test fails if this regresses.

`next` passes both lists to `build_scope` in one argument vector: `only_count`, then the pathspecs, then the exclusions (executable_revmux-round.sh:376-384). `build_scope` shifts the pathspecs off and treats the rest as exclusions (lines 89-93, 128-133).

No test passes both options. Tests 026-028 use only `--only`, and test 015 uses only `--exclude`. Test 026's awk projection prints only the Scale/Limited-to lines and the fenced Read/Commits/Changed-files blocks, so it drops the `Exclusions:` block.

Any of these regressions keeps the whole suite green:
- The shift loop breaks, and the pathspecs appear as `- app` bullets under `Exclusions:`, telling reviewers to skip the very paths they were asked to review.
- The append loops are swapped, and exclusion prose lands in the `git diff … --` read commands.
- The exclusions are lost whenever `--only` is present.

This is the normal invocation, not a corner case: the SKILL.md command template always includes `--exclude`, and the new sentence adds `--only` on top of it.
findings.fix: Add `--exclude 'some prose'` to the test 026 call, or add a companion test with both flags. Assert the exact `Exclusions:` block: it should contain only the exclusion text and no pathspec. Keep asserting that the git facts are limited to the `--only` pathspecs.

findings.title: No test passes --only together with --exclude, and test 26's awk filter discards the Exclusions section
findings.body:
The goal says the change is correct only if `--only` and `--exclude` stay separate and the tests would fail if that regressed. Nothing in the suite checks this.

What I observed:
- No test passes both options. The `--only` tests (026–028) pass no `--exclude`, and the exclusion test (015, around line 363) passes no `--only`.
- Test 026 builds its expected output from an awk filter. The filter prints only the `Scale:`/`Limited to:` lines and the three fenced blocks (read commands, commits, changed files). It never prints the `Exclusions:` section.

What follows from reading the code (I did not run it):
- `next` builds the call as `[..., only_count, <pathspecs...>, <exclusions...>]` (executable_revmux-round.sh:376-384). `build_scope` takes the first `only_count` values as pathspecs and treats the rest of `"$@"` as exclusions (lines 89-93, 128-133).
- Suppose the two append loops at 378-383 were swapped, or `build_scope` stopped shifting the pathspecs off. Exclusion prose would then land in the `git diff … --` / `git log … --` read commands, or the pathspecs would be listed as reviewer exclusions. Every existing test would stay green: none supplies both kinds of argument, and 026's filter would hide pathspecs leaking into `Exclusions:`.
- This is the usual invocation, not a corner case. The SKILL.md command template (lines 96-98) always includes `--exclude`, and the new sentence tells the agent to add `--only` on top of it.

The current code is correct; this is a coverage gap against the goal's own criterion.
findings.fix: Add `--exclude 'defer documentation polish'` to the `run_prepare_only` call in test 026. Also make its awk filter print the `Exclusions:` section, or assert that section separately with an exact match. The test then fails if exclusion text reaches the read commands or a pathspec is listed as an exclusion.

findings.title: Combined --only check runs a second diff whose result line 356 recomputes
findings.body:
Lines 335-344 run `git diff --name-only $base..HEAD -- <all pathspecs>` only to test whether the output is empty. Line 356 then runs `git diff --name-status` over the same range and the same pathspecs to fill `changed_files`. `--name-status` output is empty exactly when `--name-only` output is empty, so the emptiness test could read `changed_files` and skip the extra diff and the `only_match` round-trip.

The only commands between the two sites are read-only (`rev-parse HEAD`, `--shortstat`, `log`), and `revmux new` does not run until line 400. Moving the check therefore keeps the same error text, the same exit status 1, and the same guarantee that no round directory is created.

The one thing lost is the 'cannot evaluate combined --only pathspecs' branch. It can only fire after every pathspec has already been evaluated on its own against the same base and workdir in lines 323-333. In practice it guards a failure that cannot happen there, and errexit, active because `next "$@"` runs at top level, would still stop the script.
findings.fix: Delete lines 335-344. After line 360 add `if [ "$only_count" -gt 0 ] && [ -z "$changed_files" ]; then error "combined --only pathspecs match no changes in $base..HEAD"; return 1; fi`. Test 028 keeps covering it unchanged.

findings.title: post-apply order bumped 27→28 as if it were a test count
findings.body:
`# post-apply: N` is the suite's execution-order key. `tests/run-post-apply.sh` sorts on it numerically and rejects duplicates. It is not a test count: before this change the file had 24 test functions and the header said 27, and now it has 27 functions and says 28.

No other file uses 27 or 28, and the neighbouring orders are 25 and 40, so the bump changes nothing at runtime. It is an edit the change did not need. It also suggests the field is being read as a count; if later test additions keep incrementing it, it will eventually collide with or pass `platform_test.sh`'s 40 and silently reorder or break the post-apply run.
findings.fix: Revert the header to `# post-apply: 27 host-safe`.

findings.title: Have new tests 026-028 been shown to fail on the matching mutation (red/green calibration)?
findings.body:
The review materials include no red/green results for tests 026-028. The repository's mandatory rule in docs/solutions/design-patterns/semantic-regression-tests-over-source-shape.md requires showing that each test is sensitive to the regression it guards. The relevant mutations are:
- 026: remove the scale filtering.
- 027: remove the per-pathspec empty-match check.
- 028: remove the combined empty-match check.

The author can settle this by supplying the failing run on each mutation and the passing run after restoring the code.

findings.title: `--only` guidance has no trigger condition and contradicts the skill's cumulative-scope rule
findings.body:
The new sentence at lines 102-103 tells the agent to add `--only <pathspec>` "when the follow-up targets only part of the cumulative change". Line 23 of the same skill still says "Every later round covers this same cumulative scope plus its fixes, against the same base". An agent executes SKILL.md as its contract, and these two statements give it opposite instructions.

The profile-narrowing policy (lines 72-83) has gates that path narrowing lacks. It says "If the boundary is uncertain, retain the broader coverage" and "A partial or failed review cannot justify narrowing", and it requires reported coverage. Path narrowing gets none of these.

Step 5 rule 3 finishes on "this complete round" (line 212) without saying whether a round limited by `--only` counts as complete. Line 107 carries `--exclude` forward but says nothing about whether `--only` carries forward.

Failure case: the agent runs `next --only app`, gets a clean round, and reports convergence for the whole change. Edits outside `app` since the previous round were never reviewed, and the final report does not state the limit. The skill also does not say that pathspecs resolve against `--workdir`, or that a pathspec matching nothing makes `next` fail.
findings.fix: Put a checkable trigger next to the follow-up profile policy. For example: use `--only` only when every fix since the previous round stays inside the named paths and the previous round was complete; when unsure, keep the full scope. Amend line 23 to name `--only` as the one exception. State that a limited round is complete only for its selected paths and must be reported that way rather than claimed as converged. Say that `--only` is chosen fresh each round rather than carried forward like `--exclude`.

findings.title: Limited scope.md still tells reviewers to "review the cumulative change"
findings.body: `build_scope` writes the reviewer-facing opening sentence unchanged when `--only` is given: "Round %s of task %s: review the cumulative change against base %s, including the fixes since the previous round." It then adds a separate `Limited to: …` line under `Scale:`. scope.md is a prompt every reviewer agent reads. So a limited round gives two conflicting instructions: review the whole cumulative change, and review only these paths. The read commands carry the pathspecs, so most reviewers will follow those. A reviewer who takes the opening sentence literally may still range across the files outside the limit. That re-creates the repeat findings the option exists to prevent (issue #520, "lets the unchanged part of the diff generate repeat findings").
findings.fix: When `only_count > 0`, change the opening sentence to name the limit, e.g. "review the cumulative change against base %s within the pathspecs below", or put the `Limited to:` statement in the opening instruction.

findings.title: Diff strips data-cta/data-cta-section from offer buttons and offerAccepted has no section, because HEAD is an unrelated branch
findings.body: In the scope diff, the gift-ticket link (amazon-scorecard-offer.tsx:194, `<a className='so-gift-go' data-offer-go=''>`) and the store-block/close-band buttons lose the `data-cta='accept-offer' data-cta-section='body'` they carry at base 4bdce06aa7, and the same happens in amazon-checkup-offer.tsx. press() (scorecard :486-496) still builds `{offerKey, company?, amazonStoreKey?}` with no section. The cause is that HEAD 6fbfb05e2f does not descend from the base, so the diff reverts #6813 instead of adding PRD-3672. This is the same root cause as c1bbdb66a508f613c24c0dc24faca9e8.
findings.fix: Review the real prd-3672-offer-page-name tip, built on 4bdce06aa7 or later. On that tip, the buttons need ctaAttrs('accept-offer', 'ticket'|'hero'|'close-band'), and press() needs to put go.dataset.ctaSection into offerAccepted.section.

findings.title: Reviewed HEAD does not contain the PRD-3672 change: offerAccepted carries no `section`, and `ticket` is not a CtaSection
findings.body:
The scope's range 4bdce06aa7..6fbfb05e2f does not match the change it describes. HEAD (6fbfb05e2f) is a four-commit partner-preview branch: bbc3780d79, 97af9240d8, fd74643506 and 6fbfb05e2f. It forked from main at 79810ee497, which is 88 commits behind the stated base. The merge-base diff touches 13 partner-profile files (partner-profile.tsx, PartnerProfileView.tsx, partner-profile-model.ts, use-client-view-tab.ts and others). The scope says 10 files and lists amazon-*-offer.tsx and site.ts; neither is in that diff. The plain two-dot diff runs to 9.6 MB, because it reverses those 88 main commits, #6813's CTA_SECTIONS among them.

The state actually checked out fails every 'Correct only if' criterion:
- In amazon-scorecard-offer.tsx:492-495, `press()` builds `accepted = { offerKey, company?, amazonStoreKey? }` and never reads the pressed button's `data-cta-section`. The same holds in amazon-checkup-offer.tsx at about line 505-508. The gift ticket, store block and closing band therefore send no `section` at all, instead of `ticket` / `hero` / `close-band`.
- `rg CTA_SECTIONS|data-cta-section` finds nothing in console/components/marketing/site.ts or the offer pages on HEAD, so `ticket` is not a CtaSection here.
- No commit on any ref adds `'ticket'` to site.ts (`git log --all -S"'ticket'" -- console/components/marketing/site.ts` is empty).

The '406 tests green / typecheck exit 0' evidence must belong to some other tree, because this one contains neither the code nor the tests it describes. If this HEAD ships as the PRD-3672 PR, `offerAccepted.section` will never reach PostHog, and the SKILL.md / posthog-session-replay.md updates the scope mentions don't exist either.
findings.fix: Re-point the review at the real prd-3672-offer-page-name commit, rebased on 4bdce06aa7 or later, and re-run the scope command against that HEAD before deciding whether it ships.

findings.title: Diff removes ctaClicked handler and CTA attributes, because HEAD does not contain #6813
findings.body: At base 4bdce06aa7, document.tsx:100 defines ctaClickHandler, which captures ctaClicked from [data-cta], and the offer pages tag their buttons with data-cta/data-cta-section. At HEAD 6fbfb05e2f, document.tsx has no ctaClicked, and the offer-page buttons (e.g. amazon-scorecard-offer.tsx:194) have no data-cta. So shipping this range would stop ctaClicked on public pages. The cause is that HEAD is an unrelated partner-preview branch whose merge-base with the base is 79810ee497, so the two-dot diff reverts #6813. This is the same root cause as c1bbdb66a508f613c24c0dc24faca9e8.
findings.fix: Don't ship this range. Review the real PRD-3672 tip, built on a commit that contains #6813.

findings.title: offerAccepted не определяет кнопку, которую нажал посетитель
findings.body: При нажатии любой из трёх кнопок объект accepted содержит offerKey и, при наличии, company и amazonStoreKey, но не содержит section. То же происходит в amazon-checkup-offer.tsx:504. Это существовало до изменения: оба обработчика в исходной ревизии имели такой же payload. В проверяемой ревизии задача по разделению событий на ticket, hero и close-band остаётся невыполненной.
findings.fix: Добавить section в атрибут каждой кнопки и передавать его в offerAccepted из нажатого элемента на обеих страницах.

findings.title: Reviewed HEAD does not contain the PRD-3672 change: offerAccepted has no section, and the diff against base reverts #6813's CTA naming
findings.body:
HEAD 6fbfb05e2f is the tip of an unrelated, older partner-preview branch. It does not descend from the base 4bdce06aa7 (PRD-3663/3666 #6813); the two share the merge-base 79810ee497. Measured from that branch point, the range holds about 13 partner-profile files rather than the 10 offer-page files the scope describes, and the scope's two-dot diff runs to about 9.6 MB of reverted history.

On this HEAD every 'correct only if' condition fails:
(1) `press()` (amazon-scorecard-offer.tsx:491-495, and amazon-checkup-offer.tsx at about line 504-508) builds `{ offerKey, company?, amazonStoreKey? }` with no `section`. It never reads `data-cta-section`, so presses on the gift ticket, store block and closing band cannot be told apart.
(2) site.ts has no `CTA_SECTIONS`, `CtaSection`, `CTA_NAMES` or `ctaAttrs`, so `ticket` is not a valid section.
(3) The diff strips `data-cta`/`data-cta-section` from the GiftTicket, StoreSlot, blocked-notice and close-band elements.
(4) posthog-session-replay.md and the offer-pages SKILL.md don't describe `offerAccepted.section`.
(5) The tests still assert the old payload.

Shipping this range against main would carry none of PRD-3672 and would remove the ctaClicked/bookCallClicked tracking from the public pages. The '406 tests green / typecheck 0' evidence cannot describe the PRD-3672 change.
findings.fix: Point the review at the actual prd-3672-offer-page-name tip, built on a commit that contains #6813 (4bdce06aa7 or later). Re-run the scope diff (three-dot, from the merge-base) and the checks against that commit; do not ship this range.

findings.title: Tests pin an offerAccepted payload with no section
findings.body: The reviewer reports this as pre-existing. The test expects a payload with no section and checks only the first button, and the matching Checkup test does the same. Both pass even though PostHog cannot tell ticket, hero and close-band presses apart, while adding section to the payload would break these expectations.
findings.fix: Assert the exact payload, including the expected section, for each of the three buttons on both pages.

findings.title: Удалены тесты отправки ctaClicked
findings.body: Изменение удаляет тесты обработчика ctaClicked. В том же состоянии обработчик удалён из POSTHOG_SCRIPT, поэтому нажатие на CTA больше не отправляет ctaClicked, а оставшиеся тесты этого не обнаруживают. Это нарушает требование сохранять согласованность ctaClicked с секциями кнопок.
findings.fix: Восстановить проверку события при нажатии на CTA вместе с обработчиком и проверять section в отправленном payload.

findings.title: Reviewed head is a different branch older than base: diff removes CTA naming instead of adding offerAccepted.section/'ticket'
findings.body: Observed: HEAD 6fbfb05e2f (detached; commits are partner-preview work) has merge-base 79810ee497 with the base 4bdce06aa7 (PRD-3663/3666 #6813), so base..HEAD is not the 10-file PRD-3672 change but a ~9.6MB diff that, in the marketing area, reverts #6813. Concretely at HEAD: `CTA_NAMES`, `CTA_SECTIONS`, `CtaSection`, `ctaAttrs` are deleted from console/components/marketing/site.ts; every `data-cta`/`data-cta-section` attribute is stripped from the gift ticket, store block, blocked notice and close band on both amazon-scorecard-offer.tsx and amazon-checkup-offer.tsx; `git grep ctaClicked|bookCallClicked` finds nothing under console/components; the `offerAccepted` payload (amazon-scorecard-offer.tsx:491-495, amazon-checkup-offer.tsx ~508) is still `{offerKey, company?, amazonStoreKey?}` with no `section`; internal-dev-doc/posthog-session-replay.md loses its Public pages section including the offerAccepted bullet. Consequence: none of the goal's correctness criteria hold on the reviewed state (no 'ticket' section, no section on offerAccepted, docs don't describe it), and shipping this tree against main would remove ctaClicked/bookCallClicked tracking from the public pages. The supplied '406 tests green / typecheck 0' evidence was run on this tree, whose offer tests were edited to no longer expect data-cta on the blocked links — a green-while-broken result that says nothing about PRD-3672.
findings.fix: Review/ship the actual prd-3672-offer-page-name head rebased on main at or after 4bdce06aa7; re-run the scope's diff and the checks against that commit.

findings.title: Кнопки offer не передают section в offerAccepted
findings.body: На обеих страницах кнопки ticket и hero потеряли data-cta-section, а обработчики offerAccepted по-прежнему формируют payload без section. Поэтому при нажатии любой из трёх кнопок событие не показывает, какая кнопка была нажата. Отсутствие section в payload существовало до этого изменения; удаление атрибутов также убирает источник значения, предусмотренный целью изменения.
findings.fix: Назначить кнопкам section ticket, hero и close-band и добавить значение нажатой кнопки в payload offerAccepted на обеих страницах.

findings.title: Из загрузчика PostHog удалён обработчик ctaClicked
findings.body: После этого изменения нажатия CTA на публичных страницах больше не отправляют ctaClicked: обработчик удалён, а autocapture выключен. Это затрагивает и обе страницы offer, где требуется сохранить события ctaClicked с разделами ticket, hero и close-band. Ранее эти события отправлялись.
findings.fix: Вернуть обработчик ctaClicked и атрибуты CTA на кнопках публичных страниц.

findings.title: Reviewed state does not contain the PRD-3672 change: offerAccepted still has no section, and the range diffs unrelated history
findings.body: The range in scope.md doesn't match the checkout. HEAD 6fbfb05e2f isn't built on top of the base 4bdce06aa7 (`git merge-base --is-ancestor` exits 1; their common ancestor is 79810ee497). Compared from the branch point, the range holds 13 partner-profile preview files (partner-profile.tsx, use-client-view-tab.ts, PartnerProfileView.tsx…), not the 10 offer-page files the scope describes. The scope's two-dot command produces a ~9.6 MB diff of unrelated history. At HEAD, nothing outside console/public/ mentions CTA_SECTIONS, ctaAttrs or data-cta-section. `press()` here builds `accepted = { offerKey, company?, amazonStoreKey? }` and calls `track('offerAccepted', …)` with no `section`; amazon-checkup-offer.tsx:508 is the same. So none of the goal's correctness conditions (ticket→'ticket', store block→'hero', closing band→'close-band', `ticket` as a valid CtaSection, docs matching) hold or can be checked in this state. The 'already verified' test and typecheck results can't have come from this tree. If this HEAD shipped as PRD-3672, the event would not tell which Start button was pressed. The offer-page change itself wasn't reviewed under simplify, efficiency or test-worth because it isn't present.
findings.fix: Re-run the review with the checkout at the prd-3672-offer-page-name tip and a base that HEAD is built on (for example `git merge-base main HEAD`), using a three-dot diff.

findings.title: Удалены проверки разметки отслеживаемых CTA
findings.body: В diff удалены проверки, которые требовали data-cta и допустимый data-cta-section у отслеживаемых ссылок, а также проверяли идентичность CTA на конкретных страницах. Теперь удаление этих атрибутов с кнопки Accept the offer проходит без этих проверок: именно это произошло с кнопками на обеих страницах offer. Вместе с проверками исчезает защита контракта ctaClicked, а замена, которая его проверяет, в этом diff не показана.
findings.fix: Вернуть проверки разметки CTA и обновить ожидаемые секции кнопок offer на ticket, hero и close-band.

findings.title: Reviewed HEAD does not contain the PRD-3672 change: offerAccepted has no section, CTA_SECTIONS/'ticket' absent
findings.body: The checkout HEAD is 6fbfb05e2f ("fix: remove eager partner preview post"), a partner-preview branch, not prd-3672-offer-page-name. Its merge-base with the scope's base 4bdce06aa7 is 79810ee497, so HEAD is older than the base. The two-dot diff in scope.md therefore shows ~9.6MB of reverted base content instead of the described 10-file change. Here it removes CTA_SECTIONS, CTA_NAMES and ctaAttrs from console/components/marketing/site.ts, and data-cta/data-cta-section from every offer-page button. On HEAD, press() builds `accepted = { offerKey: key }` plus optional company/amazonStoreKey and calls track('offerAccepted', accepted, …) with no `section`. amazon-checkup-offer.tsx (~line 508) is the same. `git log --all -S"'ticket'" -- console/components/marketing/site.ts` returns nothing, so no ref holds the change. Every 'Correct only if' criterion fails on this state: no ticket/hero/close-band section is sent, and 'ticket' is not a CtaSection. The supplied '406 tests green / typecheck 0' evidence describes this state, not the PRD-3672 change. If this state is what opens as the PR, it ships none of PRD-3672 and reverts the PRD-3663/3666 CTA naming.
findings.fix: Re-run the review against the actual prd-3672-offer-page-name commit, with the diff taken from its merge-base with main (or from the true parent of the change).

findings.title: No test combines --only with --exclude, so a mix-up in build_scope's positional argument packing would stay green
findings.body: `next` passes everything to `build_scope` in one positional list: 11 fixed arguments, then `only_count` pathspecs, then the exclusions (script lines 82-93 and 376-384). The `shift 11` and pathspec loop then split that list back apart. Test 026 passes `--only` without `--exclude`, and its awk filter never prints an `Exclusions:` block. Test 015 (around line 355) passes `--exclude` without `--only`, so the pathspec loop never runs there. If the order or the count regressed, pathspecs would land under `Exclusions:` or exclusion prose would land in `Limited to:` and the git commands, and every current test would still pass. Issue #520 says to keep `--only` separate from `--exclude`, but its acceptance criteria only require tests for the narrowed scope and the dead-pathspec error. Both of those are covered, so this is a missing regression guard for a fragile interface, not a missed acceptance criterion. The current code orders the arguments correctly.
findings.fix: Add one prepare-only test, or extend test 026, that passes `--only app --only docs/guide.md --exclude 'defer polish'`. Assert that `Limited to:` and the read commands list only the pathspecs and that the `Exclusions:` block holds only `- defer polish`. Prove it red by swapping the two append loops in `next`.

findings.title: Тесты не проверяют совместное использование --only и --exclude
findings.body: Тест ограниченного раунда передаёт только --only, а тест исключений — только --exclude. Поэтому регрессия, которая удаляет исключения из scope.md только при наличии --only, оставит оба теста зелёными. В таком раунде агенту не передадут указанные ограничения, и он может проверить работу, которую вызывающий исключил. Цель изменения явно требует, чтобы тесты выявляли регрессию разделения этих опций.
findings.fix: Передать --exclude вместе с --only в тест ограниченного раунда и проверить секцию исключений в полученном scope.md.

findings.title: `--only` guidance contradicts the step-1 rule that every later round covers the same cumulative scope
findings.body: Step 1 (SKILL.md:23-24) still says: "Every later round covers this same cumulative scope plus its fixes, against the same base." The new step-2 text (lines 102-103) tells the agent to narrow a follow-up round to `--only <pathspec>` whenever it "targets only part of the cumulative change". It neither amends nor qualifies line 23. That reopens a rule SKILL.md had already settled, and it does so silently. The skill also handles the other kind of narrowing, `final`, carefully (lines 76-83): it gives the conditions under which narrowing is allowed, says a partial review cannot justify narrowing, and requires the agent to "Report the resulting coverage explicitly". The `--only` route has none of that. Step 5 rule 3 (line 212) then finishes the loop on "this complete round". So an agent reading the skill as its contract gets two conflicting instructions. It might never use `--only` because of line 23. Or it might end the loop and report convergence on a round limited to some paths, without saying that the last round covered only those paths. Since this is prose for an agent rather than code, the impact is limited, so I rated it minor.
findings.fix: Qualify line 23 so it allows path-limited follow-up rounds. In the `--only` sentence, state when narrowing is allowed (for example: every path the fixes touched is selected) and require the final report to name the paths the last round was limited to, as the `final` profile rules do.

findings.title: Pathspec handling is duplicated across --only/no-`--only` branches, and the combined check repeats the changed-files query
findings.body:
`next()` writes `git diff --shortstat`, `git log --oneline` and `git diff --name-status` twice each (lines 347-360). The two copies differ only by `-- "${only_values[@]}"`. `build_scope` repeats the same `printf ' --'` / `printf ' %q'` loop for both read commands (lines 110-116 and 118-124). Separately, the combined-selection check (lines 335-344) runs the same filtered diff that `changed_files` computes at line 356 just afterwards.

The main invariant is that every git fact uses the same pathspec list. With this many copies, any later edit (quoting, a new fact) has to be made in several places, and the invariant depends on nobody missing one. A trailing `--` with no paths means 'no pathspec' to both `git diff` and `git log`, so a single form gives the same output with and without `--only`.
findings.fix: In next(), build `pathspec_args=(--)` and append each only value, or use `-- ${only_values[@]+"${only_values[@]}"}`, which is safe under Bash 3.2 with `set -u`. Use it once in the shortstat, log and name-status calls. Turn the combined check into an emptiness test on `changed_files`. In build_scope, build the ` -- %q...` suffix once and append it to both read commands.

findings.title: Противоречивые правила охвата повторного ревью
findings.body: Новое правило разрешает ограничить повторный раунд частью изменений, но строка 23 того же файла требует, чтобы каждый последующий раунд охватывал весь первоначальный набор изменений и исправления. При запросе на частичное ревью агент получает две несовместимые инструкции: он может проигнорировать `--only` или сузить раунд вопреки правилу полного охвата.
findings.fix: Уточнить правило на строке 23 и указать, когда частичный повторный раунд допустим и как его охват влияет на завершение ревью.

findings.title: `--only` guidance contradicts SKILL.md's rule that every later round covers the full cumulative scope, and the finish rule doesn't say how a limited round counts
findings.body:
Step 1 (lines 23-24) says: "Every later round covers this same cumulative scope plus its fixes, against the same base". The new text at lines 102-103 says: "When the follow-up targets only part of the cumulative change, add one repeatable `--only <pathspec>` per part to review." The same change also leaves step 5 as it was: rule 1 stops as blocked when "coverage is incomplete", and rule 3 finishes on "this complete round needs no further eligible fixes". Neither rule says whether a path-limited round counts as complete coverage.

This SKILL.md is the contract the orchestrating agent follows. An agent can run a follow-up round with `--only app`, get no findings, and finish the loop under rule 3, reporting the cumulative review as converged. Paths outside the pathspecs, including any that still have open findings, were never re-reviewed. Or the agent can read step 1 as forbidding `--only` altogether. Either way, the new option has no rule for when it is allowed or what a limited round proves.

The profile-narrowing paragraph (lines 80-83) handles the same situation for `final`: "a finding omitted by the narrower profile is not thereby resolved. Report the resulting coverage explicitly". `--only` gets no equivalent sentence.
findings.fix: Amend step 1's "every later round" sentence to allow a path-limited follow-up. At lines 102-103, state that a limited round covers only the selected paths: carry unresolved findings outside them forward, report the limited coverage, and don't treat the limited round alone as the complete round step 5 rule 3 needs to finish.

findings.title: No test combines `--only` with `--exclude`, so mixing the two up in scope.md would pass
findings.body:
The goal says `--only` and `--exclude` must stay separate, and that the tests must fail if that regresses. Both reach `build_scope` through one positional list, built in this order: `only_count`, then the pathspecs, then the exclusions (script lines 376-384, consumed at lines 82-93 and 128-133). Correct output depends entirely on that order and on the count.

Test 026 passes `--only` without `--exclude`. Its awk filter also drops everything after the `Changed files` fence, so the `Exclusions:` section is never checked. Test 015 checks exclusions without `--only`.

Take a regression that appends the exclusions before the pathspecs in `next`, or miscounts `only_count`. With both flags given, `Limited to:` and the `git diff -- …` read commands would then carry exclusion prose. The pathspecs would show up as `- app` bullets under `Exclusions:`, telling reviewers to skip the very paths the round is limited to. Every current test would stay green.
