findings.fix: Extend test 026, or add one prepare-only test beside it, that passes `--only app --only docs/guide.md --exclude 'defer polish'`. Assert the exact scope.md, including the `Limited to:` line, the read commands, and an `Exclusions:` section listing only `defer polish`.

findings.title: Shell quoting of pathspecs in the read commands is untested; the success-path test uses only plain paths
findings.body:
`build_scope` prints each pathspec in the read commands with `printf ' %q'` (script lines 114 and 122), so reviewers can paste `git diff <base>..HEAD -- …` straight into a shell. The only success-path test, 026, uses `app` and `docs/guide.md`. `%q` and `%s` print those identically.

Such pathspecs are realistic: test 028 itself uses `:(exclude)alpha.txt`, but only on the rejection path, and globs like `missing/**/*.md` or paths with spaces are also plausible. If `%q` were changed to `%s`, scope.md would print `git diff <base>..HEAD -- :(exclude)alpha.txt`. Pasted into bash that is a syntax error at `(`. A path with a space would split into two pathspecs, and a glob would expand against the working tree. The reviewer's read command would then no longer match the git facts in the scope, and no test would fail.
findings.fix: In test 026, or the combined `--only`/`--exclude` test, add a successful pathspec with shell metacharacters, such as `':(glob)app/*.txt'` or a path containing a space. Assert the read-command lines in their `%q`-escaped form, and check that the escaped command, evaluated with `eval` in the fixture repo, lists the same files.

findings.title: `--only` guidance contradicts the rule that every later round covers the same cumulative scope, and the finish rule doesn't say how a limited round counts
findings.body:
Step 1 (lines 23-24) still says: "Every later round covers this same cumulative scope plus its fixes, against the same base." The new text at lines 102-103 says: "When the follow-up targets only part of the cumulative change, add one repeatable `--only <pathspec>` per part to review." Line 23 is not amended or qualified.

Step 5 is also unchanged. Rule 1 stops as blocked when "coverage is incomplete", and rule 3 finishes on "this complete round needs no further eligible fixes". Neither rule says whether a round limited to some paths counts as complete coverage. The carry-forward sentence (lines 106-107) carries the goal and every `--exclude` into the next round, but not the path limit.

The trigger is also ambiguous. Reading (a): the step-1 scope was itself a path subset, so every follow-up should repeat the same `--only` set. Without a carry-forward instruction, round 3 silently widens back to the whole diff. Reading (b): one follow-up may be narrowed to the files the fixes touched. That contradicts line 23, and it lets step 5 finish after a round that never re-reviewed fixes or open findings outside the chosen paths.

The `final` profile narrowing (lines 76-83) states when narrowing is allowed and requires the agent to "Report the resulting coverage explicitly". `--only` has no equivalent rule. An agent following this skill can avoid `--only` altogether because of line 23, or it can report convergence based on a path-limited round.
findings.fix: Qualify step 1's "every later round" sentence so it allows path-limited follow-ups. At lines 102-103, name the case that triggers `--only`. If a recorded path limit applies, add it to the carry-forward sentence at line 106. State that a limited round covers only the selected paths: carry unresolved findings outside them forward, report the limited coverage, and do not treat the limited round alone as the complete round that step 5 rule 3 needs to finish.

findings.title: Тесты не проверяют совместное применение --only и --exclude
findings.body: Новые тесты вызывают --only без --exclude, а существующий тест исключений вызывает --exclude без --only. Поэтому регрессия, при которой текст --exclude передаётся в Git как pathspec или исчезает из раздела Exclusions при использовании --only, останется незамеченной. Это нарушит заданный контракт: фильтр выбирает файлы, а исключение остаётся текстом для ревьюеров.
findings.fix: Дополнить тест вызовом с обоими параметрами и проверить выбранные Git-данные и отдельный раздел Exclusions.

findings.title: No test combines --only with --exclude, so the positional split in build_scope's argument list can regress unnoticed
findings.body:
`build_scope` gets one positional list: 11 fixed arguments, then `only_count` pathspecs, then the exclusions (script lines 82-93 and 376-384). Its `shift` loop decides which values become pathspecs and which become reviewer exclusions. The goal says `--only` and `--exclude` must stay separate and that the tests must fail if that regresses. No test passes both options together.

What I traced: test 026 uses `--only` without `--exclude`. The exclusion test near line 363 uses `--exclude` without `--only`. Test 026's awk filter prints only the Scale/Limited-to lines and the three fenced sections, and drops everything after the Changed files fence, including any `Exclusions:` block.

Two regressions every current test would miss:

- **Shift loop removed in `build_scope`:** the pathspecs fall through to `"$@"` and appear under `Exclusions:` as `- app` and `- docs/guide.md`. Test 026 still passes because awk never prints that block.
- **`next()` appends exclusions before the pathspecs:** with `--only app --exclude 'do not review generated files'`, the scope would say `Limited to: do not review generated files`. Its read commands would become `git diff base..HEAD -- do\ not\ review\ generated\ files`, and `app` would be listed as an exclusion.

What would follow (inferred, not run): reviewers would be told to skip exactly the paths the round is limited to, or would be handed read commands that select nothing. The current code orders the arguments correctly, so this is a coverage gap, not a defect today.
findings.fix: In test 026, or a sibling test, add `--exclude 'some exclusion'` next to the two `--only` flags. Assert the whole scope file, or at least the `Exclusions:` block, so the exclusion appears there and the pathspecs appear only on the `Limited to:` line and in the read commands.

findings.title: The per-pathspec check accepts an exclude-only pathspec that matches no changed file
findings.body: When `--only ':(exclude)missing.txt'` is checked on its own, git applies the exclusion to every changed file because no positive pathspec is present. The check therefore returns a non-empty list even when `missing.txt` is not among the changes. If a valid `--only app` is passed too, the combined-selection check also passes, and the round is created with an exclusion that matches nothing. That breaks the requirement to reject every pathspec that matches no change.

findings.title: No test fails if --only pathspecs leak into the Exclusions section
findings.body:
The goal requires that `--only` and `--exclude` stay separate and that the tests fail if that regresses. Nothing pins it. Test 026 runs `--only` without `--exclude`. Its awk filter prints only the Scale/Limited-to lines and the Read/Commits/Changed-files fences. After the Changed-files fence closes it sets `section = 0`, so an `Exclusions:` block that follows is silently dropped. Test 015 checks the full Exclusions rendering, but only with `only_count=0`. One edit that turns nothing red: in `build_scope` (executable_revmux-round.sh:89-93), copy the pathspecs without shifting them off (e.g. `only_values=("${@:1:$only_count}")`). The same happens if `next` also appends `--only` values to `exclude_values`. Either way, scope.md gains `Exclusions:

- app
- docs/guide.md` and tells reviewers to skip exactly the paths the round is limited to. Tests 015 and 026–028 all stay green. The production code is correct today; the gap is the missing regression guard the goal asks for.
findings.fix: In test 026, add an `--exclude 'some prose'` and compare the whole scope.md exactly (as test 015 does with `expected_scope`), or keep the awk filter but also print the Exclusions section. Then the expected output shows the pathspecs only under `Limited to:` and the read commands, with only the prose under `Exclusions:`.

findings.title: Pathspec list is rendered and passed through five duplicated branches instead of once
findings.body: `build_scope` has two identical `if only_count > 0; printf ' --'; for … printf ' %q'` blocks, one for the `git diff` read command and one for `git log` (110-116, 118-124). `next` also has two `if only_count > 0 … else …` pairs (347-351, 354-360) that differ only in the trailing `-- "${only_values[@]}"`. The goal's main invariant is that every git fact takes the same pathspec list. Five copies of that list are five places where a later edit (quoting, a new fact) can drift. Equivalent forms: (1) in `build_scope`, build the suffix once, e.g. `pathspec_suffix="$(printf ' %q' "${only_values[@]}")"` prefixed with ` --` under the existing guard, and append it to both read commands. (2) In `next`, use `-- ${only_values[@]+"${only_values[@]}"}`. This is the Bash 3.2 / `set -u`-safe empty-array idiom already used in tests/lib/bashunit:1742,4765. A trailing `--` with no paths means 'no pathspec' to both `git diff` and `git log`, so output is the same with and without `--only`. That removes the duplicated branches without changing output, errors, or ordering.
findings.fix: Compute the ` -- <quoted pathspecs>` suffix once in build_scope and reuse it for both read commands. In next(), replace the if/else pairs with a single call ending in `-- ${only_values[@]+"${only_values[@]}"}`.

findings.title: Were the three new tests shown to fail under their target regressions?
findings.body: No results were provided showing that the three new tests fail under the regressions they are meant to catch: removing the pathspec filter, removing the separate check of each pathspec, and removing the combined-selection check. Their sensitivity is therefore unconfirmed. Evidence of a red run under each regression, followed by a green run on the fixed code, would settle this.

findings.title: `--only` trigger is ambiguous and conflicts with the skill's own rule that every later round covers the same cumulative scope
findings.body:
The new text says: "When the follow-up targets only part of the cumulative change, add one repeatable `--only <pathspec>` per part to review." Two lines in the same skill pull the other way. Step 1 (line 23) says "Every later round covers this same cumulative scope plus its fixes, against the same base". Lines 106-107 list what each round carries forward: "Carry the original goal and every exclusion recorded so far forward; on the revmux route that is one `--exclude` per exclusion". That list leaves out the path limit.

The new sentence also doesn't say what makes a follow-up "target only part" of the change. Two readings fit:
(a) the scope recorded in step 1 was a path subset, so every follow-up should repeat the same `--only` set;
(b) the caller can narrow a single follow-up to the files the fixes touched.

Reading (a) needs an instruction to repeat the `--only` set each round, and that instruction is missing. Without it, round 3 silently widens back to the whole diff. Reading (b) contradicts line 23. It also lets step 5 "finish" after a round that never re-reviewed fixes landing outside the chosen paths, which the skill's convergence claim doesn't allow for (compare line 78: "A partial or failed review cannot justify narrowing").

An agent following this text can pick either reading, so runs diverge. Either a round is narrowed without the skill allowing it, or a path-limited scope is dropped between rounds. The text also doesn't mention that the script rejects a pathspec that matches no change, or a combined set that matches nothing. A caller can still find that out from the error message.
findings.fix: Name the single branch that triggers `--only`, e.g. "When the scope recorded in step 1 is limited to paths, pass one `--only <pathspec>` per recorded path on every follow-up round." Add the path limit to the carry-forward sentence at line 106. If narrowing a single round is also meant to be allowed, reconcile that with line 23 and the step 5 finish rule.

findings.title: No safe way to apply the journald cap on the existing server: it only runs as part of a full bootstrap.sh, which the docs say not to re-run
findings.body:
`configure_journald` is only reachable through `main()` in bootstrap.sh, after `create_directories`, `set_permissions`, `configure_firewall` and `configure_smartd`. The function is idempotent on its own: `install -d` plus `cat >` overwrites the file with the same content. But bootstrap.sh as a whole is not safe to re-run on a host where it already ran. `set_permissions` does `chown -R $PUID:$PGID` and `chmod -R 755/775/750` over appdata and every `/mnt/data` user tree. ENVIRONMENT.md:176 says outright «Не «чинить» права запуском `scripts/bootstrap.sh` на заполненном дереве». It also tells the operator to only restart smartd for smartd changes, «**не** прогон `bootstrap.sh` целиком».

The server whose disk is filling has already been bootstrapped, so it stays uncapped until someone runs the whole bootstrap. The new docs make this worse. ENVIRONMENT.md:138 and the new CLAUDE.md block say only that «`bootstrap.sh` создаёт … 90-homelab.conf», with no instruction for an existing host. An agent following CLAUDE.md to apply the cap would run bootstrap.sh and recursively reset ownership and modes on the live data and appdata. Unlike the setup steps (`./scripts/setup/NN-*.sh` «любой шаг установки запускается отдельно»), this step cannot be run on its own. The recursive chown/chmod is pre-existing; the change makes it the only delivery path for this feature.
findings.fix: Move the journald drop-in into its own re-runnable step (e.g. `scripts/setup/NN-configure-journald.sh` sourcing config.sh), or let bootstrap.sh run just that function from an argument. Document in ENVIRONMENT.md/CLAUDE.md how to apply it on the existing host without running bootstrap.sh in full.

findings.title: Doc wrongly says the prune keeps a local copy of the image for rollback
findings.body:
ENVIRONMENT.md:139 says «Удаляются только dangling images; образы остановленных сервисов и локальная копия для отката остаются». Rebuild runs `compose pull` → `down` → `up -d` for each service. When the pull moves the tag, the previous image loses its tag. Once `down`/`up -d` replace the container, nothing references that image, so it is dangling. `docker image prune -f` at rebuild.sh:33 then deletes exactly that previous version. So the previous image of every updated service is removed, which is the opposite of what the line claims. The same happens when `up -d` fails after a successful pull and `down`: the prune still runs (by design) and deletes the only local copy of the old version.

CLAUDE.md tells agents to read ENVIRONMENT.md before disk work, so an agent may plan a rollback around an image that is gone. As written prose, the impact is contained.
findings.fix: Change the sentence to say that tagged images, including those of stopped services, are kept, and that the previous version of each rebuilt service is removed. Rolling back means pulling a pinned tag again.

findings.title: ENVIRONMENT.md says the dangling-image prune keeps the local rollback copy, but that copy is exactly what it deletes
findings.body:
The new line says: «Удаляются только dangling images; образы остановленных сервисов и локальная копия для отката остаются.»

Here is what `do_rebuild` (scripts/docker/_lib.sh:272-274) does for a service on a moving tag such as `:latest`:
1. `compose pull` moves the tag to the new image, so the previous image becomes untagged, i.e. dangling.
2. `down` + `up -d` replaces the container that referenced the old image.
3. The new `docker image prune -f` (rebuild.sh:33) deletes that previous image, because it is now dangling and unused.

So after a rebuild that pulled a new image, no local previous version is left to roll back to. The worst case is a service whose `pull` and `down` succeed but whose `up -d` fails. The prune still runs, by design, and deletes the only local copy of the working old version.

The part about stopped services' images is correct: those stay tagged. The rollback claim is false. CLAUDE.md tells agents to read ENVIRONMENT.md before disk work, so an operator or agent may plan a rollback around an image that is gone. This is a documentation defect only.
findings.fix: Drop «и локальная копия для отката». Say that tagged images, including those of stopped services, are kept, but the previous version of an updated image is removed, so a rollback means pulling a pinned tag again.

findings.title: ENVIRONMENT.md says the local rollback copy of an image survives the dangling prune; it does not
findings.body: The new line says: `docker image prune -f` removes only dangling images, "образы остановленных сервисов и локальная копия для отката остаются" (images of stopped services and the local rollback copy stay). In `do_rebuild` (scripts/docker/_lib.sh:272-274), `pull` moves the tag to the new image. The previous version becomes `<none>:<none>`, which is a dangling image. Once `up -d` recreates the container on the new image, nothing references the old one, so the prune added to rebuild.sh:33 deletes it. A rollback copy is exactly what this prune removes. Nothing in the repo tags or keeps a rollback image (a search for rollback/откат/docker tag finds no such mechanism). The worst case is a service whose pull and down succeed but whose `up -d` fails: the prune still runs and deletes the only local copy of the old image. An operator who trusts this note will believe they can roll back offline when they cannot. This is a prose defect, hence minor.
findings.fix: Drop the "локальная копия для отката остаются" claim. Say instead that the previous image version left untagged by `pull` is deleted, and that a rollback has to re-pull a pinned tag.

findings.title: The disk-space push shows the free-space value without its unit
findings.body: Both new messages render `свободно {{ states('sensor..._disk_free') }}.`. `states()` returns only the bare number. The unit (GiB for the Glances disk_free sensors) is an attribute and is not included. So the push reads e.g. "SSD: занято 87.3%, свободно 12.4." with no unit. The neighbouring alerts in this file write their unit into the template (`°C` at lines 92, 106, 123; `RPM` at 199), and the usage half of these same messages adds `%` by hand. The problem is on both line 64 (SSD) and line 78 (RAID).
findings.fix: Append the unit on both lines, e.g. `{{ states('sensor.127_0_0_1_rootfs_disk_free') }} ГБ`, or use `state_attr(..., 'unit_of_measurement')`.

findings.title: Dashboard comment still says «Три группы» after a fourth group was added
findings.body: The comment just above the cards reads «# Три группы вместо одной плитки glance…». It described the old layout: Диски / Материнка / Вентиляторы. This change adds a fourth group, «Место», so the comment now gives the wrong count. The view header comment (lines 486-493) lists which sensors were added and when, but it does not mention the new rootfs usage sensors.
findings.fix: Change «Три группы» to «Четыре группы» (or drop the count), and note the rootfs usage sensors in the view header comment.

findings.title: config.sh is now sourced twice in bootstrap.sh; the source inside configure_network is dead
findings.body: The change adds `source "$PROJECT_DIR/scripts/lib/config.sh"` at the top level (bootstrap.sh:66) so that `configure_journald` can read `JOURNALD_SYSTEM_MAX_USE`. `configure_network` still sources the same file at line 197. config.sh only assigns and exports constants, and nothing between line 66 and line 197 changes them, so the second source has no effect. It also suggests the function needs its own private load, which is no longer true. The project's existing pattern is one top-level load, as in scripts/setup/06-run-bootstrap.sh:9.
findings.fix: Delete the `source` line inside `configure_network` (bootstrap.sh:197).

findings.title: Очистка не гарантирует сохранение локального образа для отката
findings.body: Новое описание обещает сохранение локальной копии для отката. Однако при обновлении `latest` прежний образ теряет тег, а `do_rebuild` удаляет старый контейнер через `down` (`scripts/docker/_lib.sh:272–274`). Если других ссылок нет, прежний образ становится dangling и удаляется новой очисткой. Это соответствует [документации Docker](https://docs.docker.com/engine/manage-resources/pruning/#prune-images), поэтому оператор не может рассчитывать на описанный локальный откат.
findings.fix: Убрать обещание сохранения копии для отката. Уточнить, что сохраняются образы с тегами или ссылками от существующих контейнеров.

findings.title: The journald cap can only be applied by rerunning the full bootstrap, which the docs forbid on the live server
findings.body:
`configure_journald` is reachable only from `bootstrap.sh`'s `main()`. There is no separate `scripts/setup/NN-*.sh` step for it, and no documented manual command. The server is already set up, so the only way to get the drop-in onto it is to rerun `bootstrap.sh`. That also runs `set_permissions`: recursive `chown -R 1000:1000` / `chmod -R 775/750` over `/mnt/data/public`, `users`, `backups` and appdata. ENVIRONMENT.md:176 forbids exactly this ("Не «чинить» права запуском `scripts/bootstrap.sh` на заполненном дереве"), and KTD6 in the RAID plan calls it irreversible.

The new docs say only "`bootstrap.sh` создаёт `/etc/systemd/journald.conf.d/90-homelab.conf`… и перезапускает `systemd-journald`" (ENVIRONMENT.md:138; same claim in CLAUDE.md:70). Meanwhile CLAUDE.md tells agents "любой шаг установки запускается отдельно". So either the cap never reaches the existing host, or an operator or agent applies it by running bootstrap and rewrites permissions on the whole data tree. The smartd section (ENVIRONMENT.md:163) shows the precedent for this situation: it documents the manual command and says not to run the whole of `bootstrap.sh`.
findings.fix: Document the manual application for an existing host in ENVIRONMENT.md/CLAUDE.md and repeat the warning against running the full bootstrap: write the two-line drop-in with `SystemMaxUse=$JOURNALD_SYSTEM_MAX_USE`, then `sudo systemctl restart systemd-journald`. Alternatively, move the step into its own standalone setup script.

findings.title: Claim that prune keeps the "local copy for rollback" is false: the previous image is the one that gets pruned
findings.body:
The doc says: "Удаляются только dangling images; образы остановленных сервисов и локальная копия для отката остаются." Services track reused tags such as `:latest`. When `do_rebuild` pulls a new image, the previous image loses its tag and becomes dangling. After `down`/`up -d` no container references it, so the `docker image prune -f` that `rebuild.sh` now runs deletes it.

This matters most when a service fails. If `up -d` fails after `pull` and `down` succeeded, the old image is dangling and unreferenced, and the prune (which deliberately runs after failures too) removes the only working previous version. The doc tells the operator a rollback copy survives; it does not.
findings.fix: Drop the rollback clause, or state that the previous version of a re-tagged image becomes dangling and is removed by the prune.

findings.title: View comment still says «Три группы» after a fourth group was added
findings.body: The comment directly above the cards reads "# Три группы вместо одной плитки glance…". This change adds a fourth separator group, «Место», ahead of «Диски», «Материнка» and «Вентиляторы». The comment now describes the old layout. The view header comment (lines 486–493) also lists which sensors were added and when, but does not mention the new rootfs usage sensors.
findings.fix: Change to «Четыре группы» (or drop the count), and note the rootfs usage sensors in the view header comment.

findings.title: No test covers a prune failure combined with a service failure, so a forced success exit would go unnoticed
findings.body: The goal requires that "a prune failure is a warning that leaves the exit status as the services set it". The only prune-failure test runs with all services succeeding and asserts status 0. Suppose the warn branch in `rebuild.sh` were changed to `exit 0` or to reset `failed=()`. That test would still pass, and the existing service-failure test would too, because there the prune succeeds. Yet a run where service `b` fails and the prune also fails would then report success. Nothing would catch that regression.
findings.fix: Add a case with `FAKE_DOCKER_FAIL_PULL_SERVICE=b` and `FAKE_DOCKER_FAIL_PRUNE=1` that asserts exit status 1, exactly one `image prune -f`, and the `[!]` warning.

findings.title: Disk-space push prints free space with no unit
findings.body: Both new messages render `свободно {{ states('sensor.…_disk_free') }}.`, which gives text like "свободно 12.4.". The Glances `disk_free` sensor reports in GiB, but `states()` returns only the bare number. The neighbouring alerts in this file all include their units ("°C"), and the usage value here gets "%". The same issue is on line 78 for the RAID alert.
findings.fix: Append the unit, e.g. `{{ states('sensor.127_0_0_1_rootfs_disk_free') }} GiB` (or use `state_attr(..., 'unit_of_measurement')`), on both lines 64 and 78.

findings.title: Очистка не сохраняет локальный образ для отката
findings.body: Новое утверждение «локальная копия для отката остаётся» неверно при обновлении изменяемого тега. В do_rebuild команда pull переносит тег на новый образ, а down удаляет контейнер, который удерживал предыдущий образ. Если других тегов и контейнеров нет, предыдущий образ становится dangling и удаляется последующим docker image prune -f. Оператор не сможет выполнить обещанный локальный откат.
findings.fix: Указать, что предыдущий образ может быть удалён; для сохранения образа для отката нужен отдельный тег.

findings.title: The journald cap can only be applied by running all of bootstrap.sh, and the recursive set_permissions step runs before it
findings.body:
The new `configure_journald` step (defined around lines 414-426) is wired in only as the last step of `main()` in `scripts/bootstrap.sh`. There is no `scripts/setup/NN-*.sh` step for it and no documented manual command. The function itself is idempotent: `install -d` plus `cat >` overwrites the drop-in, then journald restarts. The only way to reach it, though, is a full bootstrap run, and that run is not safe on a host where bootstrap already ran.

The live server was bootstrapped before this change. Getting the cap onto it means rerunning bootstrap.sh in full, and that calls `set_permissions` first (lines 141-165): `chown -R 1000:1000` and `chmod -R 775/750` over `$APPDATA_PATH`, `$DATA_PATH/public`, `$DATA_PATH/users/*` and `$DATA_PATH/backups`. ENVIRONMENT.md:176 forbids exactly this: «Не «чинить» права запуском `scripts/bootstrap.sh` на заполненном дереве». chmod without `X` sets the exec bit on every file, and chown overwrites the `root:root` that Syncthing sets on purpose. A full rerun also redoes the netplan, firewall and docker-user steps first, so under `set -e` any failure in those stops the run before the journald step.

The new docs (ENVIRONMENT.md:138, CLAUDE.md:70) say only that «`bootstrap.sh` создаёт … 90-homelab.conf» and restarts journald. CLAUDE.md also says «любой шаг установки запускается отдельно», but this step cannot run on its own. That leaves two outcomes:
- Nobody reruns bootstrap, and the journal on the live SSD stays uncapped while the docs read as if the cap is in place.
- An operator or agent follows the docs, reruns bootstrap.sh, and permissions under appdata and /mnt/data get rewritten recursively.

The smartd section (ENVIRONMENT.md:163) shows the precedent for this situation: it documents the manual command and says not to run the whole of bootstrap.sh.
findings.fix: Make the journald configuration a standalone, re-runnable step (e.g. `scripts/setup/NN-setup-journald.sh` sourcing config.sh, or a `configure_journald`-only entry point that bootstrap also calls). In ENVIRONMENT.md/CLAUDE.md, document applying it on an existing host without the full bootstrap: write the drop-in with `SystemMaxUse=$JOURNALD_SYSTEM_MAX_USE`, then `sudo systemctl restart systemd-journald`.

findings.title: ENVIRONMENT.md says dangling-image prune keeps the local rollback copy, but that copy is exactly what it deletes
findings.body:
The new line says: "Удаляются только dangling images; образы остановленных сервисов и локальная копия для отката остаются."

Here is what `do_rebuild` does for a service on a moving tag such as `:latest`, which is most of these services (for example glances is `nicolargo/glances:latest-full`):
1. `compose pull` moves the tag to the new image, so the previous image becomes untagged, i.e. dangling.
2. `down` + `up -d` replaces the container that referenced the old image.
3. The new `docker image prune -f` then deletes that previous image, because it is now dangling and unused.

So after any successful rebuild of an updated image, there is no local previous version left to roll back to. This holds for every service that pulled a new image, and also on the failed-service path, which the change deliberately prunes on as well.

The part about images of stopped services is correct: those are still tagged. The rollback-copy claim is false. An operator who trusts it during an incident like the ytpod/yt-dlp breakage will find nothing to roll back to. This is a documentation defect only; the prune behaviour itself is what the goal asks for.
findings.fix: Drop "и локальная копия для отката", or replace it with a note that the previous image of an updated `:latest` service is removed, so to roll back you pin a version tag and pull it again.

findings.title: A disk alert is lost if automations reload during its 10-minute window, or if it is deployed while usage is already above the threshold
findings.body: numeric_state arms an entity at attach time only if the entity is currently below the threshold. So two cases lose the alert. First, an automation reload or HA restart during the 10-minute `for:` window, while usage is already above 85% (SSD, lines 54-59) or 90% (RAID, lines 68-73). Second, deploying these automations when a disk is already over the threshold. In both cases the alert will not fire until the value drops back below the threshold and crosses it again. Two things limit this. First, the entity re-arms whenever the sensor goes unavailable and comes back: a failed numeric check arms it, and the file's server_glances_autoreload notes say that happens after Glances restarts or the server reboots. Second, disk usage changes slowly, and every existing temperature alert in the file uses the same trigger pattern. So the gap is real but narrow, not 'never re-arms'.
findings.fix: Optionally add a `homeassistant: start` / `event: automation_reloaded` trigger with a numeric_state condition (above 85/90), so an exceedance that already exists still produces a push.

findings.title: Документация ошибочно обещает сохранить образ для отката
findings.body: При обновлении изменяемого тега pull переносит тег на новый образ, а down удаляет старый контейнер. Если других ссылок нет, предыдущий образ становится dangling и новый prune удаляет его. Поэтому обещание сохранить локальную копию для отката неверно: откат может потребовать повторного скачивания. Условия удаления подтверждает [документация Docker](https://docs.docker.com/engine/manage-resources/pruning/).
findings.fix: Убрать обещание сохранения копии для отката и указать, что предыдущий образ может быть удалён.

findings.title: config.sh is now sourced twice in bootstrap; the in-function source in configure_network is dead
findings.body: The change adds `source "$PROJECT_DIR/scripts/lib/config.sh"` at the top of bootstrap.sh (line 66) so that configure_journald can read JOURNALD_SYSTEM_MAX_USE. configure_network still sources the same file again at line 197. config.sh only assigns and exports constants (GITHUB_*, INSTALL_PATH, HOSTNAME, TIMEZONE, NET_*, TS_*, IT87_*, APT/CARGO arrays, `USER=${USER:-...}`). Nothing between line 66 and line 197 changes any of them, so the second source re-assigns the same values and has no effect. That leaves two places that load the same configuration, and a reader can't tell which one configure_network depends on.
findings.fix: Delete `source "$PROJECT_DIR/scripts/lib/config.sh"` at line 197 inside configure_network, since the top-level source already provides NET_IP/NET_INTERFACE_MATCH/etc. Or drop the new top-level source and source config.sh inside configure_journald, as configure_network already does.

findings.title: New CLAUDE.md block and rebuild comment are in English inside a Russian instruction file
findings.body: Every other block of CLAUDE.md is in Russian, apart from the boilerplate `## Agent skills` section. The new block (lines 70–72, e.g. "`rebuild.sh` prunes dangling Docker images after all requested services, including a run where a service failed") and the edited comment on line 61 ("pull + restart, then prune dangling images", next to "остановка", "деплой") are in English. The mismatch changes no agent behaviour, but it breaks the file's convention, and the ENVIRONMENT.md version of the same facts was written in Russian.
findings.fix: Translate lines 61 and 70–72 into Russian so they match the surrounding blocks and ENVIRONMENT.md «Контроль свободного места».

findings.title: Prune behaviour of rebuild.sh is stated twice in CLAUDE.md
findings.body: Line 61 ("`rebuild.sh svc1  # pull + restart, then prune dangling images`") and line 71 ("`rebuild.sh` prunes dangling Docker images after all requested services…") both describe the same behaviour, in two conditional blocks. That makes two sources of truth, and a later change to the prune (for example adding a filter) has to be edited in both places. Line 71 adds the useful facts (it prunes after a failure, never `-a`), so line 61's addition is the redundant one.
findings.fix: Revert line 61 to `# pull + restart` and keep the full statement only in the disk-space block, or replace the line-71 bullet with a one-line pointer.

findings.title: Disk-alert bullet drops the 10-minute duration and the reason for avoiding snap_* sensors, with no pointer to ENVIRONMENT.md
findings.body: Line 72 says "Home Assistant alerts on root SSD usage above 85% and RAID `/mnt/data` usage above 90%… use the real rootfs sensors, never `snap_*` sensors." It leaves out the `for: "00:10:00"` condition in hardware_health.yaml, so an agent asked why an alert didn't fire on a short spike has an incomplete contract. It also leaves out why `snap_*` is wrong (loop mounts always read 100%), which is the gotcha an agent can't find by looking. Neighbouring blocks (RAID, SMART, backups) end with a pointer to the matching ENVIRONMENT.md section, and this one does not point to «Контроль свободного места», where both facts already live.
findings.fix: Add "for 10 minutes" and a pointer: "Подробности — `ENVIRONMENT.md` → «Контроль свободного места»" (or a short "loop mounts are always 100%" clause).

findings.title: ENVIRONMENT.md claims the rollback copy survives the prune, but dangling-image prune deletes exactly the pre-pull image
findings.body: The new line says `docker image prune -f` removes only dangling images and that «локальная копия для отката остаются». In do_rebuild the order is pull → down → up -d. `compose pull` moves the tag to the new image, so the previous image becomes `<none>:<none>`. After `up -d` the recreated container uses the new image, so the old one is dangling and unused, and the prune that now runs at the end of every rebuild deletes it. The local copy you would roll back to is exactly what gets removed. The goal requires the docs to say what the scripts do; an operator relying on this sentence after a bad update would find no local image to roll back to and would have to re-pull an older tag. Only the prose is wrong; the script behaves as the goal intends.
findings.fix: Drop the rollback-copy clause, or say that the previous version of a rebuilt image is removed after a successful rebuild and a rollback needs a re-pull by tag or digest.

findings.title: Disk-space alerts fire only on crossing; a disk already over threshold (or crossing while Glances is unavailable) never alerts
findings.body: Both new automations use a `numeric_state` trigger with `above: 85` / `above: 90`. HA arms this trigger only after it has seen the value outside the range, so it fires on a transition, not on a sustained state. Disk usage rarely goes back down, so this matters here. Concrete case: if the RAID is already at 92% when this package is deployed, or when HA restarts, the automation never fires until usage drops below 90 and climbs again. The goal is "sends an alert when the root disk or the data disk stays above its threshold". The same applies if the crossing happens while the Glances sensors are unavailable; the file itself documents that this happens after reboots and Glances restarts. I did not confirm HA's arming behavior for unavailable sensors. The existing temperature alerts share this pattern, but temperatures oscillate and usage does not.
findings.fix: Add a periodic re-check, e.g. a `time_pattern` trigger plus a `numeric_state` condition with above: 85/90, and keep `mode: single`, or add a `homeassistant: start` trigger with the same condition, so an already-full disk still produces a push.

findings.title: Disk-space push messages print the free-space value with no unit
findings.body: Both new messages render `свободно {{ states('sensor.…_disk_free') }}.` (line 64 for rootfs, line 78 for RAID). `states()` returns only the number. The unit (GiB from Glances) is in the `unit_of_measurement` attribute. The push reads like «SSD: занято 87.1%, свободно 31.4.», and the reader cannot tell GiB from GB or percent. Every other message in this file adds its unit by hand (`°C`, `%`). Only the free-space value has none.
findings.fix: Append the unit: `{{ states('sensor.127_0_0_1_rootfs_disk_free') }} {{ state_attr('sensor.127_0_0_1_rootfs_disk_free', 'unit_of_measurement') }}` (same for the RAID sensor), or hard-code ` GiB`/` ГиБ`.

findings.title: Disk-space alerts need a below-threshold reading first: a disk already over the threshold at deploy or reload, or a reload during the 10-minute `for:`, never alerts
findings.body: Both new automations (lines 55–59 for SSD, 69–73 for RAID) use a `numeric_state` trigger with `above: 85` / `above: 90` and `for: "00:10:00"`. In HA this trigger is armed only by a reading outside the range. At setup it arms the entity only if the current value is below the threshold. If the disk is already over 85% / 90% when the package is deployed, when automations are reloaded (any UI automation edit does this), or when HA restarts with Glances already up, the trigger never arms and never fires. A reload or restart inside the 10-minute `for:` window also cancels a pending alert, and the trigger then sets up again in the not-armed state. Disk usage rarely drops back down, so in these cases the alert can stay silent indefinitely. An earlier claim that crossings during Glances unavailability are lost is wrong: an armed trigger stays armed through an unavailable state, and that path still fires. The gap is limited to the deploy/reload/restart cases above. The dashboard group still shows the values.
findings.fix: Add a `homeassistant: start` trigger and a periodic `time_pattern` trigger (e.g. `hours: "/1"`, as `server_glances_autoreload` already does with `/10`). Then add a `numeric_state` condition above 85/90 with `for: "00:10:00"`. Keep `mode: single`. This only touches the two new automations.

findings.title: Документация неверно обещает сохранение образа для отката
findings.body: При обновлении тега pull может оставить старый образ без тега. После compose down старый контейнер удаляется, и docker image prune -f может удалить этот dangling-образ. Поэтому локальная копия для отката, которую обещает документация, не обязательно сохранится.
findings.fix: Уточнить, что prune может удалить предыдущий образ, если он больше не имеет тега и не используется контейнером.

findings.title: Doc claims the rollback copy of an image survives the prune; it is exactly what gets pruned
findings.body: The new ENVIRONMENT.md line says that after `rebuild.sh` runs `docker image prune -f`, 'Удаляются только dangling images; образы остановленных сервисов и локальная копия для отката остаются'. But `do_rebuild` (scripts/docker/_lib.sh:272-274) does `pull` → `down` → `up -d`. The pull moves the tag to the new image, so the previous image loses its tag. Once `up -d` recreates the container on the new image, nothing references the old one, so it is dangling, and that is what `docker image prune -f` deletes. After a rebuild, the previous version of a rebuilt service is gone from the host. Anyone reading this (ENVIRONMENT.md is the reference CLAUDE.md tells agents to read first) would expect an older local image to roll back to and would not find one.
findings.fix: Drop 'и локальная копия для отката' or say the reverse: the previous image of every rebuilt service is removed, so rolling back means pulling the old tag again.

findings.title: configure_network still re-sources config.sh, which bootstrap now loads at top level
findings.body: The change adds `source "$PROJECT_DIR/scripts/lib/config.sh"` at the top level of bootstrap.sh (line 66) so that `JOURNALD_SYSTEM_MAX_USE` is defined. `configure_network` still sources the same file again at line 197, and that call is now redundant. Bootstrap does not reassign any config.sh variable between the two. Two load points make it unclear which one matters, and future edits could make them diverge.
findings.fix: Delete the `source "$PROJECT_DIR/scripts/lib/config.sh"` line inside configure_network. The top-level source at line 66 already provides NET_IP, NET_INTERFACE_MATCH and the rest.

findings.title: Disk-space push messages print free space with no unit
findings.body: Both new messages show `свободно {{ states('sensor.127_0_0_1_rootfs_disk_free') }}.` (and the RAID equivalent at line 78). `states()` returns only the number, without the unit Glances attaches (GiB), so the push reads like 'свободно 12.4.' The existing alerts in this same file add the unit after `states()` (e.g. `...temperature') }}°C`), so these two break the file's own pattern and leave the free-space figure ambiguous.
findings.fix: Add the unit, e.g. `свободно {{ states('sensor.127_0_0_1_rootfs_disk_free') }} GiB.`, or use `state_attr(..., 'unit_of_measurement')`.

findings.title: Server view comment still says «Три группы» after a fourth group («Место») was added
findings.body: The comment above the Сервер view's cards reads «Три группы вместо одной плитки glance…». This change adds a new separator/grid group «Место» at the top of that card list, so the view now has four groups: Место, Диски, Материнка, Вентиляторы. The comment no longer matches the code below it.
findings.fix: Change to «Четыре группы…» (or drop the count) and mention that «Место» shows the rootfs disk-usage sensors.

findings.title: Документация обещает сохранить локальный образ для отката
findings.body: При обновлении образа под тем же тегом старый образ может остаться без тега. После удаления старого контейнера в ходе rebuild он становится dangling, и `docker image prune -f` его удаляет. Поэтому локальная копия для отката не всегда сохраняется, хотя документация утверждает обратное.
findings.fix: Уточнить, что старый образ может быть удалён, если он не имеет тега и не используется контейнером.

findings.title: ENVIRONMENT.md claims a local rollback copy survives the prune, but the prune deletes exactly that image
findings.body: The new line says: «Удаляются только dangling images; образы остановленных сервисов и локальная копия для отката остаются.» There is no rollback mechanism anywhere in the repo (no `docker tag`, no retained previous tag; grep for rollback/откат finds nothing in scripts). In `do_rebuild` (`scripts/docker/_lib.sh:272-274`), `pull` moves the tag to the new image, so the previous image becomes untagged `<none>`. `down` and `up -d` then recreate the container on the new image, which leaves the old image dangling. The `docker image prune -f` added at `scripts/docker/rebuild.sh:33` deletes precisely that previous version. After a successful rebuild there is no local copy to roll back to. An operator, or an agent told by CLAUDE.md to read ENVIRONMENT.md first, who counts on rolling back locally after a bad update will find the old image gone. The rest of the line, that tagged images of stopped services remain, is correct.
findings.fix: Replace the rollback clause with the truth: «образы остановленных сервисов остаются; предыдущая версия образа пересобранного сервиса становится dangling и удаляется — откат только через повторный pull конкретного тега».

findings.title: Server view comment still says «Три группы» after the change adds a fourth group
findings.body: The comment directly above the edited cards reads «Три группы вместо одной плитки glance: та выкладывала семь разнородных значений в общую сетку…». This change inserts a new separator group «Место» (line 503-505) at the top of that card list. The view now has four groups (Место, Диски, Материнка, Вентиляторы); before the change there were three. Read side by side, the comment and the new separator contradict each other. The comment is the one that is wrong.
findings.fix: Update the comment to «Четыре группы…» (or drop the count) and mention that «Место» shows the rootfs disk-usage sensors.

findings.title: Disk-space push prints the free-space value with no unit
findings.body: Both new messages render `свободно {{ states('sensor..._disk_free') }}.`. `states()` returns only the bare number; the unit (GiB from the Glances integration) lives in the `unit_of_measurement` attribute. The push therefore reads e.g. «SSD: занято 87.1%, свободно 31.4.», so the reader cannot tell whether it is GiB, GB or percent. Every other message in this file adds its unit by hand (`°C`), and the usage value in the same message adds `%`. Only the free-space value is left without one.
findings.fix: Append the unit: `свободно {{ states('sensor.127_0_0_1_rootfs_disk_free') }} {{ state_attr('sensor.127_0_0_1_rootfs_disk_free', 'unit_of_measurement') }}` (same for the RAID sensor), or hardcode ` ГиБ`.

findings.title: Документация ошибочно обещает сохранить образ для отката
findings.body: После загрузки новой версии по тому же тегу прежний образ может остаться без тега. Когда rebuild удаляет старый контейнер, этот образ становится dangling, и последующий `docker image prune -f` удаляет его. Поэтому локальная копия для отката не всегда остаётся, хотя документ утверждает обратное.
findings.fix: Уточнить, что прежний образ может быть удалён, если у него больше нет тега и контейнеров.

findings.title: Doc says prune keeps the rollback copy, but the pre-pull image of each rebuilt service is exactly what `docker image prune -f` deletes
findings.body: Observed: `do_rebuild` runs `compose pull` (moves the `:latest`-style tag onto the new image, leaving the previous image untagged/dangling), then `compose down` (removes the only container referencing the old image), then `up -d` on the new image. `rebuild.sh:33` then runs `docker image prune -f`, which removes dangling images not referenced by any container — i.e. the previous version of every service that was just rebuilt. The new line in ENVIRONMENT.md states «образы остановленных сервисов и локальная копия для отката остаются», which is false for the rebuilt services (it is true only for tagged images of stopped services). Inferred consequence: an operator or agent reading ENVIRONMENT.md (which CLAUDE.md tells agents to consult) expects to be able to retag/run the previous image after a bad update and finds it gone; this also covers the failed-service path the change deliberately prunes on — a service whose `up -d` fails after a successful pull+down loses its old image in the same run. Prose defect, so minor.
findings.fix: Rewrite the sentence: dangling images, including the previous version of every rebuilt service, are removed; tagged images of stopped services stay. Optionally note that a rollback needs a pinned tag or digest.

findings.title: Disk-space push messages show the free-space value with no unit
findings.body: Both new alerts write `свободно {{ states('sensor..._disk_free') }}.` — `states()` returns only the numeric state, not `unit_of_measurement`. As far as I know (not checked against a live install), the Glances `disk_free` sensor reports in GiB, so the push reads like 'SSD: занято 87.2%, свободно 11.9.' and gives no unit for the number the alert exists to report. The usage part hardcodes `%` and is fine. Contained cosmetic impact on the notification text.
findings.fix: Append the unit, e.g. `{{ states('sensor.127_0_0_1_rootfs_disk_free') }} {{ state_attr('sensor.127_0_0_1_rootfs_disk_free', 'unit_of_measurement') }}` or a literal ` ГБ`.

findings.title: Applying the journald cap on a live server requires rerunning bootstrap, which first re-runs set_permissions on appdata and DATA_PATH
findings.body: On a server where bootstrap has already run, the only way to apply or re-apply the journald limit through this script is to run bootstrap again, and bootstrap calls set_permissions first. That function recursively changes owners and modes in appdata and DATA_PATH. ENVIRONMENT.md warns that this also overwrites Syncthing permissions. The permission step existed before this change, but the new step puts it on the path to configuring journald on a live server.
findings.fix: Make the journald configuration a separate step (for example its own setup/NN-*.sh) that can be rerun without running the rest of bootstrap.

findings.title: Таймер numeric_state не переживает перезапуск Home Assistant
findings.body: Если заполнение диска превысило порог, но Home Assistant перезапустился или автоматизации были перезагружены до истечения 10 минут, ожидающий таймер сбрасывается. Если датчик при загрузке уже показывает значение выше порога, новый переход через порог не происходит, и уведомление не отправится, пока заполнение не опустится ниже порога и снова не превысит его. Та же проблема есть у RAID-уведомления.
findings.fix: Добавить проверку сохраняющегося превышения при запуске и после перезагрузки автоматизаций, используя сохраняемое время или периодическую проверку.

findings.title: Документация обещает сохранить предыдущий образ для отката
findings.body: При обновлении тега `docker compose pull` прежний образ может стать dangling. После `compose down` контейнер, который на него ссылался, удалён, и новый `docker image prune -f` может удалить этот образ. Поэтому утверждение, что локальная копия для отката остаётся, неверно.
findings.fix: Убрать обещание сохранения образа для отката или описать условия, при которых он сохраняется.

findings.title: configure_network still re-sources config.sh now that bootstrap sources it at top level
findings.body: The change adds `source "$PROJECT_DIR/scripts/lib/config.sh"` at top level (line 66) so configure_journald can read JOURNALD_SYSTEM_MAX_USE. configure_network already had its own `source "$PROJECT_DIR/scripts/lib/config.sh"` at line 197, so the script now has two load points for the same config. After the top-level source that second one does nothing: bootstrap never reassigns any config.sh variable (HOSTNAME, NET_*, TS_*, USER, the IT87_* values) between line 66 and configure_network, and re-sourcing config.sh just sets the same values again (`USER=${USER:-...}` keeps what is already set). Pre-existing line, but the change is what makes it redundant. A reader can no longer tell which source is the one that matters.
findings.fix: Delete the `source "$PROJECT_DIR/scripts/lib/config.sh"` line inside configure_network; the top-level source at line 66 already provides NET_IP, NET_INTERFACE_MATCH, etc.

findings.title: ENVIRONMENT.md says the rollback copy survives the prune, but `docker image prune -f` deletes the pre-pull image of every rebuilt service
findings.body: The new line says: «Удаляются только dangling images; образы остановленных сервисов и локальная копия для отката остаются.» `do_rebuild` (scripts/docker/_lib.sh:272-274) runs `pull` → `down` → `up -d`. The pull moves the tag to the new image, so the previous image is left untagged (`<none>:<none>`). Once the container is recreated on the new image, nothing references the old one. It is dangling, and the `docker image prune -f` added at rebuild.sh:33 deletes it. The same happens on the failed-service path, where `up -d` fails after a successful pull and down. Nothing in the repo tags the old image for rollback. After a rebuild there is no local copy to roll back to. CLAUDE.md tells agents to read ENVIRONMENT.md first, so an operator or agent who plans to restart the previous local image after a bad update will find it gone. The claim is also the stated reason the prune is considered safe. The part about tagged images of stopped services staying is correct.
findings.fix: Replace the rollback clause, e.g. «образы остановленных сервисов остаются; предыдущая версия образа пересобранного сервиса становится dangling и удаляется — откат только через повторный pull конкретного тега/digest». Alternatively, tag the old image before pulling if a local rollback copy is actually wanted.

findings.title: ENVIRONMENT.md hard-codes the journal cap value instead of pointing to config.sh
findings.body: ENVIRONMENT.md:138 hard-codes `SystemMaxUse=1G`. CLAUDE.md names `JOURNALD_SYSTEM_MAX_USE` in `scripts/lib/config.sh` as the source of this value, and bootstrap.sh reads it from there. If config.sh changes to 2G and bootstrap is rerun, the host gets 2G while ENVIRONMENT.md still says 1G. The alert thresholds (85%/90%) are likewise restated in CLAUDE.md, ENVIRONMENT.md and hardware_health.yaml.
findings.fix: Write «`SystemMaxUse=$JOURNALD_SYSTEM_MAX_USE` (scripts/lib/config.sh)» rather than the literal 1G. Optionally point the threshold lines at hardware_health.yaml.

findings.title: "use the real rootfs sensors" does not say which entities those are
findings.body: CLAUDE.md:72 says: "use the real rootfs sensors, never `snap_*` sensors." It does not give the entity ids. They appear only in the header comment of `services/homeassistant/config/packages/hardware_health.yaml` (`sensor.127_0_0_1_rootfs_disk_usage`, `sensor.living_room_127_0_0_1_rootfs_mnt_data_disk_usage`), and the RAID one has a non-obvious `living_room_` prefix. An agent editing these alerts or the dashboard has to work out what "real" means, and different runs may pick different sensors. The reason `snap_*` is excluded (loop mounts always read 100%) is only in ENVIRONMENT.md:140, so the ban has no justification next to it.
findings.fix: Point to the source: "entity ids — header of `services/homeassistant/config/packages/hardware_health.yaml`; `snap_*` loop mounts always read 100%."

findings.title: The new block's trigger "Home Assistant hardware alerts" is wider than its content
findings.body: The trigger `<important if="you are working with disk space, journald, or Home Assistant hardware alerts">` also fires for any work on the CPU-temperature, fan and RAID-temperature alerts in hardware_health.yaml. The block itself only covers disk-usage alerts, so those runs load content that does not apply to them. Work on the «Сервер» dashboard's «Место» group, which line 72 describes, does not match the trigger wording at all. The branch is "disk usage alerts/dashboard", not "hardware alerts".
findings.fix: Narrow the trigger to the branch the block handles, e.g. `if="you are working with disk space, journald, or Home Assistant disk-usage alerts or dashboard"`.

findings.title: The `-a` guardrail is stated as a negation without its reason
findings.body: CLAUDE.md:71 says: "It never uses `docker image prune -a`." The real intent is a guardrail: keep the prune to dangling images, because `-a` would delete the images of stopped services. The line states this as a prohibition and leaves the reason in ENVIRONMENT.md. An agent asked to free more disk space sees `prune -a` named in its instructions with no reason given, so it has nothing to weigh against using it.
findings.fix: State the target and the reason: "`rebuild.sh` prunes dangling images only (`docker image prune -f`), so images of stopped services stay available."

findings.title: Summary-bar PDF button lacks busy, failure and disabled-reason feedback, which renders only in the off-screen card
findings.body: The bar is visible only while the header card is out of view, yet all feedback for its 'Скачать PDF' action renders inside the card. That covers the busy label 'Подготовка PDF…', the 'Создаём PDF…' and 'Обрабатываем изображения…' status lines, the failure `message` (e.g. from reportPdfFailure) and `draftError`. The bar's label never changes. Concrete cases: (1) with an invalid copy count, or while images are still processing, the bar button turns disabled and the reason appears only in the hidden card. (2) If generation started from the bar fails, the error goes into the hidden card and the button re-enables with nothing visible. The old sidebar was sticky and kept these messages next to its button, so this gap is new.
findings.fix: Mirror the busy label in the bar (`busy ? 'Подготовка PDF…' : 'Скачать PDF'`, with a matching aria-label). When `message`, `draftError` or `preparing` is set, show a short status line in the bar or point to one with aria-describedby.

findings.title: "Изменить" focuses the field before scrolling, so the smooth / reduced-motion scroll branch is effectively dead
findings.body: The summary bar's edit handler calls `firstField?.focus()` with no `preventScroll` option, then `header?.scrollIntoView({ behavior: shouldAnimate ? 'smooth' : 'auto', block: 'start' })`. `HTMLElement.focus()` scrolls the focused element into view instantly by default, and the project sets no `scroll-behavior` anywhere (`rg scroll-behavior src` finds nothing). Clicking "Изменить" far down the minis list therefore jumps the page to the Формат trigger, and the later smooth `scrollIntoView` only nudges the remaining offset. The `matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference)')` check that chooses smooth or instant scrolling has almost no effect: users always get the jump, never the animated return.
findings.fix: Call `header?.scrollIntoView(...)` first and then `firstField?.focus({ preventScroll: true })`, or keep the current order and pass `{ preventScroll: true }` to `focus()`.

findings.title: Scale popover className adds the dead `minis-scale-popover` class and repeats the primitive's defaults
findings.body: The popover's className includes `minis-scale-popover`, which no CSS rule or test references; a repo-wide search finds only this line. So the class implies styling or a test hook that does not exist. The same className also passes `rounded-lg`, `shadow-md` and `bg-surface-elevated` again, which the new Popover primitive already sets (`--color-popover` resolves to surface-elevated). It adds `border border-border` on top of the primitive's `ring-1 ring-foreground/10`, so the popover ends up with two outlines.
findings.fix: Remove `minis-scale-popover` and cut the className down to what differs from the primitive (the width and `p-4`). Keep either the border or the ring, not both.

findings.title: Accordion primitive left with no callers after the settings sidebar was removed
findings.body: The removed settings sidebar in PaperMinisGenerator was the only consumer of `@/components/ui/accordion`: the base revision imports Accordion, AccordionContent, AccordionItem and AccordionTrigger there. After this change, `rg -n "Accordion|accordion" src --glob '!src/components/ui/accordion.tsx'` returns nothing. The primitive is now dead code in the shared UI folder. It is in-repo only, with no persisted data or external consumer, so removing it is safe unless it is being kept on purpose.
findings.fix: Delete `src/components/ui/accordion.tsx`, or note that it is kept on purpose as part of the primitive set.

findings.title: New Popover primitive splits surface and content unlike the existing dropdown-menu primitive, with mismatched data-slot names
findings.body: `src/components/ui/dropdown-menu.tsx:22-40` puts the React Aria `Popover` and its inner `Menu` in one `DropdownMenuContent`, so callers use a single Content component. The new `popover.tsx` exports `Popover` (the positioned surface) and `PopoverContent` (a `Dialog`) separately, and callers must nest them by hand. The naming is also crossed: `data-slot="popover-content"` sits on the `Popover` surface, while the component named `PopoverContent` gets `data-slot="popover-dialog"`. A later caller or `[data-slot=popover-content]` selector would plausibly target the wrong element.
findings.fix: Follow dropdown-menu: one `PopoverContent` that renders `Popover` + `Dialog` with `data-slot="popover-content"`. At minimum, align the data-slot names with the exported component names.

findings.title: Sticky summary bar uses translucent backdrop blur and a drop shadow, which DESIGN.md forbids, and the DESIGN.md edit in the same change never mentions the bar
findings.body: The new `.minis-summary-bar` styles are `background: color-mix(in oklch, var(--color-surface-elevated) 94%, transparent); box-shadow: 0 0.25rem 1rem oklch(0 0 0 / 8%); backdrop-filter: blur(0.75rem);`. That is a frosted-glass bar with a drop shadow. docs/DESIGN.md:58 forbids glass shadows and glassmorphism, and docs/DESIGN.md:152 rules out drop-shadow by default. This change also edits DESIGN.md (lines 95 and 97) to describe the header card but says nothing about the sticky bar or the scale popover, so the doc and the shipped UI now disagree.
findings.fix: Give the bar an opaque `var(--color-surface-elevated)` background with the existing bottom border, and drop `backdrop-filter` and `box-shadow`. Alternatively, write the bar into DESIGN.md as an explicit exception.

findings.title: Summary-bar hidden assertions pass even when the bar is visibly on screen
findings.body: getByRole skips elements inside aria-hidden="true", and toBeHidden also passes when no element is found. The component sets aria-hidden separately from the CSS, so both hidden checks (lines 298 and 328) pass even if a transform or visibility bug keeps the bar on screen the whole time. The test therefore cannot catch a break in the rule that the bar appears only after the settings card scrolls out of view.
findings.fix: Check that the bar is hidden with a CSS locator that finds it regardless of aria-hidden. For the button, use getByRole with includeHidden: true.

findings.title: Summary-bar PDF button lacks busy/failure/blocked feedback, which renders only in the off-screen card
findings.body:
Observed: the bar's PDF button (lines 946–953) always has the label and aria-label 'Скачать PDF'. All feedback for that action renders only in `.minis-header-pdf` inside the header card (lines 852–866, 872): the busy label 'Подготовка PDF…', the 'Создаём PDF…' and 'Обрабатываем изображения…' status lines, `message` (e.g. the failure text set by `reportPdfFailure`) and `draftError`. The bar is only visible while that card is out of the viewport.

What follows: a user scrolls down to the rows and clicks 'Скачать PDF' in the bar. While the PDF is generated, the button just turns disabled with no label change. If generation fails, the error goes into the hidden card and the button re-enables with nothing visible. If a row draft is invalid or images are still processing, the bar button is disabled and the reason is shown only in the card. The `role="status"` regions still announce to screen readers, but sighted users get no explanation. So the bar's action starts the same operation as the card's button, but it does not behave the same from the user's side, which the goal asks for.
findings.fix: Mirror the busy label in the bar (`{busy ? 'Подготовка PDF…' : 'Скачать PDF'}` plus the matching aria-label). When `message`, `draftError` or `preparing` is set, show a short status in the bar, or make the bar's 'Изменить' path surface it.

findings.title: Fixed top summary bar has no matching scroll-padding, so it can cover focused controls
findings.body:
Observed: `.minis-summary-bar` is `position: fixed; inset-block-start: 0; z-index: 40`. It is about 3.5rem tall, and taller when it wraps under 40rem. It is visible whenever the header card is scrolled away, which is exactly when the user is working in the rows below. Nothing in the stylesheets sets `scroll-padding-block-start` (the only scroll offset is `scroll-margin-block-start` on the header card itself).

What follows: when a keyboard user Shift+Tabs upward through row controls (height select, copy count, duplicate/delete), the browser scrolls each newly focused control just into view at the top edge of the viewport, under the opaque bar. The focus ring is hidden behind the bar (WCAG 2.4.11, focus not obscured). The project profile counts keyboard reachability and visibility of state as reportable. This is new with the change: the old layout used a sticky sidebar and had no full-width fixed overlay.
findings.fix: While the bar can be visible, add `scroll-padding-block-start` to the scrolling root that equals the bar's height, e.g. `html:has(.minis-summary-bar[data-visible='true']) { scroll-padding-block-start: 4rem; }`. Scoping it to visibility avoids changing other pages.

findings.title: IntersectionObserver callback reads the first (oldest) entry instead of the latest
findings.body:
Observed: `new IntersectionObserver(([entry]) => setHeaderOutOfView(!entry.isIntersecting))` destructures only `entries[0]`. IntersectionObserver queues one entry per rendering update in which the target crosses a threshold, and delivers them later in a task. If the main thread is busy across several frames (this tool decodes and processes images and builds PDFs on the client), several entries for the same header can arrive in one callback, oldest first.

Inferred consequence: if the user scrolls past the header and back during such a stall, the callback applies the stale first entry. The bar then stays shown while the card is in view, or stays hidden while the card is out of view, until the next threshold crossing. That breaks 'the summary bar appears only while the card is out of view'. The trigger needs a main-thread stall that overlaps a scroll in both directions, so it is uncommon.
findings.fix: Use the last entry: `(entries) => setHeaderOutOfView(!entries[entries.length - 1].isIntersecting)`.

findings.title: Тест ищет миниатюру до закрытия модального popover
findings.body: После ввода 97 появляется кнопка «Сбросить измерение». Tab переводит фокус на неё и оставляет popover открытым. Popover использует стандартный модальный режим [React Aria](https://react-aria.adobe.com/Popover#popover), который скрывает внешние элементы от accessibility tree. Поэтому finalMini, заданный через getByRole('article'), не находится: scrollIntoViewIfNeeded() завершается по таймауту до проверки панели. Этот новый сценарий блокирует обязательный browser-check даже при исправном интерфейсе. Вывод получен чтением кода; тест не запускался.
findings.fix: После Tab явно закрыть popover через Escape и дождаться его закрытия, затем прокручивать страницу к finalMini.

findings.title: baseStyleSummary is a second copy of the baseStyleOptions labels, lowercased by hand
findings.body: `baseStyleSummary` (lines 71-75) holds the same three labels as `baseStyleOptions` (lines 64-68), just lowercased. If someone renames a label and updates only one table, the header Select and the sticky summary bar will show different names for the same setting. `Record<BaseStyle, string>` checks that every key is present, not that the text matches.
findings.fix: Drop `baseStyleSummary` and derive the text: `baseStyleOptions.find(({ value }) => value === settings.baseStyle)?.label.toLocaleLowerCase('ru-RU')`.

findings.title: Popover className repeats the primitive's defaults and adds a dead class
findings.body: The new `Popover` primitive (src/components/ui/popover.tsx:37) already sets `rounded-lg`, `shadow-md` and `bg-popover`. In global.css, `--color-popover` is defined as `var(--color-surface-elevated)`. The one caller passes `rounded-lg`, `shadow-md` and `bg-surface-elevated` again, which resolve to the same values. It also adds `minis-scale-popover`, a class that no CSS file mentions: `rg minis-scale-popover` only finds this line. And it adds `border border-border` on top of the primitive's `ring-1 ring-foreground/10`, so the popover gets two outlines. The effect is that the primitive's defaults are overridden to the same values, plus an unused class.
findings.fix: Shorten the caller className to the parts that differ from the primitive: the width and `p-4`. If the border is the intended outline, keep `border border-border` and drop the ring (dropdown-menu uses `ring-1 ring-border`). Remove `minis-scale-popover`.

findings.title: The 'closes on Escape and an outside click' test repeats the dismissal checks in the two tests before it
findings.body:
Here is the edit that turns this test red: make the popover non-dismissable, for example `isNonModal`, or stop Escape from closing it. The same edit already fails the two tests just before it:
- The focus-return test (line 179) asserts `open: false` after Escape.
- The `test.each` (lines 104-177) closes the popover by Escape and by outside pointerdown, then clicks the trigger and calls `getByRole('spinbutton')`. If the popover had not closed, that click would toggle it shut and `getByRole` would throw.

So this test catches no defect the others miss. It adds a third place to keep in sync, and nothing says which test owns the dismissal contract.
findings.fix: Either delete this test, or keep it as the single owner of dismissal and make the `test.each` and focus tests assert only the draft commit and focus return.

findings.title: Summary-bar download test would accept the printer test sheet instead of the minis PDF
findings.body: The new sticky-bar test checks the downloaded file only for the `%PDF-` signature. If the bar button's handler were swapped for `downloadPrinterScaleTestSheet()`, the test would still pass: a download happens, the signature matches and the other checks still hold. The user, however, would get the calibration ruler instead of their minis.
findings.fix: Assert `download.suggestedFilename()` against `^paper-minis-\d{8}-\d{4}\.pdf$`, as the existing `uploads a front and back and downloads a PDF` test does.

findings.title: Повтор запроса не ограничен ошибками MembraneError
findings.body: Новая схема проверяет только data.key. Если client.run выбросит обычный Error с data: { key: 'rate_limit_exceeded' }, connectionGraphql повторит запрос вместо немедленной передачи ошибки вызывающему коду. При успешном повторе исходная ошибка будет скрыта; при постоянном отказе появятся два лишних вызова и две задержки. Это нарушает явное условие цели: повторять только MembraneError, остальные ошибки передавать без изменений.
findings.fix: Добавить в RateLimitRefusal проверку isMembraneError: Schema.Literal(true), соответствующую признаку в тестовом объекте ошибки.

findings.title: Тест не проверяет ограничение повторов только ошибками MembraneError
findings.body: Новый отрицательный сценарий проверяет только другой data.key. Он не обнаруживает нарушение условия из goal.md: повторять только MembraneError. Если client.run выбросит обычный Error с data.key === 'rate_limit_exceeded', схема в linear-graphql.ts:253 примет его без проверки isMembraneError. Обёртка подождёт и повторит запрос вместо немедленного возврата исходной ошибки. Если следующая попытка успешна, исходная ошибка будет скрыта. Это нарушение введено данным изменением.
findings.fix: Добавить сценарий с обычным Error, у которого data.key равен 'rate_limit_exceeded', но отсутствует isMembraneError. Проверить возврат того же объекта ошибки, один вызов и отсутствие ожиданий; дополнить проверку типа ошибки в реализации.

findings.title: ENVIRONMENT.md says the local rollback image survives the prune, but the prune deletes it
findings.body:
The new line says that after `docker image prune -f` only dangling images are removed, and that the local copy for rollback stays ("локальная копия для отката остаются"). In `rebuild.sh`, `do_rebuild` runs `pull`, then `down`, then `up -d`. The pull moves the tag to the new image, so the previous image becomes untagged, which is what dangling means. Once `up -d` replaces the container, nothing references the old image any more, and the prune at `scripts/docker/rebuild.sh:33` deletes it. So the previous image of every rebuilt service is exactly what gets removed.

This includes the failure path the goal requires the prune to run after. If `down` succeeds and `up -d` fails, the old container is gone, the old image is dangling and unused, and the prune removes it. The operator then has no local image to roll back to, while the doc tells them they do. The script behaviour is intended; the defect is in the doc.
findings.fix: Drop the claim about a retained rollback copy. Say instead that the previous image of each rebuilt service is removed, and that rolling back needs a re-pull by tag or digest.

findings.title: Документация ошибочно обещает сохранить образ для отката
findings.body: При обновлении glances с новым nicolargo/glances:latest-full команда pull переносит тег на новый образ, а down удаляет старый контейнер. Прежний образ без других тегов и контейнеров становится dangling, поэтому добавленный prune удаляет его. Новое утверждение, что локальная копия для отката остаётся, неверно и вводит оператора в заблуждение при подготовке отката. Это следует из [правил Docker image prune](https://docs.docker.com/engine/manage-resources/pruning/).
findings.fix: Убрать обещание сохранить локальную копию для отката и указать, что прежние образы без тегов и контейнеров удаляются.

findings.title: ENVIRONMENT.md says a local rollback copy survives the prune, but the prune deletes it
findings.body: The new line says that after `docker image prune -f` the images of stopped services "и локальная копия для отката остаются" (and the local rollback copy stays). That is not true for the flow in `do_rebuild` (`scripts/docker/_lib.sh:272-274`). `pull` moves the tag to the new image, so the previous image becomes untagged. `down` and `up -d` then replace the container, so no container uses the old image. That untagged, unused image is exactly what `docker image prune -f` deletes. The previous image only survives when no new image was pulled, or when the old container is still running because `down` failed. After a rebuild there is no offline copy to roll back to. An operator reading this note will think they can return to the previous image without the registry, and they cannot. This is prose only, so it is minor.
findings.fix: Drop the rollback clause, or say plainly that the previous image of every rebuilt service is removed and a rollback needs a fresh pull.

findings.title: Dashboard comment still says three groups after a fourth («Место») was added
findings.body: The comment directly above the cards still reads `# Три группы вместо одной плитки glance: ...`. This change adds a «Место» separator and grid in front of «Диски», «Материнка» and «Вентиляторы», so the Сервер view now has four groups. The comment gives the wrong count for the layout it describes.
findings.fix: Change "Три группы" to "Четыре группы", or drop the count.

findings.title: Disk-space push shows the free-space value with no unit
findings.body: The SSD and RAID messages (lines 64 and 78) end with `свободно {{ states('sensor..._disk_free') }}.`. `states()` returns only the bare number, without the sensor's unit (Glances reports disk free in GiB). The push therefore reads something like "свободно 12.3.". The other alerts in this file always add the unit by hand, for example `°C` at lines 89 and 104, and these messages do the same for usage with `%`. The free-space value is the only one left without a unit.
findings.fix: Add the unit after the template, e.g. `свободно {{ states('sensor.127_0_0_1_rootfs_disk_free') }} ГБ.`, and do the same for the RAID message.

findings.title: configure_network still sources config.sh, which bootstrap now sources at the top level
findings.body: The change adds `source "$PROJECT_DIR/scripts/lib/config.sh"` at the top level (line 66) so `configure_journald` can read `JOURNALD_SYSTEM_MAX_USE`. That load already supplies the `NET_*` values that configure_network reads, so the second `source` at line 197 now does nothing. Nothing between the two loads changes those variables. The extra line makes it look as if config is loaded only inside that function, or as if it overrides something, and neither is true. The line predates this change, but this change made it dead.
findings.fix: Delete the `source` line inside `configure_network` (scripts/bootstrap.sh:197).

findings.title: Документация ошибочно обещает сохранить образ для отката
findings.body: Новое утверждение неверно при обновлении сервиса с тегом latest, например AdGuard. В scripts/docker/_lib.sh:272–274 выполняются pull, down и up: тег переходит новому образу, а старый контейнер удаляется. Если других ссылок нет, прежний образ становится dangling и удаляется очисткой в scripts/docker/rebuild.sh:33. Поэтому оператор не может рассчитывать на обещанную локальную копию для отката. Такое поведение подтверждает [документация Docker](https://docs.docker.com/engine/manage-resources/pruning/#prune-images).
findings.fix: Убрать обещание сохранения копии для отката и указать, что прежние образы без тегов и контейнеров удаляются.

findings.title: ENVIRONMENT.md says the local rollback copy of an image survives the prune, but for moving tags it is the copy that gets pruned
findings.body: The new text says: "Удаляются только dangling images; образы остановленных сервисов и локальная копия для отката остаются." Almost every service uses a moving tag (17× `latest`, plus `stable`, `beta`, `alpine`, `latest-full`). On rebuild, `docker compose pull` moves the tag to the new image, so the previous image loses its tag and becomes dangling. `down` + `up -d` then removes the last container that referenced it. The `docker image prune -f` at `scripts/docker/rebuild.sh:33` deletes exactly that image. After a rebuild that pulled an update, no local copy of the old version is left to roll back to. An operator who trusts this line during a bad update will find the old image gone and has to pull it again by digest.
findings.fix: Rewrite the sentence to say the previous version of a moving-tag image (`latest` etc.) becomes dangling after pull and is deleted. Only images that still carry a tag survive, such as those of stopped services or old pinned versions.

findings.title: Stale comment: the server view now has four groups, but the comment still says three
findings.body: The comment directly above the cards reads `# Три группы вместо одной плитки glance: ...`. This change adds a fourth separator group, «Место» (line 503), in front of «Диски», «Материнка» and «Вентиляторы». The comment now gives the wrong count for the layout it describes. The comment should change, not the code.
findings.fix: Change to «Четыре группы …» (or drop the count), and optionally note that «Место» shows the rootfs usage sensors.

findings.title: rebuild.sh header still says only "pull + restart" after the change adds an image prune
